questions.topicDefinition:
SAP Bank Communication Management is used to manage interfaces for communication with banks and gives you the ability to connect with your bank, track the entire lifecycle of a transaction, and improve straight-through processing and compliance with internal policies. Bank Communication Management is also responsible for batch creation and approval, the payment status monitor, and the bank statement monitor.

When working with Bank Communication Management, payments in one or more payment runs can be mapped and processed in a payment status monitor. This monitor also serves as a repository for incoming status messages from SWIFT and individual banks. The payments in the payment run can be grouped into one or more batches according to your requirements. For example, payments can be grouped by low or high payment amount. You also have the option to use digital signatures to approve, reject or resubmit payments
questions.question:
Are you intending to use SAP Bank Communication Management functionalities, like:

- managing multiple bank communication interfaces
- enabling connections to your banks
- track the lifecycle of payments for transactions
- creation and approval of payment batches
- track the status of bank statements ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This step allows you to enable two-factor authentication for the Approve Bank Payments app.
In this activity, you have the option to enable two-factor authentication for the Approve Bank Payments app. If you enable two-factor authentication, the business user submitting payment batches for processing by the bank will be asked to authenticate their identity using SAP Cloud Platform Identity Authentication (IAS).
questions.question: Is a two-factor authentication for the approval of bank payments required ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites:  Default Currency].  WIthin this step, you define the default currency and the resubmission date for payments.
When a payment batch is evaluated for release (such as dual control, triple control, automatic release and so on), the total batch amount can be evaluated based on the default currency if the payments in the batch consist of different currencies or different company code (hence different local currency).
For resubmission of payments, the resubmission date from the current date can be set.
Example
Default Currency = EUR
Default resubmission days = 5
--> The default resubmission date = the current date + 5
questions.question: Which default currency and resubmission days shall be taken into consideration for payment batch release evaluation ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define rules that determine which reason should be automatically specified for reversing a rejected payment document and which payment block option should be automatically specified for blocking the reopened items.
In the My Inbox - Process Rejected Payments app, you can reverse payment documents rejected in the approval process or by the bank. For each rejected payment document, a reason for the reversal is automatically specified. The cleared items in the payment document will be reopened. If the automatically specified payment block option confirms a block, the reopened items will be blocked and cannot be paid in other payment runs.
You define a set of rules to determine which reason should be automatically specified for reversing a rejected payment document and which payment block option should be automatically specified for blocking the reopened items. The rules are for different combinations of paying company code, payment method, house bank, and account ID. You also define the sequence for applying these rules. The sequence number and the reversal reason are mandatory fields.
questions.question: For reversing rejected payment documents, which reversal reasons (e.g. wrong posting) shall be automatically specified and which payment block option (e.g. blocked for payment) shall be specified for blocking the reopened items ? If necessary, please additionally refer to information of the paying company code, payment method, house bank, house bank ID.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have made settings in Map External Status to Internal Status according your needs]. This activity allows you to enable the rejection of payments that were previously accepted by the bank. Enable the functionality for accepting late rejects from your bank.
By default, the transition from the final status 'Accepted by Bank (BAC)' to the status 'Rejected by Bank (BRE)' is not allowed. In exceptional cases some banks send a technical acceptance first, which is not followed by the final 'Accepted by Bank' incoming message. Therefore, this technical acceptance can be considered as status 'Accepted by Bank', until it is later followed by status 'Rejected by Bank' for some payment items.
questions.question: Is it required to enable a late rejection of payments that were previously accepted by the bank for specific company codes or house banks ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This step allows you to assign external status codes to internal status codes.
You can interpret the status codes from the external world. Every incoming status message has a code which can be mapped to an internal status code based on a company code and house bank.
You can also activate Incomplete Processing for incoming payment files. You can use this option when your bank does not provide the complete information about changed statuses of each payment item included in a payment batch
questions.question: Is is required to assign external statuses of your banks for payment items to internal status codes ? If yes, please specify which external status code shall be mapped to which payment business transaction (e.g. Accepted by bank). Is this only relevant for specific company codes or house banks ? Is an activation of processing incomplete incoming payment files required ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This activity allows you to assign descriptions for internal reason codes to external reason codes from external entities, such as banks.
You interpret the reason codes you receive from external entities, such as banks. These mappings will be displayed in the batch and payment monitor (BNK_MONI) transaction with external reason code and internal description to interpret the codes for your system.
questions.question: Is there a list, which documents the mapping of internal to external reason codes from banks ?

questions.topicDefinition: This configuration allows you to create internal reason codes with descriptions. You create internal reason codes and descriptions, which you can later use as values to map them to external reason codes you receive from external entities, such as banks.
questions.question: Are you intending to map external reason codes from banks to internal reason codes for more detailed tracking of payment items ? If yes, please specify the internal reason codes, which will be required.

questions.topicDefinition:
SAP Advanced payment management allows you to centralize all payment activities of a corporate group.

Advanced payment management supports four payment scenarios: Internal payments, payments ‘in name of’ with forwarding only, payments ‘in name of’ with routing optimization, and payments 'on behalf of'.

It integrates with other areas within S/4HANA such as In-House Cash, Cash Management, Bank Communication Management, Bank Account Management and General Ledger.
questions.question:
Are you intending to use SAP Advanced Payment Management functionalities, like:

- Centralize payment operations for efficiency and control
- Deliver end-to-end visibility of the payment lifecycle
- Track the lifecycle of payments for transactions
- Build a foundation for frictionless, instants, secure and cost-effective payments
- Inbound/outbound management of transactions and related data in different formats and sources (PINO, POBO, etc.)
- Payment data enrichment and validation
- Rule-based payment messages routing ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this activity, you define and maintain the rules for EBICS order type for outgoing MBC messages.
During output processing, the system checks this configuration and populates the EBICS order type to the outgoing MBC message. The configuration is checked using the data from the output order or, in case of grouping scenarios, with a random order. Therefore, define grouping conditions and EBICS order type determination rules accordingly.
questions.question: Which EBICS order types in advanced payment management exist per clearing area, company code, house bank, and payment order type ? If necessary, please additionally refer to service level code and local instruments.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have made the required settings in Customizing for advanced payment management as follows:
Define Clearing Areas
Define Message Types
Define Formats, Define Media, and Define Channels
Define Payment Order Types]. In this activity you make settings for the determination of the internal payment order type. The system uses this control information for certain validation and processing throughout advanced payment management. You define this information in the payment order. The combination of message type and original message type allows the system to distinguish uniquely between credit transfers and direct debit and between bank-to-bank R-messages (reject/return).
If the system cannot determine the payment order type, it assigns an error and sends the payment order to Postprocessing.
questions.question: To determine internal payment order types it is necessary to assign certain validation steps for processing throughout advanced payment management. Please define for the specific clearing area, which XML message identifier, for which channel, format, and medium shall receive which payment order type ? If needed, please refer to the payment method, local instrument, collection type, and type derivation indicator.

questions.topicDefinition: In this activity, you maintain the settings for inbound messages received through the connector for SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity.
questions.question: Are you using SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity ? If yes, please provide the information how the inbound messages, which you are receiving through the connector, needs to be setup. Please refer to the sender/receiver ID if necessary, message type, origin, and the converter ID which is relevant.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: The outgoing converter uses DMEE. The respective flag might be set in the converter attributes]. Assign a message type for Multi-Bank-Connectivity messages generated using the outgoing DMEE converter. An outgoing DMEE converter might not be distinguished with a unique Format/Medium/Channel combination per outgoing DMEE format tree. To differentiate the different formats generated using the DMEE this customizing can be used to assign an alternative Message Type.
Standard Settings:
If no value is maintained the standard value assigned to the converter is used.
Example:
The output of DMEE Tree type PAYM with format tree CGI_CT will be passed to Multi-Bank-Connectivity as message typePAIN.001.05. MBC provides a respective BADI implementation for this message type.
questions.question: Is the outgoing converter using DMEE ? If yes, is there a need to distinguish with a uniquie Format/Medium/Channel combination, besides SAP Standard ? If yes, please specify the clearing area, format tree, and message type, which will be required.

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: The rule IDs must have been maintained in the settings for Bank Communication Management under Rule Maintenance]. In this activity, you maintain the rule IDs that are used in SAP Bank Communication Management workflow settings for payments that are passed from advanced payment management.
questions.question: Are you intending to use SAP Bank Communication Management ? If yes, which rule IDs need to be applied for workflow settings for payments from advanced payment management ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this activity, you maintain the outbound settings for sending messages via the connector for SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity.
questions.question: Are you using SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity ? If yes, please provide the information how the outbound messages, which you are sending through the connector, needs to be setup. Please refer to the sender/receiver ID if necessary, message type, origin, and the converter ID which is relevant.

questions.topicDefinition:
In this activity you maintain the format in which data is passed into and out of advanced payment management.
The format describes  the structure of the fields and records of the payment objects that are used in advanced payment management.
Format is used along with medium and channel in order to define a format converter. Here, you define the formats that are used when defining format converters.
Example: Datenträgeraustausch (DTAUS) is a format for the exchange of data internally within Germany.
questions.question: Which formats do you expect to be passed into and out of advanced payment management (e.g. PAIN001, MT101, IDoc, etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this activity you maintain the channel used to deliver data to advanced payment management. You use channels as one of the elements for defining a converter.
An example of a channel that can be defined here is SWIFT.
questions.question: From which channels are you expecting data to be transferred to the advanced payment mananagement module (e.g. SWIFT, TRM etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
You can define the rules for mapping or transforming data to enable data exchange with your financial institution in the required data format. You can create new format mappings or copy from existing ones, display the details of your existing format mapping, as well as import, export, edit, check, delete, and release these mappings.
By setting up format mappings, you can determine how the system interprets data received from your financial institution and how to map that to the incoming payment structures stored in the system.
questions.question: For data enablement exchange with your financial institutions, specific data format mappings can be required. Which data formats are required and how shall the mapping look like ? Is it necessary to implement/maintain specific mappings besides the SAP Standard mappings ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[The following prerequisites are required to determine the receiver ID: You have defined an outgoing converter. You have defined an outbound message type and have assigned it to an outbound message]. In this activity, you can determine the receiver IDs used by the SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity outbound connector. This information can be used in conjunction with the message type at SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity to determine the correct receiving system.
Example:
The head office company code 1010 is sending a pain.002 message (/Pain.002.001.09) to its subsidiary 1710 for failed order processing. The receiver ID used at SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity is set to CC<company code>. The configured message type is Pain.002

The corresponding configuration is:
Message type: Pain.002
Company code: 1710
Receiver ID: CC1710
questions.question: Which message types are relevant for the SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity outbound connector ? Which of these message types (e.g. CAMT.054) shall be mapped to which receiver ID and company code if necessary ?

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: You have already defined the following: Format, Channel, Medium]. Define an inbound or outbound interface to surrounding systems. A converter is represented by the combination of 4 attributes. Format, medium, channel and direction are linked with a conversion program, which is responsible for interpreting the data and translating it into the required target data structure or file format.
questions.question: The predefined format, channel and medium need to assigned for conversion. How and in which combination shall these predefined settings be maintained and converted ? Please additionally refer to the direction (e.g. incoming/outgoing), the support of file forwarding, and the origin.

questions.topicDefinition:
In this Customizing activity, you can classify bank response codes per financial institute. For each institute, different status codes can be expected. You can set the classification for the values you receive from your bank.
You can classify each entry into one of the following categories:
Completed: This will finalize pending files, orders, transactions and then trigger subsequent actions. This can include the further processing of pending Clearing item (CLR) to post to the GL.
Rejected: This will trigger the exception handling framework to deal with the error scenario. You can either specify the exception handling reaction based on the provided error reason code (see also Assign Exception Handling Reaction to Bank Reject /PF1/V_STAT_REAC) or use error code based Define Default Reaction Types*configuration or master data set-up via transaction code /PF1/EH.
Standard Settings
If bank specific values are not configured, the system will use those entries without the specified bank. If no configuration is provided for status code, defaults settings will be applied.
ACSC, ACCC status codes imply completed.
RJCT, CANC status codes are handled as rejected.
All other codes will be handled as intermediary information, which will be followed by a status of either category Completed or Rejected.
questions.question: For bank responses codes from different financial institutes, is it required to classify them individually ? If yes, what values do you receive from your banks ? Which categories shall be assigned to the values ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have defined exception handling reactions]. In this Customizing activity, you can assign exception handling reactions to the relevant bank reject messages. The provided reason code can be used to identify the proper handling of the rejected file, order or transaction.
Standard Settings:
The system will use the most specific (bank specific) entry. If no matching entry for the bank is available, the generic entry without bank identifier will be applied.
If no specific reaction type is defined, the ' Define Default Reaction Types' or Master data configuration will be used for the standard error code 'Bank Reject(002010)'.
questions.question: Is it required to have specific exception handling reactions for reject messages for banks ? If yes, which exception handling reactions shall be assigned to the relevant bank reject messages in order to handle the rejected file ?

questions.topicDefinition: Connect banks and other financial institutions with corporate customers on a secure network owned and managed by SAP. The SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity solution offers multiple services over one single channel, while supporting the deployment of new ones.
questions.question:
Are you intending to use SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity functionalities, like:

- Facilitate host-2-host connectivity to financial institutions
- Reach a large number of banks by using a standard exchange protocol based on EBICS
- Automate steps associated with the execution and reconciliation of payments, order-to-cash applications, and order entry documents
- Enable direct integration with payment approval processes
- Remove file- and middleware-based integration with a service-based offering unified with ERP  ?

questions.topicDefinition:
You use this configuration to assign Parameter Sets for Bank Statement processing.

If you have defined a parameter set for a combination of sender ID and message type, the system will use this parameter set when planning a job for bank statement processing. If a variant has also been defined for the same combination, then the parameter set assignment will be used.
questions.question: For the processing of bank statements via MBC, what kind of formats do you plan to process (e.g. MT940, XML, etc.) ? Are there bank specific formats ? Is it intended to process intraday statements ? What kind of message types are being used (e.g. CAMT, PAIN, MT) ?

questions.topicDefinition: Within this step you can maintain the relevant EBICS users.
questions.question: Which bank connection shall be used (e.g. EBICS, Host-2-Host, SWIFT e.g.) ? If EBICS is being used, shall static bank user be used (same bank user for same payments to the bank or dynamic mapping for all approval users to bank users) ?

questions.topicDefinition: This configuration step allows you to map the approval users to the relevant EBICS users.
questions.question: Which approval users shall be mapped to which EBICS users ?

questions.topicDefinition: Via this step you have the possibility to maintain the compression (and decompression) settings for specific message types.
questions.question: Which message types shall be compressed and decompressed ? Please additionally specify the relevant (de)compression category (e.g. ZIP, GZIP).

questions.topicDefinition:
You use this configuration to maintain approval user settings. You can set up different sequences, like:
1 First Approval User
2 Second Approval User
-1 Last but one Approval User
-2 Last but two Approval User
LAST Last Approval User
questions.question: Which approvers from the approval process shall be mapped to the bank users ?  Note: Only two approvers can be mapped to bank users.

questions.topicDefinition: Within this step you can determine the EBICS order type from specific company codes, house banks, and house bank IDs etc.
questions.question: Which EBICS order types are required ? Are there specific determination rules which shall apply for the determination of order types (optional) ? If so, please additionally specify the order type(s).

questions.topicDefinition: Via this step you can maintain sensitive data classifications. This includes the information of specified message types (e.g. like PAIN.001) and Origin (e.g. Payment Factory or Treasury).
questions.question: Which message types shall be marked as sensitive data ?

questions.topicDefinition:
You can use this Customizing activity to maintain application-specific inbound processing steps.
A processing step is always defined as an assignment of an application that should be triggered for processing of the payload received by the SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (MBC) Message. The assignment is made for Message Types that are received in the header information of an MBC Message.
You can define several steps for each application. Please make sure to define different step numbers when assigning several applications to one Message Type.
You can use the Active flag to activate/deactivate the configuration entries. Only steps marked as active will be triggered during the runtime.
Please note that this configuration is optional and overrules the default settings defined in the MBC Connector. By creating an entry in this configuration, the default steps assigned within the MBC Connector will no longer be executed. Therefore, if you need to define steps that should be triggered, then do make sure to additionally define the entries for the default steps as well.
questions.question: How shall incoming files be processed ? Is it necessary to overrule the default settings defined in the MBC connector with regards to the maintenance of application-specific inbound processing steps ? If yes, which message types shall be maintained with regards to the relevant application ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this Customizing activity you can define a custom Sender ID for a Message Type and/or Receiver ID. For example, you could define different Sender IDs for communicating with different banks.
These custom Sender IDs are used by the connector for the SAP Financial Services Network whenever a message is created. For payment messages created via Payment Medium Workbench, the system uses the Customer Number maintained at House Bank level as the Sender ID (the corresponding custom Sender ID entries are ignored). However, the system uses the custom Sender ID maintained in this Customizing activity as a fallback, and it is used in the event that the Customer Number has not been maintained at House Bank level.
You can leave the Message Type and/or Receiver ID blank. The system treats such entries as relevant for all Message Types and/or Receiver IDs. In the event of multiple valid entries, the system uses the most specific one.
When you are planning to manually create FSN Messages by uploading files to the connector from your local computer (the Pick-Up Files report), you might consider maintaining the exact Sender IDs and Receiver IDs, because the value helps from the Pick-Up Files report also use these Customizing settings.
questions.question:
Is there a need to specify specific sender and target receiver IDs besides the custom IDs generated out of the system ? Is there a list available, which specifies the sender and target receiver IDs for communication with your banks ? Do you have a use case of manual uploading of messages ? 

Note: Manual uploading of messages is not recommended.

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: You have saved the variant in transaction FF.5]. In this customizing activity you maintain the Variant for a SenderID/ReceiverID and Message Type in the view BSNAGT/V_VARI.  The system processes incoming messages according to the message type, which is specified in the Web service interface. For MT940 (bank statement), MX camt.053 and MT942 (account report), or MX camt.052, the report RFEBKA00 (transaction FF.5) is executed with the relevant variant, as configured in this Customizing activity.
questions.question: Which variants shall be applied for which message types ?

questions.topicDefinition: Via this activity you can maintain routing settings for specific Sender/Receiver IDs and the relevant message types if needed.
questions.question: Is there a need for specific routings, besides the MBC default routing ? If yes, please specifiy for which Sender/Receiver and message type shall these specific routing settings be applied (e.g. HTTP API, RFC API, Web Service, etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition: You use this activity to maintain SWIFT - relevant parameters. The Multi-Bank Connectivity message gets selected based on the Receiver ID and Message Type configured in this activity. The system then extends the message header with these parameters.
questions.question: In case SWIFT connectivity is in scope. Is it required to extend the message header of specific message types (e.g. MT300 etc.) ? If yes, please specifiy the SWIFT parameters and refer for which message types and Receiver ID this shall be maintained.

questions.topicDefinition: In this configuration activity, the parameters are defined on which the sub procedure determination depends on.
questions.question: For the subprocedure determination for electronic bank statement processing, is it required to define parameters besides the SAP Standard content ? If so, please specify and refer to data type, data category, and data source routine.

questions.topicDefinition:
Here, you can define the payment clearing groups with which you can group your business partners.
A payment clearing group is an attribute with which you can categorize your suppliers and customers into groups. In the Manage Bank Statement Reprocessing Rules app, you can use the attribute as a condition of the reprocessing rule. That means, with the Payment Clearing Group attribute, you have another option to actively influence the processing of your bank statement items. The advantage of this attribute is that you can refer to certain business partners in one condition by using the correct payment clearing group.
Standard Settings:
Select New Entry to create new payment clearing groups. You have to define a unique identifier for each payment clearing group and give them a descriptive name that helps you recognize the payment clearing group when you use them in the following tasks:
in your business partners' master data (in the BP transaction) when you assign the payment clearing groups to your business partners to group them
in the Manage Bank Statement Reprocessing Rules app when you select the payment clearing groups in the reprocessing rules' conditions.
questions.question: Is it required to group your suppliers and customers for bank statement processing ? How many groups shall be created ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step you can display the average cost of reprocessing incoming payments.
The average cost of reprocessing an incoming payment is required by the 'Reprocessing Rate of Incoming Payments' app.
Standard Settings:
In the standard system, the table does not contain any entries.
questions.question: Is there a need to monitor the average cost of reprocessing incoming payments ? If yes, please specify for which company code and with which average cost (incl. currency) this shall be monitored.

questions.topicDefinition:
You can sort the type code list for the payment transactions of your electronic bank statements by assigning codes to posting rules or algorithms or by creating new codes.
In this Customizing activity, you can make basic settings for the account statement. You can create transaction types by entering names and descriptions for the transactions you require. In this activity you assign (external) business transaction codes to an (internal) posting rule. As a result, you can use the same posting specifications for different business transaction codes. You can also assign account symbols to the accounts.
A posting rule specifies how an account statement item is posted. For more information about posting rules, navigate to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Product Assistance in the SAP Help Portal (https://help.sap.com/) and search under Finance for Posting Rules.
questions.question: Which BTC are being used in your bank statements which you receive from your banks ? Is there a list available which indicates certain type codes of your bank statements to specific postings ? Are there any posting rules which can be applied for the processing of bank statements ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Here, you can define basic settings for importing and posting bank statements by creating parameter sets.
Parameter set defines how your imported bank statements should be posted. You can use your parameter set in the Manage Incoming Payment Files app to define how your imported bank statements should be processed.
questions.question: How shall the posting of bank statements be processed (e.g. Only import, import and post, etc.) ? Are there any specific requirements with regards to the posting ?

questions.topicDefinition: Via this step you can configure specific format data and mapping for incoming files from banks. The system imports bank statements in certain formats, e.g. MT940. You can tell the system to map the values of certain records of the incoming format to output fields that are given in the target structure. To do that, you need to create format mappings.
questions.question: Is it required to map specific values of the incoming files from banks to the system (e.g. MT940) besides the SAP Standard mapping ?

questions.topic: Basic Settings for Cash and Liquidity Management
questions.topicDefinition: You can define the basic settings that are required for using Cash and Liquidity Management, including scope determination, change request grouping options, bank account control modes, snapshots, as well as the cash request functions.
questions.question:
Are you planning to use one of the following functionalities within the SAP Cash Management and Bank Account Management solution:

- Enable snapshots within cash positioning
- Enable cash trade requests within cash positioning (for this the Trading Platform Integration is required - please see L2 question in topic Trading Platform Integration)
- Enable workflow processes within BAM
- Enable bank account closing processes within BAM
- Enable revision processes within BAM

questions.topicDefinition: With this activity, you can define rules for manually releasing cash flows. You assign a logical system with the company code and planning level information. Cash flows with such information are filtered in the back-end system and can be selected subsequently in the Release Cash Flow app for further review and release.
questions.question:
Are there any specific Cash Flows which need to be released manually (e.g. Dividend, Tax payments) ? 
What kind of Cash Flows need to be released manually and which rules should be applied for this ? E.g. Analyze all Cash Flows from Company Code A with Planning Level B etc.

questions.topicDefinition: [As a prerequisite, please define your Stop Condition Profiles via the app Flow Builder: Stop Conditions] In this customizing activity, you can make additional configuration for Financial Accounting (FI) in One Exposure. You can define the association between the company code and the profile of stop conditions.
questions.question: Where do you want to stop the determination of the liquidity item for actual cash flows ? Are there different stop conditions per company codes ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this Customizing activity, you can define the default derivation logic for liquidity items for company codes that have Cash Management activated. Each entry assigns a query sequence and a derivation function to a company code, which the system uses to derive liquidity items for that company code. For example, liquidity items can be determined based on the accounts referenced by the line items in documents posted to ledgers (G/L, accounts receivable, or accounts payable).
Note: The derivation rules that you define here only work for new postings. To generate liquidity items against existing posting data, you must run the rebuild program.
questions.question: For each item of your liquidity hierarchy what information such as G/L account, planning level etc. defines which cash flows need to be assigned to a liquidity item ?

questions.topicDefinition: Via this IMG step it is possible to specify grouping structures. These structures enable you to group together bank and subledger accounts in the cash position or the liquidity forecast and cash concentration.
questions.question: Is there a need to group bank and subledger accounts for cash position or liquidity forecast ? If yes, how would this grouping look like ?

questions.topicDefinition: [This is a prerequisite for SAP ID 104081]. Define the groupings, and stipulate the main headings and the line headings that the system displays in the cash position or liquidity forecast.
questions.question: [This is a prerequisite for SAP ID 104081]. Is it intended to have specific groupings (e.g. specific Banks) within the cash position ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this IMG setting it is possible to define several runtime parameters for the Flow Builder. The Flow Builder is executed as a background job and with delta run mode*, the program will read runtime parameters for a given company code from this configuration. If not found, the program will read one default entry that company code equals space. If not found, the program will use the parameters of its selection screen (i.e., values of the variant when it is scheduled).
When the Flow Builder is executed on-line, or with mass run mode or test run, the program will not read from this configuration.
questions.question: Is it necessary to read specific runtime parameters for a given company code ?

questions.topicDefinition: This configuration is to extend account assignment fields for One Exposure (FQM_FLOW) and map them from Accounting Document Segment (BSEG). It only applies to the source of accounting documents. You have the possibility to extend account assignment fields for One Exposure and map them from Accounting Document Segment.
questions.question: Which fields from the account document are relevant to be taken over to the cash management process and therefore shall be displayable in the cash position ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this customizing activity, you can define generic settings for Flow Builder Plus. The Flow Builder Plus introduces new configuration which enables generating specific cash position cash flows and liquidity analysis cash flows.
questions.question: Do you plan to trace document line items from Financial Accounting or Materials Management in Cash Management ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this customizing activity, you can make additional configuration for Financial Accounting (FI) in One Exposure.
questions.question: Is it planned to do Cash Positioning only or is it also planned to use the Liquidity Analysis functionality ? Is there a need to track documents (e.g. posting on revenue/expense account) ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this Customizing activity, you can define query sequences based on existing queries. As a prerequisite you have defined the relevant queries in Define Queries for Liquidity Item Derivation.
questions.question: For each item of your liquidity hierarchy what information such as G/L account, planning level etc. defines which cash flows need to be assigned to a liquidity item ? (Think of a potential reuse of queries for multiple sequences)

questions.topicDefinition: You use this activity to define settings for memo records that are generated from imported bank statements, including intraday bank statements and end-of-day bank statements.
questions.question: Which imported end-of-day bank statements should be posted directly and for which should only memo records be created ? Is there a specific definition for the derivation of planning types for intraday memo records needed ?

questions.topicDefinition:
You use this activity to activate or deactivate source applications for One Exposure from Operations on a company code basis.
Once a source application is activated, the forecasted transactions from this source application are integrated into the One Exposure from Operations hub, and the forecasted cash flows are therefore available in Cash Management reporting.
You can initialize the One Exposure from Operations hub for existing source application data using the activity Load Transaction Data Source Application into One Exposure from Operations Hub.
The source application One Exposure is a prerequisite for all other source applications. Activating this source application means that the One Exposure from Operations hub accepts data at all. It is especially necessary to activate this source application if data from remote systems shall be transferred into the One Exposure from Operations hub.
The source application Financial Operations comprises accounting documents representing invoices and payments as well as bank statements. This source application is a prerequisite for all other source applications except for the source application One Exposure.
In this activity, you enter each combination of source application and company code individually. To activate or deactivate multiple company codes for several source applications simultaneously, use the activity Activate Multiple Source Applications.
questions.question: Is there a need to activate or deactivate specific source applications for One Exposure on a company code level ? Are there any data from remote systems which shall be transferred to the One Exposure ?

questions.topicDefinition: You use this activity to define authorization groups for cash pools that have the service provider Bank - Time Dependent. This is required before you start working with this type of cash pool in the Manage Cash Pools (Version 2) app. By assigning authorization groups to a cash pool, you restrict access to this cash pool to a certain group of users.
questions.question: Do you require specific authorization groups for cash pools ? If yes, how would such an authorization group look like and how many are needed ?

questions.topicDefinition: You use this activity to define a number range for cash pools that have the service provider Bank - Time Dependent. This is required before you start working with this type of cash pool in the Manage Cash Pools (Version 2) app.
questions.question: Is there a need to have different number ranges for different Cash Pools ? How many different number ranges shall be applied ?

questions.topicDefinition: You can define the date difference tolerance between the value date and the posting date to decide whether the value date of an accounting document line item needs to be reviewed and corrected. This configuration is to define the date difference tolerance between Value Date (BSEG-VALUT) and Posting Date (BKPF-BUDAT) to decide whether the Value Date of an accounting document line item needs to be reviewed and corrected.
questions.question: Which differences in days (between Value Date and Posting Date) would there be allowed before a review and correction is necessary ? Please refer to company code and house bank if needed.

questions.topicDefinition: This setting is relevant for executing cash trade requests. With this you can assign planning levels to cash trade requests with the status of Created, Submitted and Released. You can then see cash trade requests in different statuses by planning level. Planning levels are derived for cash trade requests.
questions.question: Are you intending to use the cash trade request functionality ? Is it necessary to track different statuses (like created, submitted, and released) with different planning levels ? Which planning levels shall be assigned to which status ?

questions.topicDefinition: For incoming bank transfers, you can define clearing accounts for posting to general ledger for payment transactions with bank accounts. The relevant accounts are specified by house bank account, payment method, and currency (if the currency is not specified, the account applies to all currencies).
questions.question: Are you planning to use bank account transfers within cash management ? Are you planning to use payment requests for bank transfers ?

questions.topicDefinition: For outgoing bank transfers, you can define clearing accounts for posting to general ledger for payment transactions with bank accounts. The relevant accounts are specified by house bank account, payment method, and currency (if the currency is not specified, the account applies to all currencies).
questions.question: Are you planning to use bank account transfers within cash management ? Are you planning to use payment requests for bank transfers ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this step you define separate Cash Management planning levels for payment requests. If the Cash Management update writes the flows to a bank account, you must define a separate planning level for payment requests. Otherwise, the payment requests are displayed at the same level as the bank statement postings when you call up the cash position.
This setting is optional if the Cash Management update writes the flows to a bank clearing account.
questions.question: Do you intend to use payment requests for payments ? If yes, is there a need to define a specific planning level for the status of these payment requests ? Which planning levels should be assigned with regards to the relevant payment method ?

questions.topicDefinition: This IMG setting is relevant for Materials Management (MM) and Sales and Distribtion (SD) modules. With this you can allocate the transactions from MM and SD to the planning levels you have defined for updating this data. This allocation is necessary since the system cannot determine the planning level by using master record fields, as it does to access data from Financial Accounting (FI)
questions.question: Do you intend to use MM and SD data in Cash Management ? Is it necessary to track the transactions from MM and SD via planning levels ?

questions.topicDefinition: If the Cash Management update writes the flows to a bank account, you must define a separate planning level for payment requests. Otherwise, the payment requests are displayed at the same level as the bank statement postings when you call up the cash position.
questions.question: For reporting your cash position, which data sources (e.g. Bank Accounting, Sales and Distribution) do you want to include and on which granularity level ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this step, you define the planning groups for customers and vendors. A planning group represents particular characteristics, behaviors, or risks of the customer or vendor group. In this way, you can break down incoming and outgoing payments according to the amount, the probability of the cash inflow or outflow, the type of business relationship, and so on.
questions.question: Is it planned to classify customers or vendors in your cash position (e.g. probability of payment) ? If yes, on which granularity level do you want to do this ?

questions.topicDefinition: Memo records generated from bank statements contain only planning type information. With this activity, you define planning types and map planning levels to planning types. This way, memo records generated from bank statements automatically acquire a planning level that can be used in further analysis.
questions.question: What kind of categorization of memo records do you plan to work with in Cash Management (e.g. confirmed or unconfirmed, from bank statements etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this activity, you can allocate blocked levels for the levels of the liquidity forecast. When you post with a payment blocking indicator, the system takes the blocked level instead of the standard level of the corresponding planning group.
questions.question: Are there any payment blocks for applications within Cash Management ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this Customizing activity, you can create and change liquidity items. You create liquidity items to represent the source and use of cash flows in your company. It can then be used as a dimension for financial planning and reporting in Cash and Liquidity Management.
questions.question: Out of which different sources do you receive cash flows in your company (including the cash flow direction, e.g. cash paid for tax, cash receipt from debt) ? Which structure and hierarchy (divided into business background) for incoming and outgoing payments should be applied (e.g. metals, commodities) ?

questions.topicDefinition: You use this Customizing activity when you want to process additional accounting document items that the system does not automatically classify. For this you can assign flow types to G/L accounts for additional journal entries (accounting documents) that are not automatically imported to the system. This is relevant for the flow types which categorize the flows in One Exposure (FQM_FLOW).
questions.question: Is there any need to create and assign "specific" flow types on G/L account level, besides the respective flow types in SAP Standard ?

questions.topicDefinition: Tolerance groups are relevant for defining groups for reconciliations between forecasted cash flows and intrady memo records. In this step, you define the tolerance groups for cash flow reconciliation. When you reconcile intraday memo records with forecasted cash flows, there might be a difference in the amount. The system then checks whether the bank account has a tolerance group defined. If the bank account has no tolerance group assigned, or the difference exceeds the defined limit of the tolerance group, the system prompts a warning message to warn you about the notable difference.
questions.question:
For the bank statement reconciliation, do you intend to have a tolerance with regards to the amount and percentage ?
How shall this tolerance be setup in the system?

questions.topicDefinition: In this step, you define profiles for the calculation of bank account balance in cash concentration. You then assign planning levels that represents the source and use of cash flows to these profiles. By assigning different planning levels, various forms of profiles can be predefined.
questions.question: Do you intend to maintain Cash Pools and therefore the Cash Concentration functionality ? Do you use specific calculation procedures for Cash Concentration for different Cash Pools ? Should the resulting transfers be classified with different planning levels depending on the profile ?

questions.topicDefinition: You can define your own additional activities for power of attorney. If you assign these activities in the power of attorney, they are only relevant for reporting purposes.
questions.question: For reporting on power of attorney, is it required to classify and distinguish various powers of attorney, e.g. according to the amount of the maximum payment allowed ?

questions.topicDefinition: When you create a power of attorney, you must assign an authorization group. Only users with authorization for the relevant authorization group can create, process, or display powers of attorney in the Manage Powers of Attorney for Banking Transactions app
questions.question: For the management of the power of attorney, are there separate gropus of users assigned to manage e.g. certain groups of bank accounts or bank accounts of certain company codes ?

questions.topicDefinition: With this activity, you define settings for integrating end-of-day electronic bank statements with cash management at company code level. You define how bank statement data is consumed by cash management, and whether posting is needed for imported bank statements.
questions.question:
Are there any company codes for which bank statements will not be posted in the system, but only be imported for cash management ?
Are there any company codes for which only the balance of each bank statement needs to be transferred to the system or is the transfer on item level always required ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Define the channels through which the power of attorney for banking transactions can be exercised.

A channel is managed either by the bank or by you. You assign the channels to the implementation.
questions.question: Are all your powers of attorney managed by you or are there any bank-managed ones ?

questions.topicDefinition: You use this activity to define what statuses are relevant in the bank account lifecycle, how bank accounts are activated in each status, and what tabs are visible in the bank account master data for a certain type of bank account. You can define different settings for different bank account contract types, account types, and company codes
questions.question: What are the required statuses for your bank accounts from opening to closing ? Are several different status schemes required for different groups of bank accounts or compayn codes ? How shall the transition from one status to the next and to the previous status be controlled for every status change, i.e. 2-person verification, workflow or direct change ?

questions.topicDefinition: Customers can define "bank account types" to classify their bank accounts. This can be useful to distinguish bank accounts for reporting purposes, e.g. bank accounts which are used exclusively by certain business areas or for a certain business purpose like loan accounts, ty accounts, payroll acconts, etc. Bank account types can also be used as selcetion criteria to structure the cash positioning in the Cash flow Analyzer App.
questions.question: Do you intend to structure your bank accounts into separate groups for reporting or processing purposes ? If yes, which groups exist and how will the bank accounts in within these gropus be used (are they current accounts used for payments and receiving bank statements, or technical accounts) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Certain fields of the bank account master Data can be defined as "sensitive". Depending on the assigned account control mode (e.g. workflow or dual control) a change in any of these sensitive fields triggers a change control process. 
Whether a field should be regarded as sensitive or not can depend on the bank account type (this can be an additional reason to introduce separate bank account types) or company code
questions.question:
For which of the fields in the bank account master data should a change control process be triggered when the content is changed ?
Does the sensitivity of bank account fields depend on company code ?
Are there separate gropus of bank account that require a different set of sensitive fields ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Per bank account it is possible to define users or groups of users which are allowed to approve payments made from this bank account.
If the payment approval functionality in bank account management is NOT used, then instead payment approvals can be defined in BCM (Bank Communication Management)
Groups of approvers can be defined and assigned to a bank account in the "manage bank accounts" app. Payments approval gropus can be assigned to bank account types and company codes and can be restricted according to the payment amount.
questions.question:
Which distinct business groups (e.g. users from treasury department and users from operative departments) of payment approvers with the same authorization level exist in your company ?
Are there multiple levels of approval and/or a dependence on payment amounts ?
Are there various approval patterns for different types of bank accounts (e.g. those accounts managed by the treasury department) or for different company codes ?

questions.topicDefinition: An authorization group can be assigned to a bank account in BAM. Only users authorized for this authorization group will be allowed to make changes to the resprective bank accounts.
questions.question: Is it required to distinguish certain groups of bank account which shall only be maintained by users with a special authorization ? (e.g. some users are only allowed to change "internal bank accounts", whereas others are allowed to change any)

questions.topicDefinition: For Email notifications sent from BAM, it is possible to specify templates and enable or disable the use of those
questions.question: What kind of E-Mail notifications shall be sent during the overall bank account management process and which E-Mail templates shall be used ?

questions.topicDefinition: For certain scenarios like "edit a bank account" or "display a bank account" it is possible to define the field status of the bank account master data, i.e. it can be specified which fields should be mandatory, hidden, or read-only
questions.question: Can you provide a list of bank account master data fields that are mandatory for your process ? Which fields shall not be editable or are not needed at all ?

questions.topicDefinition:
The following 4 data constellations are regarded as an error in the standard setup:
•Error message FCLM_BAM_MAINT187: In the Manage Bank Accounts app and the Maintain Payment Approver - For Multiple Bank Accounts app, this message appears when the system identifies a payment approver that is not a defined system user.
•Error message FCLM_BAM_MAINT466: In the Manage Bank Accounts app, this message appears when you try to link a house bank account with a different company code from the bank account or there are such cases in existing bank account master data.
•Error message FCLM_BAM_MAINT522: In the Manage Bank Accounts app, this message appears when the bank account description is missing in a certain language.
•Error message FCLM_BAM_MAINT537: In the Manage Bank Accounts app, this message appears when you try to link more than one house bank account with the ID category Central System: House Bank Account to a bank account or there are such cases in existing bank account master data.
questions.question: Are there any reasons why these errors need to be bypassed as warnings for all or certain users ?

questions.topicDefinition:
With Bank Account Management, each bank in use must be represented by a business partner instance and with a linkage maintained between the bank (entry in table BNKA) and the business partner instance. To define the business partners for banks, we recommend that you define the bank hierarchy first. After you define the position of a bank in the bank hierarchy, the system automatically assigns or creates a business partner, and establish the linkage between the business partner and the bank. After the bank is added to the hierarchy, the system checks whether the bank has a corresponding business partner instance with role TR0703.

In the bank account import file, you may maintain the Contact at Bank and Bank Relationship Managerfields. After the file is imported, the specified contact persons can be assigned to the bank account automatically and also assigned to the bank's business partner automatically. As the two contact persons are external to the company, they can only be represented by a business partner instance with the BP Role of BUP001 Contact Person
questions.question: Is there a list of banks you currently interact with ? Is it required to maintain and report a bank hierarchy ? Are you planning to capture contacts at banks or bank relationship managers within the Bank Account Management ? If so, please create a list with the respective information.

questions.topicDefinition:
The Transaction Manager is based on the business partner concept. Financial transactions are concluded with business partners within the Transaction Manager. Typical business partners include banks or central treasury departments.

You have to assign roles to your business partners, which correspond to the partner’s function in the financial transaction. The main roles are “Issuer” (TR0150), “Counterparty” (TR0151), “Depository Bank” (TR0152), “Beneficiary” (TR0154), and “Guarantor” (TR0200).
questions.question: How shall internal and external business partners (e.g. banks) be structured ? Are there specific naming conventions and number ranges which shall be applied ? Is there a list of business partners available with which you are currently interact with ? Please specify, which of them are relevant for which kind of transactions etc.

questions.topic: SAP Treasury and Risk Management Integration
questions.topicDefinition: Provides comprehensive features and functions to secure against financial risks (liquidity risks​, FX risks, counterparty risks, and further market risks). Accurate registration and a comprehensive view of all business activities aligned with (inter)national accounting principles such as IFRS and US GAAP is included.
questions.question:
Which of the following SAP Treasury and Risk Management functionalties are you intending to use:

- FX, derivatives, securities, money market, or trade finance transactions ?
- Market data management
- Exposure management
- Hedge management
- Treasury accounting
- Risk management (risk analyzer)
- Treasury analytics (reporting) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
The Trading Platform Integration connects external trading platforms (like 360T, FXall, Bloomberg etc.) with your SAP back-end system. With this SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) you can Transfer FX transactions, fixed term deposits/loans (money
market) and purchase/sale of money market funds from external trading platforms to your SAP system automatically. Addionally you can transfer trade requests from your SAP system to external trading platforms, store competitive bids, process intercompany trades, and for example check counterparty limits and its utilization.
questions.question: Are you intending to use the Trading Platform Integration to connect your SAP back-end system to your trading platform to transfer transactions automatically to your SAP TRM system ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for FX Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: [As a prerequisite, please see 104118]. Within this setting, you assign your predefined rounding rules and tolerances to currencies which are relevant for the calculation of the opposite amount in FX transactions.
questions.question: Which rounding rules should be setup for which company code and currency ? Additionally, what tolerance should be setup for these rounding rules in percent ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration step supports you if you need to create rounding rules, for example for calculating accrued interest for purchases and/or sales.
You can select one of these rules when you enter the purchase or sale of a bond in the system. Moreover, you have the option of defining a rounding rule in the class data. This then appears as a default value when you enter a transaction.
questions.question: Do you have specific rounding rules which need to be applied for financial transactions (e.g. bond issuance) ? Is there a need for specific rounding rules as a default value within a transaction ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: Wihtin this setting you can define fund types differentiating the kinds of funds. You assign the fond types in the class data. This setting is relevant for the securities area.
questions.question: Are you intending to implement funds within the securities area ? Is there a need to differentiate between different fund types (e.g. money market funds) for reporting purposes ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: Define the classifications that can be assigned to bond classes when they are created. These classifications let you subdivide bonds into groups that are independent of the system settings (such as product category and product type). This indicator can be used for evaluations, for example.
questions.question: Are you intending to implement bonds within the securities area ? Is there a need to classify the respective bonds (e.g. government bonds) for reporting purposes ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: [As a prerequisite, please see 104039]. You can assign bond classifications to product types. Classifications for bonds are defined in the Define Classification for Bonds configuration activity. The assignment of classifications to product types enables you to have specific classifications for the different product types.
questions.question: Which predefined classifications should be visible for which type of bonds (Product types) ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this step, you assign a calendar to the various currencies to determine the working days. The system performs a working day check to check all the flows that result from the transaction against the calendar defined here. Some calendars are predefined. You can define specific calendars in the configuration activity Maintain Calendar.
questions.question: Which local calendars are being used for the various currencies you are using ?

questions.topicDefinition: [This step is a prerequisite for 102794]. Via this configuration setting it is possible to define calculation indicators for currency translations of credit and debit postings. Therefore you can define a Rate Calculation ID and assign a rate type (e.g. M - Standard translation at average rate) for debit and credit postings.
questions.question: With regards to currency translations, how many calculation indicators are needed for credit and debit postings ? Which rate types (e.g. M - Standard translation at average rate) should be applied to the respective indicators ?

questions.topicDefinition: For the update to Cash Management, you need to assign a planning level for the combinations of company code, product type, and activity type. The Cash Management planning level explains the origin of the opening and closing account balances for the cash position and liquidity forecast.
questions.question: Are you planning to use Cash Management ? If yes, on which granularity level are you planning to report treasury transactions within Cash Management (e.g. product type, activity/status) ?

questions.topicDefinition: Within this configuration step it is possible to assign the bank identifier code (BIC) to company codes, change the calculation indicator, and indicate the relevant company codes as treasury centers. This can be used for correspondence, exchange rates and for treasury reporting purposes.
questions.question: Are you planning to use the correspondence framework and if yes, which BIC codes do you have for the affected company codes ? Do you have different currencies which need to be setup for the different company codes ? What kind of Fiscal Year Variant should be applied for the different company codes ? With regards to the exchange rate calculation indicators of the mentioned company codes, which should be used for the relevant company codes ? Is there a need to report specific Treasury Centers and if yes, which company codes should be marked and what rank should they receive ?

questions.topicDefinition: Define portfolios per company code. You use the portfolios as an organizational element to group various financial transactions for reporting purposes. You can use this once you create a financial transaction via assigning the portfolio on the Administration tab. Afterwards the usage as a selection criterion or as an analysis characteristic in risk management is possible.
questions.question: Is there a need to group transactions for reporting ? How many different groupings are needed ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this configuration step you have the possibilty to define your rating procedures and the assignment of ratings to them. You can rate business partners by different means, such as their credit standing and payment history, or according to other criteria. Ratings can be performed according to your own rules, as well as through specialist service providers, such as Standard & Poors or Schufa. Several rating procedures have already been delivered. You can define others according to your requirements. You can also set one of the rating procedures as the standard rating procedure and flag this rating procedure as internal.
questions.question: Are you intending to rate specific business partners (e.g. by credit standing, payment history etc.) ? Is this only related to a specific group of business partners (e.g. banks) ? Is it planned to have information (like rating agency ratings) imported as market data ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for FX Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this step, you define the leading currencies for the various currency pairs. The system uses these settings to determine the rate notation when you enter FX spot/forward transactions and FX options.
In addition, you can enter the number of days between conclusion of the FX transaction and the value date in the Spot Days field. Usually, this is two working days. Depending on the currency, there may be deviations from this rule. You should only make an entry in this field if practices on the international foreign exchange market follow a different rule to the usual two-day rule.
questions.question: Which currency pairs are relevant for your FX transactions ? With regards to the currency pair, which currency shall be the leading and which one the following currency ? For these FX transactions, is there a need to define a number of days between conclusion of the FX transaction and the value date (Spot Days) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for FX Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define which currencies are non-deliverable. A non-deliverable currency is a currency that is thinly traded or non-convertible.
When you create a non-deliverable forward (NDF), the system uses the entries in this table to establish which of the currencies entered in the NDF transaction is the non-deliverable one. The currency that is deliverable is then set as the settlement currency.
You can change the settlement currency to another currency afterwards. The check is only executed once.
questions.question: Which non-deliverable currencies are you intending to use ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Intercompany Trading
questions.topicDefinition: Within this setting you can determine the product types and transaction types for which mirror transactions can be created for affiliated companies.
questions.question: Do you have intercompany trades (e.g. Money Market, FX) ? Out of which company codes (outgoing) are these trades being created and with which corresponding partner (incoming) ? Which product and transaction types are affected ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Intercompany Trading
questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can map the company codes and the business partners representing them to enable the mirror transaction function.
You have different company codes representing the affiliated companies of your enterprise. If you want to use the mirror transaction function, you must create a business partner for each affiliated company code. In this configuration activity, you map the company codes and the business partners representing them.
questions.question: Company codes need to be affiliated with a business partner in role TR0151 Counterparty for trade mirroring. Which company codes should be affiliated with which business partner ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Intercompany Trading
questions.topicDefinition: This setting is relevant for the mapping of the different product and transaction types for trade mirroring. This has to setup as an Outgoing direction (sending company code) and Incoming direction (receiving company code). The meta text is a unique identifier between the Outgoing and Incoming direction.
questions.question: Which company codes are currently triggering the mirror transactions (outgoing)? Which receiving (incoming) company codes are there ? What product & transaction type combination is intended to be used ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Intercompany Trading
questions.topicDefinition:
This step is only relevant for cash flow transactions. Here you can map the product type and transaction type to a flow type for cash flow transactions.
The flow types for other products are read from the mapping table defined under Map Product Types and Transaction Types.
questions.question: Is it planned to use cash flow transactions (product category 540) ? Which product and transaction types should be mapped to which flow types ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Intercompany Trading
questions.topicDefinition:
In this step you can maintain the table for processing incoming data from the view of the receiving company code with the product/transaction types that have already been mirrored.
The entries for the activities and the activity categories are predefined in the system. The system only supports the mirror function. The counterparty is the business partner assigned to the sending company code.
questions.question: [SAP ID 101134 is a prerequiste]. With regards to the incoming (receiving) company code of a mirror transaction, what company codes are on the receiving (incoming) side and with which business partner (outgoing) ? Which product and transaction types are affected ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: Via this configuration step you can define the bank guarantee types that you need. When you create a bank guarantee transactions, you need to specify a bank guarantee type from those defined.
questions.question: What bank guarantee types are you intending to use (e.g. Credit Facilities Guarantee, Lease Guarantee) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Money Market Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define the necessary flow types for your product types in the Money Market area.
A flow type must be defined for all possible flows in a financial transaction so that they can later be assigned.
These settings are preconfigured. Update the settings per your needs. For example, if you need an additional flow type for specific charges.
questions.question: For the Money Market area, are there any kind of specific flows (e.g. Fees, commissions, tax) which need to be setup ? Are these flows only relevant for outgoing/incoming payments or both ? Are there any flows which are not covered in SAP Standard ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for FX Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define the necessary flow types for your product types in the Foreign Exchange area.
A flow type must be defined for all possible flows in a financial transaction so that they can later be assigned.
These settings are preconfigured. Update the settings per your needs. For example, if you need an additional flow type for specific charges.
questions.question: For the Foreign Exchange area, are there any kind of specific flows (e.g. Fees, Commissions, Tax) which need to be setup ? Are these flows only relevant for outgoing/incoming payments or both ? Are there any flows which are not covered in SAP Standard ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for OTC Derivative Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define the necessary flow types for your product types in the OTC Derivatives area.
A flow type must be defined for all possible flows in a financial transaction so that they can later be assigned.
These settings are preconfigured. Update the settings per your needs. For example, if you need an additional flow type for specific charges.
questions.question: For the OTC Derivatives area, are there any kind of specific flows (e.g. Fees, Commissions, Tax) which need to be setup ? Are these flows only relevant for outgoing/incoming payments or both ? Are there any flows which are not covered in SAP Standard ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define the necessary flow types for your product types in the Trade Finance area.
A flow type must be defined for all possible flows in a financial transaction so that they can later be assigned.
These settings are preconfigured. Update the settings per your needs. For example, if you need an additional flow type for specific charges.
questions.question: For the Trade Finance area, are there any kind of specific flows (e.g. Fees, Commissions, Tax) which need to be setup ? Are these flows only relevant for outgoing/incoming payments or both ? Are there any flows which are not covered in SAP Standard ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Money Market Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
[SAP ID 102106 is a prerequisite]. Assign the flow types to the transaction types of your product types in the money market area that are necessary to completely portray the financial instruments.
Via New entries, you assign the necessary flow types to all the defined combinations from the product and transaction type. Save your entries.
questions.question: [SAP ID 102106 is a prerequisite]. The already defined flow types (or SAP Standard flow types), for which product/transaction type combination are they being applied ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for FX Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
[SAP ID 102109 is a prerequisite]. Assign the flow types to the transaction types of your product types in the FX area that are necessary to completely portray the financial instruments.
Via New entries, you assign the necessary flow types to all the defined combinations from the product and transaction type. Save your entries.
questions.question: [SAP ID 102109 is a prerequisite]. The already defined flow types (or SAP Standard Flow Types), for which Product/Transaction Type combination are they being applied ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for OTC Derivative Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
[SAP ID 102107 is a prerequisite]. Assign the flow types to the transaction types of your product types in the OTC Derivative area that are necessary to completely portray the financial instruments.
Via New entries, you assign the necessary flow types to all the defined combinations from the product and transaction type. Save your entries.
questions.question: [SAP ID 102107 is a prerequisite]. The already defined flow types (or SAP Standard Flow Types), for which Product/Transaction Type combination are they being applied ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
[SAP ID 102108 is a prerequisite]. Assign the flow types to the transaction types of your product types in the trade finance area that are necessary to completely portray the financial instruments.
Via New entries, you assign the necessary flow types to all the defined combinations from the product and transaction type. Save your entries.
questions.question: [SAP ID 102108 is a prerequisite]. The already defined flow types (or SAP Standard Flow Types), for which Product/Transaction Type combination are they being applied ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this step, you check or complete the assignment of a contract type and flow type to the cash flow indicator and the indicator for fictitious cash flows. Assign the cash flow indicator to your flow types.
These settings are relevant for the net present value calculation. All flows of a financial transaction need to be assigned to a cash flow indicator, otherwise the NPV calculation is stopped. Set the fictitious indicator for a flow if you do not want to consider that flow in the NPV calculation.
Proposals for the assignment of the cash flow indicator depend on the calculation category of the flow types.
questions.question: For the net present value (NPV) calculation, are there any cash flows which are indicated as fictitious and not considered in the NPV calculation ? Are there any flow types which have "special" cash flow indicators (besides SAP Standard) which need to be assigned ?

questions.topicDefinition:

You can choose the values you enter here in the financial transaction data using the input help. If you don't want to use these values, you can also enter any other text in this field.
questions.question: Is there a specific need to assign financial transactions to a specific group (e.g. for reporting) ? What kind of groupings should be available ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step, you can define values for the Characteristics field on the Administration tab within the financial transaction data.
You can choose the values you enter here in the financial transaction data using the input help. If you don't want to use these values, you can also enter any other text in this field.
questions.question: Is there a specific need to assign financial transactions to a specific group (e.g. for reporting) ? What kind of groupings should be available ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step, you can define values for the Internal Reference field on the Administration tab within the financial transaction data.
You can choose the values you enter here in the financial transaction data using the input help. If you don't want to use these values, you can also enter any other text in this field.
questions.question: Is there a specific need to assign financial transactions to a specific group (e.g. for reporting) ? What kind of groupings should be available ?
