questions.topicDefinition: Via this configuration step, you can define document types related to L/C by a name and a description, which can be assigned to document templates later.
questions.question: For Trade Finance Transactions, what kind of document types shall be implemented (e.g. Application, Contract Document) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Money Market Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this activity, you can assign the time and amount structure to the various financial transactions via condition types. Interest, repayment or commission are examples of condition types. Define the necessary condition types for your product types.
Condition types automatically generate flows which are the basis for further processing in Finance  and Cash Management as well as for analysis in Treasury and Risk Management. The classification divides up the condition types according to business criteria. Via the chosen classification, you restrict the possible condition categories. Condition categories allow the system to interpret and process your settings.
questions.question: Are there any "special" conditions (besides the SAP Standard conditions) which are required (e.g. reoccuring fees on a conditional basis) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Money Market Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: [SAP ID 103139 is a prerequisite]. Here you can assign the necessary condition types to each product type at transaction type level to be able to represent a financial product completely.
questions.question: Which conditions shall be applied for which Product/Transaction Type combination ? Are there any conditions (like fees) which are reoccuring on a conditional basis ? For facility transactions, which conditional flows should be assigned ?

questions.topicDefinition: Via this configuration step, it is possible to maintain attributes for FX transactions, such as rate type, translation to LC etc.
questions.question: What exchange rate type shall be applied for which FX transaction (e.g. M - Standard translation at average rate) ? Shall foreign currency flows be translated to local currency using the transaction rate ?

questions.topicDefinition:
With this activity, you can define derivation procedures and rules for derived flows, such as tax flows.
You can generate additional flows automatically based on an original flow. You do this by defining derivation procedures and then assigning rules to each procedure. The rules determine how one flow is generated from another. The derived flow is a percentage of the original flow amount.

Important note:
In order to apply a derivation procedure when a transaction is created, you must assign the derivation procedure to a business partner. You make this assignment in the business partner master data using the function Standing Instructions: Derived Flows.
questions.question: Is there a need to define derivation procedures for e.g. for interest income tax ? If yes, for which products will this be relevant (please also refer to the validity date and the respective flows) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Money Market Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define the different transaction types for your product types. Define which administration functions/processes you want to use for the different business types.
The transaction type is used to structure the different types of financial transactions of a product type specifically. The transaction types are based on the transaction categories available for a product category.
questions.question: For the Money Market area, which transaction type are you intending to use (e.g. borrowing, investment) ? For which Product Types are you planning to use these Transaction Types ? If Facilities are intended to implement, which Transaction Types are relevant for Facilities (e.g. obtained/received or assigned) ? If Commercial Papers are planned to implement in the Money Market Module, please define the assignment of Purchase and Sale Transaction Types for the respective Product Types.

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define the different transaction types for your product types. Define which administration functions/processes you want to use for the different transaction types.
The transaction type is used to structure the different types of financial transaction of a product type specifically. The transaction types are based on the transaction categories available for a product category.
questions.question: Which Transaction Types are needed for Letter of Credits and Bank Guarantees (e.g. Applicant/Issue or Beneficiary/Receive) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Usage of Derived Flows is a prerequisite]. In this activity, you can define the calculation procedures for generating derived flows.
By defining calculation procedures, you can control the amount of the derived flows in relation to the currency and the amount of the original flow.
By choosing 'Define Derivation Procedures and Rules', you can then select one of the calculation procedures when you define the derivation rules.
questions.question: [Usage of Derived Flows is a prerequisite]. Do you intend to use specific calculation rules for derived flows, such as charges that increase at a specific nominal amount (or any other) ? Is there a list with all these calculation rules available ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
[Definition of Document Types is a prerequisite]. With this step you can define document templates and assign multiple document types to one document template.
When assigning document types to a document template, you can decide whether they are used in the creation of L/C or presentation of L/C by selecting the corresponding checkboxes. You can also specify the number of originals and copies needed. When you create an L/C or a presentation (delivery of documents) for an L/C, you can select a document template so that all the document types of this template are automatically displayed. In this way, you do not need to enter the related document types one by one.
questions.question: [Definition of Document Types is a prerequisite]. Is there a need to define specific document templates ? If yes, to which document types should these templates be assigned to ? Please specifiy if they are relevant for the creation, presentation, and additionally the number of originals and copies which are needed.

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: On this configuration step you can define rejection reasons for L/C presentations by assigning a reason code and a description that you can select later when you reject a presentation.
questions.question: Please define a list of rejection reasons for L/C presentations if needed.

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration activity allows you to Assign condition types to condition groups.
As a prerequisite the condition types must already be defined under Define Condition Types - Securities. The condition groups are predefined in the system. You must assign all condition types needed for a specific condition group. In addition, you define the sequence in which the condition types within a condition group are displayed, and for which condition types entries are mandatory. Conditions that are used less frequently in a particular condition group can be suppressed. The suppressed condition types are not shown in the standard maintenance dialog. You need to make an additional selection to call them up.
questions.question: Are there specific conditions which can be gathered in a group with regards to the assignment to the related Product Type (e.g. for Issued Bonds) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition: Via this setting you can define transaction types and assign these to the product types for securities. You also define the main technical aspects of Transaction Management.
questions.question: For the Securities area, which transaction type are you intending to use (e.g. Purchase, Sale, Issue (Placement), Issue (Redemption)) ? For which Product Types are you planning to use these Transaction Types ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define condition types. For this you create a three-character key and assign the appropriate flow type to it. The system then assigns the flow category and the FiMa calculation category from the flow type to the condition type automatically.
To ensure correct cash flow processing, you must enter a reference condition type for some condition types. For floaters, for example, the interest rate adjustment date or the fixing of the maximum or minimum interest rate refers to the variable interest rate. You must enter the indicator of the corresponding reference condition type in the RefC field (in this case, Variable Interest).
For some condition types, you only need to enter the FiMa calculation category.
There are SAP Standard condition types are delivered with the system to cover common business transactions in the securities area. You can use these condition types without making any adjustments:
Condition Type	Condition Type Text
100	Interest (Percentage-Quoted)
101	Variable Interest
111	Dividend
113	Bonus
116	Profit Distribution
118	Repayment Rate
119	Repayment Price
133	Additional Payment
134	Interest (Unit-Quoted)
209	Interest Rate Adjustment
263	Full Repayment upon Maturity
questions.question: Are there any "special" conditions (besides the SAP Standard conditions) which are required (e.g. reoccuring fees on a conditional basis) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Securities Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
With this configuration step you assign a flow category to each flow type. The system uses the flow category to determine the calculation category. The classification, which divides the flow types according to business criteria, is always Structure for transaction flow types, and is therefore predefined in the system.
For each flow type, you define whether you want the flows to be updated to Cash Management and Financial Accounting, in other words, whether they are relevant to Cash Management and to posting.
Using the Net Payment Amount indicator, you can determine whether the flow is included in the net payment amount* calculation
questions.question: For the Securities area, are there any kind of specific flows (e.g. Fees, Commissions, Tax) which need to be setup ? Are these flows only relevant for outgoing/incoming payments or both ? Are there any flows which are not covered in SAP Standard ?

questions.topicDefinition:

As a prerequisite you have defined the transaction types you require for the product types in the Define Transaction Types - Securities configuration activity and defined the transaction flow types in the Define Flow Types for Transaction -Securities configuration activity.
questions.question: For the Securities area, are there any kind of specific flows (e.g. Fees, Commissions, Tax) which need to be setup ? Are these flows only relevant for outgoing/incoming payments or both ? Are there any flows which are not covered in SAP Standard ?

- Cash Management (e.g. Planning types)

questions.question: For the update in Cash Management, is it required to have specific planning types assigned for the respective product type ? questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:
In this step you assign the time and amount structure to the various financial transactions that you wish to represent in Transaction Manager through condition types. Interest, repayment, or commission are examples of condition types. Condition types automatically generate flows, which are the basis for further processing in FI and Cash Management as well as for the analysis in Market Risk Analyzer.
To define your condition types, you assign the following:

A classification
A condition category
A flow type
The classification categorizes the condition types according to business criteria. You restrict the possible condition categories through the chosen classification. Condition categories allow the system to interpret and process your settings.
To be able to assign a flow type to the condition types, you first need to define the flow types using the activity Define Flow Types.
questions.question: Are there any "special" conditions (besides the SAP Standard conditions) which are required (e.g. reoccuring fees on a conditional basis) ?

questions.topic: Treasury Master Data for Trade Finance Transactions
questions.topicDefinition:

As a prerequisite the settings in the activity Define Product Types, you have defined the product types that you require. In the activity Define Transaction Types, you have defined the transaction types necessary for the product types. In the activity Define Condition Types*, you have defined all the necessary condition types and assigned the flow types that need to be generated from the condition type.
questions.question: Which conditions shall be applied for which Product/Transaction Type combination ? Are there any conditions (like fees) which are reoccuring on a conditional basis ?

questions.question: For the OTC Derivative area, which transaction types are you intending to use (e.g. Swap, Purchase, Sale) ? For which Product Types are you planning to use these Transaction Types ?

Classification

Flow type

questions.topicDefinition:
This activity gives you the possibility to define or adapt product types for money market transactions based on the available product categories.
Product types help to distinguish between different money market financial instruments. Differentiation is necessary if the individual instruments are subject to different processing rules or if you want to create different levels for the evaluation. By assigning different structural characteristics, various forms of transactions can be predefined.
The financial transaction is only finally set up by combining the product type with a transaction type.

questions.topicDefinition:
Product types help to distinguish between different money market financial instruments. Differentiation is necessary if the individual instruments are subject to different processing rules or if you want to create different levels for the evaluation. By assigning different structural characteristics, various forms of transactions can be predefined.

By assigning product types to condition groups, you ensure that only certain conditions types can be maintained or displayed as standard conditions for each product type.
The product category is an internal key that controls how the product type assigned to it is processed. The following product categories are available for the securities area:
010 Stock
020 Investment Fund
040 Bond
Several product types can refer to one product category

Differentiation is necessary if the individual instruments are subject to different processing rules or if you want to create different levels for the evaluation. By assigning different structural characteristics, you can predefine various forms of transactions.
The financial transaction is only finally set up by combining the product type with a transaction type.
questions.question: In the OTC Interest Rate Derivatives area, what Product Types are intended to be used in the future setup (e.g. Swaps, FRAs, etc.) ? Do these instruments need to be separated in different Product Types (e.g. for Reporting purposes) ?

questions.question: For securities account management, is it required to maintain an additional assignment for update types to specific functions of securities account management (e.g. debit position, manual posting, etc.) ? If so, please specify for each relevant function.

questions.question: For securities account management, is it required to create additional update types besides the SAP Standard content ? If so, please define the update type and specify what calculation type, effective interest calculation settings, payment directions, flow classifications, and debit position settings shall be taken.

questions.topicDefinition:
Assign the cash flow indicator and the indicator for fictitious cash flows to securities update types.

questions.question: For the securities area, is it required to assign specific update types to cash flow indicators besides the assignment in SAP Standard ? Are there any combinations which shall be marked as fictitous ? If so, please specify.

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: The update types must be created in the configuration activity Define Update Types and Assign Usages and assigned to usage 9001 Derived Business Transactions. The position management procedures must have been created in the configuration activity Define Position Management Procedure]. Via this step you assign update types for the derived business transactions. Derived business transactions are triggered by operative business transactions and complement them. This means that the derived business transactions can be different for different valuation areas, even if they stem from the same operative business transactions.
questions.question: Which update types are relevant for the assignment of derived business transactions ? Is it required to make any adjustments to the SAP Standard settings ? If an update type needs to be posted, you define the posting rules for the update type in the Define Account Determination activity]. You must assign the update types for all relevant valuation procedures of a position management procedure.

Standard Settings:
Predefined settings for all predefined position management procedures are available. You can adjust the settings to suit your requirements.
questions.question: Which update types are relevant for valuation purposes ? Is it required to make any adjustments to the SAP Standard settings ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this step you can replace the update types for derived business transactions with alternative update types, based on certain conditions. The position change category of the old update type is automatically assigned to the new update type.You make these settings for a given position management procedure. Alternative update types can be used to avoid P/L inflation. The P/L account is inflated when the system generates income-related derived business transactions that offset each other (such as a realized price loss and a positive OCI translation). By using alternative update types, you can group these flows and post them to the same P/L account.
The following conditions are currently supported:
01 Total amount realized for security >= 0
02 Total amount realized for security < 0
03 Total amount realized for foreign currency >= 0
04 Total amount realized for foreign currency < 0
05 P-Hedge Accounting
07 P-Hedge Accounting: Hedge Adjustment
08 Reclassification after Balance Sheet Recognition
Total amount realized for security = Security price gain - Security price loss + Translation of security write-up (not posted to P/L) - Translation of security write-down (not posted to P/L) + [Translation of discount - Translation of premium]

Total amount realized for foreign currency = Exchange rate gain - Exchange rate loss + Translation of FX write-up (not posted to P/L) - Translation of FX write-down (not posted to P/L)

[...] only relevant for gross procedure

You can maintain alternative update types with condition 08 Reclassification after Balance Sheet Recognition in the hedge management and accounting of net open exposures solution. These alternative update types allow reclassification postings to different G/L accounts after the balance sheet recognition date, if balance sheet recognition is configured in the hedging area.
questions.question: Is it required to replace update types for derived business transactions with alternative update types, based on certain conditions (e.g. to avoid P/L inflation) ? If so, please specifiy the position management procedure, the "old" update type and the "new" update type.

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: Define the update types and assign them to the usage Transaction Management]. Via this activity you assign an update type for open and close transactions for product types and transaction types of FX transactions, OTC derivatives, and futures.
questions.question: For FX, OTC derivatives, and futures, which update types shall be be assigned for the respective open and close transactions ? Please additionally specify product and transaction types.

Predefined Content:
Position Outflow: AAT_I001 AAT - Internal - Position Outflow
Position Inflow: AAT_I002 AAT - Internal - Position Inflow
questions.question: For the flows related to account assignment transfers, is it required to change the predefined SAP Standard content ? If so, please specify and additionally provide product type and transaction type information if required.

questions.topicDefinition:

questions.question: Which of your update types are relevant for Cash Management ?

Note:

The update types have been assigned to the usage Exercise rights in the Update Types to Usages configuration activity available in your configuration environment]. You assign the update types for posting the position inflows and outflows and payment flows.
If you have selected the differentiation term Lot to split up your positions in the parallel valuation areas, you also define how lots should be created for the rights categories.

Note:
You can also make generic entries. In this case, you do not select a particular rights category, and the entries apply for all rights categories. If, however, a more specific entry exists for a rights category, this overrides the generic entry.
questions.question:
Are you executing rights within the securities area ? Example for exercise rights would be:
- Callable Bond
- Puttable Bond
- Security Swap
- Stock Option
- Bond Option etc.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have defined the update types beforehand]. For the valuation class transfer, assign one update type for the clearing and one for the posting of the units/nominals.

Standard Settings
In the predefined content, the following settings are made:
VT_001 Clear Units/Nominal
VT_002 Post Units/Nominal
You can't delete the settings in this configuration activity.
questions.question: Is it required to change the predefined standard content from SAP in case of valuation class transfers ? If so, please specify.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: The update types have been defined]. Within this configuration you define the components to be included in the account assignment reference transfer and the corresponding update types for these components.You restrict the components by selecting the account symbols. The system only considers account symbols with the following posting categories:

1 Position posting in position currency
6 Other G/L account posting in position currency
7 Other G/L account posting in payment currency
4 Profit-related posting in position currency
5 Profit-related posting in payment currency
questions.question: For the transfer of account assignment references, which components shall be included ? Are there components which shall be restricted ? Please specify the relevant account symbols and choose the required update types for clearing and posting.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: If you want to consider the accrued interests as part of accrual/deferral, the following conditions must be fulfilled:
Either the position change category for the accrued interest update types must be 1000 No Position Change or you do not make an entry for the update types under Set Effects of Update Types on Position Components. Make settings for the difference procedure in the configuration activity Update Types for Accrual/Deferral using the update types AD1004 and AD1995. Do not set the With Netting Acct indicator for the difference procedure in the configuration activity Update Types for Accrual/Deferral.
The following update types must be relevant for posting:
SAM5000 Nominal Interest Rate
AD1004 Accrual
AD1005 Reset Accrual
SE8701 Accrued Interest Received
SE8702 Accrued Interest to Pay
Configure the FI posting of the update types as follows:
Update Type - Debit - Credit
SAM5000 - Bank - Accrual
AD1004	- Accrual - Revenue
AD1005	- Revenue - Accrual
SE8701 - Bank - Accrual
SE8702 - Accrual - Bank
The account for the account symbols Accrual and Revenue must be identical for all positions between which transfer postings can be made]. The settings in this configuration activity are relevant for the following situations: If you want to consider accrued interests as part of accruals/deferrals according to the difference procedure. In this case, you must assign the update types for the accrued interest to the relevant accrual/deferral settings as well.
If you have used the legacy data transfer to transfer accruals/deferrals for positions according to the difference procedure, you need to make sure that the accrual/deferral function recognizes the accrual/deferral flows. This way, the 'old' accruals/deferrals are considered with future accruals/deferrals.
For profit-related flows that are accrued/deferred according to the difference procedure, you define which update types in the legacy data transfer represent these accruals/deferrals.
questions.question:
Do you consider accrued interests as part of accruals/deferrals according to the difference procedure ? If so, please specify the assignment of  update types for the accrued interest to the relevant accrual/deferral settings.

Are you intending to use the legacy data transfer to transfer accruals/deferrals for positions according to the difference procedure ? If so, how shall the 'old' accruals/deferrals are mapped with future accruals/deferrals ?

questions.topicDefinition: This activity allows you to assign the required update types to the corporate action categories.
questions.question: Is it currently planned to capture corporate actions within the Treasury and Risk Management module ? If so, which corporate actions (like e.g. stock split, capital reduction, etc.) and which update types shall be assigned to position inflow and outflow ?

questions.topicDefinition: Within this step you can mark the update types that are relevant for payment.
questions.question: Which of your update types are shall be marked as payment relevant ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: The update types must be defined]. Within this step you assign a position change category to update types that are not generatedin the treasury subledger but are required there.
This assignment is only relevant for update types that are not generated in the treasury subledger but are required there.
You can assign the following position change categories:

1000 No Position Change
1002 Incoming Payment
1004 Post Clearing Items
1005 Post Negative Clearing Items
1006 Indirect Position Change
1010 Post Negative Purchase Value
1011 Post Purchase Value
1012 Post Variation Margin
1013 Clear Variation Margin
1014 Post Costs to Cost Component (assign the update types for capitalized costs if the capitalized costs are to be noted separately (exclusively))
1015 Post Costs to Purchase Value Component (assign the update types forcapitalized costs if the capitalized costs are to be included)
1020 Outgoing Payment
1021 Post Accrued Interest Paid
1022 Post Accrued Interest Received
1023 Post Repayment (Negative)
1024 Clear Repayment (Positive)
1025 Post Deferral Items; Post Negative Purchase Value
1026 Post Negative Deferral Items; Post Purchase Value
9999 Excluded from Position Management
In the case of derived business transactions, valuation flows, position initialization flows, and so on, you may not make any assignments here.

To post accrued interest via a compensation account, you must make the following settings to post to the accrued interest position component:

Position change type 1022 (Post Accrued Interest Paid) is assigned to the update type for accrued interest to be paid when a purchase is made.
Position change type 1021 (Post Accrued Interest Received) is assigned to the update type for accrued interest received when a sale is made.
Note:

If no assignment is made for an update type here, the update type is not taken into account when determining the position component.
questions.question: For the areas of FX, money market, derivatives, etc. specific update types are assigned to position change categories (e.g. post purchase value). Are there any update type to position change categories assignments which are required besides the preconfigured SAP Standard ? If yes, please specify and define if this only relevant for specific valuation areas or accounting codes.

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this step you assign the corresponding update types to the flow types used in transaction management of Treasury and Risk Management.
These settings are preconfigured. Update the settings according to your needs.
questions.question: For the areas of FX, money market, derivatives, etc. specific flow types are assigned to update types. Are there any flow type to update types assignments which are required besides the preconfigured SAP Standard ? If yes, please specify and define the direction and contract type of these entries.

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define all the update types that are required to manage the positions in the parallel valuation areas.
Update types carry information about flows to accounting. In this configuration activity, you can define the update types and assign them to their usages.
Note: One update type can be assigned to different usages.
An update type is assigned to a usage if the following applies:
The update type is created by the usage.
The update type is processed in the usage.
The following usages require update types:
Transaction Management
Accrual/Deferral
Initialize Positions
Derived Business Transactions
Key Date Valuation
Transfer Account Assignment Reference
Hedge Accounting for Positions
Legacy Data Transfer
Valuation Class Transfer
These settings are preconfigured. Update the settings according to your needs.
questions.question: For the areas of FX, money market, derivatives, etc. specific update types are preconfigured in SAP Standard. Are there any update types which are required besides the preconfigured SAP Standard ? If yes, please specify and define the usage of these update types (e.g. transaction management).

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have defined your update types]. Define derivation rules for tax flows and enter the relevant tax rates for various flows in the securities area.
The system uses the amount in the original flow (or incoming flow) and the tax rate that has been defined here in order to generate a flow record for the taxes (outgoing flow) automatically.
questions.question: Are you intending to derive tax flows in your Treasury system ? If so, please specify the relevant company codes, products, countries, securities accounts, and percentage. Additionally please define which incoming and outgoing update types are relevant and if a rounding needs to be applied.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: The update types must already be defined and assigned to usages in the Define Update Types and Assign Usages configuration activity. In addition, all necessary settings for the update types need to be made, such as Indicate Update Types as Relevant to Posting and Define Account Determination]. Within this step you can define which revenue flows you want to accrue/defer and which accrual/deferral procedure and method you want to use.
You make the accrual/deferral settings for the following product groups:
001 Securities
003 OTC Transactions: Money Market, Forex, Derivatives
questions.question: For the usage of accrual and deferral, which update types are relevant and which procedure (difference/reset) and method (e.g. pro rata) shall be used ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You must define the update types under Define and Assign Update Types]. This configuration allows you to assign update types to product types for the creation of open and close business transactions. You assign update types to product types for the creation of the open and close business transactions. This enables position management and accounting processes for exposure subitems. The update type for the open is needed within the hedging relationship on the start date of the exposure subitem.
The update type for the close is needed within the hedging relationship on the end date of the exposure subitem.
questions.question: Are you intending to use the hedge accounting functionality via the SAP Treasury and Risk Management module ? If so, please specify the product types and the update types which are required for open and close business transactions.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You define the update types under Define Update Types and Assign Usages]. Via this step you assign update types to the business transactions relevant for hedge accounting. You use this activity to assign update types to the following business transactions:

Designation
Dedesignation
Classification
Reset Classification
Reclassification
Swap Transfer: The update types for the swap transfer are relevant for the creation of incoming and outgoing transfer flows.
Alternative Hedging Reclassification
Dedesignation Transfer: This business transaction is needed during the execution of an FX option used as hedging instrument, when you decided to designate the underlying FX transaction into the existing hedging relationship.
Designation Transfer: This business transaction is needed during the execution of an FX option used as hedging instrument, when you decided to designate the underlying FX transaction into the existing hedging relationship.
questions.question:
Are you intending to use the hedge accounting functionality via the SAP Treasury and Risk Management module ? If so, please specify the product types and additionally define update types for:
- Designation (+/-)
- Dedesignation (+/-)
- Classification
- Reset Classification
- Reclassification
- Swap Transfer (+/-)
- Alternative Hedging Reclassification
- Desdesignation Transfer (+/-)
- Designation Transfer (+/-)

questions.topicDefinition: Within this step, you define the position management procedures you require, which establish the rules for managing the treasury positions, for example, how the positions are valued, and how the derived business transactions are generated in the case of position outflows or balance sheet transfers. You can create a new position management procedure, copy an existing position management procedure, change an existing position management procedure, or display the existing position management procedures.
questions.question:
For treasury position management different valuation and amortization steps can be configured. Within SAP Standard some examples are being given. Is it necessary to change the exisiting procedures ? If yes, please specifiy the different requirements, such as:
- Valuation (& procedures)
- Amortization (& procedures)
- Impairment procedure
- Write-Off procedure
- Hedge Accounting (evaluation type & CVA/DVA type)
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this configuration step you can define the sorting sequence of the corporate action in relation to the other business transactions for each corporate action category.

There is a fixed relation between corporate action categories and business transaction categories. If the system needs to sort business transactions the following logic for corporate action business transactions is executed:

1. Get the corporate action category for the business transaction category.
2. Check if configuration for sorting priority exists.
1 Move Corporate Action to End of Day
Corporate actions get sorting priority 08.
Example: A purchase, a sale and a stock split all take place on the same day.
questions.question: If you have predefined corporate actions with the Treasury and Risk Management you can sort them in different sequences. Which corporate action category (e.g. stock split, stock swap, etc.) shall be assigned to which sorting sequence (e.g. move corporate action to start of day, end of day, or default system settings) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This steps helps you to define valuation procedures for the valuation category 012 Transfer Current Portion that posts the amount of repayments for a treasury position that are due within a certain period (for example, within the next 12 months) to a specific G/L account for balance sheet purposes.

Use
The valuation step is executed with a reset transfer at key date + 1 day.

The valuation category is relevant for the following position management categories: Securities/Loans/Money Market Transactions/Listed Options
Normal Style (Without Index-Linked Bonds), Securities/Loans with Installment Repayment (Without Index-Linked Bonds)
Index-Linked Bonds
questions.question: Is it a requirement to post the amounts of repayments for a treasury position that are due within a certain period (e.g. 12 months) to a specific G/L accountg ? If yes, for how many months, to which rate type, nominal or book value, and to which conversion rate (book rate or market rate) ?

questions.topicDefinition: In this configuration activity, you define valuation steps that are executed when you change positions, transfer postings, or valuate key dates. Once you have defined each valuation step, you must make settings in the following configuration activities to assign valuation steps to each position so that the resulting flows can be posted correctly. Define FX rate valuation procedures for forward exchange transactions that determine the write-up/write-down rules, rate types, forward category, and other relevant settings.
questions.question:
For the rate valuation procedures of FX transactions you can define different settings for your position management procedures. Within SAP Standard some examples are being given. Is it necessary to change the exisiting procedures ? If yes, please specify the different requirements, such as:
- NPV type
- Write-Up / Write-Down rule
- Gain/Loss handling
- Rate Types (e.g. for spot purchase/sale)
- Forward category
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition:
With this step you can define procedures for one-step valuation that determine write-ups/write-downs in the security and in the foreign currency in one step, depending on the total amount in local currency.
In this configuration activity, you define valuation steps that are executed when you change positions, transfer postings, or valuate key dates. Once you have defined each valuation step, you must make settings in the following configuration activities to assign valuation steps to each position so that the resulting flows can be posted correctly.
questions.question:
For the one-step valuation procedures to determine write-ups/write-downs you can define different settings for your position management procedures. Within SAP Standard some examples are being given. Is it necessary to change the exisiting procedures ? If yes, please specify the different requirements, such as:
- NPV category
- NPV type
- Gain/Loss handling
- Rate Types
- Write-Up/-Down Rule
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition: In this configuration activity, you define valuation steps that are executed when you change positions, transfer postings, or valuate key dates. Once you have defined each valuation step, you must make settings in the following configuration activities to assign valuation steps to each position so that the resulting flows can be posted correctly. Define procedures for the security valuation to determine gains and losses due to rate changes.
questions.question:
For the security valuation procedures you can define different settings for your position management procedures. Within SAP Standard some examples are being given. Is it necessary to change the exisiting procedures ? If yes, please specify the different requirements, such as:
- NPV category
- NPV type
- Gain/Loss handling
- Rate Types
- Write-Up/-Down Rule
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition: In this configuration activity, you define valuation steps that are executed when you change positions, transfer postings, or valuate key dates. Once you have defined each valuation step, you must make settings in the following configuration activities to assign valuation steps to each position so that the resulting flows can be posted correctly. Define foreign exchange valuation procedures that determine the gains and losses resulting from changes in the FX rate.
questions.question:
For the foreign currency valuation procedures you can define different settings for your position management procedures. Within SAP Standard some examples are being given. Is it necessary to change the exisiting procedures ? If yes, please specify the different requirements, such as:
- Component for valuation
- Gain/Loss handling
- Rate Type
- Write-Up/-Down Rule
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step you specify for single positions (securities) which consumption sequence procedure you want to use to determine the positions to be sold.
You can choose between the following consumption sequence procedures:

LIFO = Last In First Out; here, the position bought last is sold first.
FIFO = First In First Out; here, the position bought first is sold first.
Manual assignment; here, for every sale, a dialog box is displayed where you specify which positions you want to sell. You also have the option of distributing the sale to different single positions.
questions.question:
Is it a requirement to capture single positions in the area of securities (Lot Accounting) ? If yes, please specify information like:
- Company codes
- Consumption sequence (e.g. manual, FIFO, LIFO, etc.)
- Defaul for manual consumption sequence
- Valuation area
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define valuation steps that are executed when you change positions, transfer postings, or valuate key dates. Once you have defined each valuation step, you must make settings in the following configuration activities to assign valuation steps to each position so that the resulting flows can be posted correctly. Define valuation procedures for the valuation category Amortization that distribute the premium or discount (the difference between payment and repayment amounts) over the term.
The valuation category is relevant for the position management categories Securities/Loans/Money Market Transactions/Listed Options, Normal Style (Without Index-Linked Bonds), Securities/Loans with Installment Repayment (Without Index-Linked Bonds), and Index-linked Bonds.
questions.question:
For the amortization procedures you can define different settings for your position management procedures. Within SAP Standard some examples are being given. Is it necessary to change the exisiting procedures ? If yes, please specify the different requirements, such as:
- Calculation category (e.g. SAC, LAC)
- Gross/Net
- Rate Type
- Amortization to ... (e.g. End of Term, End of Fixed Period etc.)
- Reset
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition: Within this step you can define differentiations for treasury positions. The treasury position (or subledger position) is the most detailed level into which you can break down the balance sheet accounts of the Treasury and Risk Management subledger (TRL). On the positions level, the key date valuations are made, and the position components are managed. The differentiation terms of the different product groups delimit the positions. Some differentiation terms are predefined by the system for each product group, but there are additional differentiation terms that you can also select.
questions.question: Is it required to differentiate the treasury positions on specific differentiation criteria like portfolio, functional area, profit center, etc. (please see the SAP Help page for more detailed information) ? If yes, please define the differentiation criteria and explain which valuation area and accounting code needs to be assigned to the predefined differentiation criteria. Is a single position management required ? If yes, which product types assignment is necessary ? Is it required to capture external lots ? If yes, please specify the company codes.

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this configuration step you can define up to five custom differentiation terms and then enter the corresponding values for each new custom differentiation term.
Under Define and Assign Differentiations, you can then define and assign a differentiation using these custom differentiation terms.
The custom differentiation terms that are used in a differentiation must be entered in the financial transaction data on the Administration tab.
questions.question: Is it required to define custom differentiation terms, which can be entered in the financial transaction data on the administration tab ? If yes, please specify up to five custom differentiations and define the corresponding values for each.

questions.topicDefinition:
This step helps you to specify whether the derived business transactions are processed online or offline, and which status they should have when they were created.
Make the following settings concerning the derived business transactions. For each accounting code or valuation area, you can make different settings for the derived business transactions. You can also make a general setting relevant for all accounting and valuation area combinations without a specific setting.
questions.question: Shall the derived business transactions be updated immediately every time a business transaction leads to a change in position ? Note: If there is a large amount of data, it can be useful to update it via a batch job. Shall these derived business transactions always have the same status as the original business transaction ? If an immediat update is required, please specify a reversal reason, which the system can automatically use if a business transaction has been reversed (e.g. 01 processing error).

questions.topicDefinition:
This activity allows you to define corporate action types for the corporate action categories that are predefined in the system.
Using the corporate action types, you can specify additional evaluation groups to classify corporate actions.
You can, for example, assign posting authorizations depending on the corporate action type.
questions.question: Is it required to capture corporate actions like stock split, stock swap etc. within the securities area ? If yes, please specify if the predefined content is sufficient or needs to be changed/enhanced.

questions.topicDefinition:
[Note: This configuration activity is preconfigured. You can adjust the settings to suit your requirements]. This configuration helps you to check and define the rules that govern how the position management procedures are assigned to treasury positions.
You control the assignment of position management procedures* using the parameters accounting code, valuation area, valuation class, product category, product type, transaction type, and portfolio.
You can work with initial entries, that is, you could choose a position management procedure for valuation class 21 without specifying the other factors. The selected position management procedure is then assigned to all positions with valuation class 21 unless there are other suitable entries for which the remaining factors to the right in the assignment table are specified.

The general determination algorithm works as follows:

1. For a position specified by accounting code, valuation area, valuation class, product category, product type, transaction type, and portfolio, all records in the assignment table are determined that are compatible with the specific position.
2. The most suitable entry is chosen.
questions.question:
Which position management procedure shall be assigned to which combination of:
- Accounting code
- Valuation area
- Valuation class
- Product category
- Product type
- Transaction type
- Portfolio
- Securities account group

Note: Not all of the entries mentioned above need to be defined (more detailed information are considered before general information).

questions.topicDefinition:
This activity allows you to assign the individual securities accounts to securities account groups when you define the securities accounts using the Manage Securities Accounts app. Define the securities account groups you require for each company code.
For securities positions, you can select the securities account group as a differentiation criterion under Define and Assign Differentiations* so that the key date valuation occurs at the level of the securities account groups.
questions.question: Is it required to assign individual securities accounts into specific groups ? If so, please specify the groups.

questions.topicDefinition: [Predefined content is available]. This activity allows you to define reasons for reversing documents and assign them to the corresponding FI reason. You can enter these reasons when reversing documents.
questions.question: Is it required to enhance/maintain the predefined reversal reasons for reversing documents ? If so, please define the short/long name, and specify the FI reversal reason.

questions.topicDefinition:
This activitiy gives you the possibility to exclude product groups, product categories, and product types from the transfer to the parallel valuation areas.

The following options are available:

- Exclude certain product groups, product categories, and product types from the transfer to all parallel valuation areas
- Exclude certain product groups, product categories, and product types from the transfer to specific valuation areas
- Exclude certain product groups, product categories, and product types from processing in specific accounting codes (across all valuation areas or for given valuation areas).
questions.question: Is it required, that specific product groups, product categories or product types shall be excluded from the transfer to the parallel valuation areas ? If so, please specify the products.

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step you can assign additional account assignments to the treasury positions (position indicator) depending on the company code and account assignment reference. The values are then also transferred to the accounting document.

These settings are checked during the creation process of the treasury positions after the creation of the financial transaction. The values of the additional account assignments are assigned to the treasury positions and are then also transferred to the accounting document.
questions.question: Is it required to assign additional account assignments to the treasury positions (position indicator) to transfer the values to the acccounting document ? If so, please specify and refer to company code, account assignment reference, cost center, and functional area if required.

questions.topicDefinition: Within this configuration step you can check the assignment of accounting codes and valuation areas and the specific settings made for the combinations of accounting codes and valuation areas. You can change some of these settings only if no financial transactions are available in the company code.
questions.question: Your predefined valuation areas (e.g. IFRS, local GAAP, etc.) and accounting codes, in which combinations shall they be assigned  ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have defined the chart of accounts and all the required accounts in Financial Accounting. You have defined all account assignment references under step Define Account Assignment References. Under Define Account Symbols configuration activity, you define abstract account symbols. You defined your update types. You indicated the update types as relevant for posting]. Within this activity you define the account determination settings for the flows in the parallel valuation areas. The account determination settings define the accounts to be used when the flows are posted to Financial Accounting. The system only posts flows in the parallel valuation areas if an update type is set as relevant for posting under Indicate Update Types as Relevant to Posting and if posting specifications have been defined for the corresponding update types in this configuration activity.

You can define different account determination settings for an update type, depending on the valuation area. You could, for example, assign posting specifications to an update type in valuation area 002 that differ from the posting specifications for the same update type in valuation area 003. Alternatively, you could use the same posting specifications, but assign different G/L accounts to a account symbol for each valuation area.
questions.question: How shall the predefined information, like account assignment references, account symbols, and update types be defined for the flows in the parallel valuation areas ? Please specify the accounts to be used when the flows are posted to FI.

questions.topicDefinition: For each combination of company code, product type, and transaction type, assign a general valuation class for use as a default value when you create a financial transaction.A general valuation class must be assigned to every financial transaction from which the special valuation classes of different valuation areas can be derived.
questions.question: For the securities area, is it required to have a default GVC value when you create a financial transaction ? If so, please specify the GVC for the relevant product and transaction type combination and company code.

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define the account assignment references that you require. Account assignment references are required for each treasury position. You use the account assignment references to determine the G/L account in FI in which the relevant position is to be posted. You assign the G/L accounts to the account references in the configuration activity Assign G/L Accounts to Account Symbols.  You can use the account assignment references to control the posting of the treasury positions in the general ledger. You do this by making the assignment of G/L accounts in FI dependent on the account assignment reference for each account symbol (position and interest/dividend revenue).

You create the account assignment references independent of the valuation areas. You can assign the account assignment references to positions valuation area-dependent and/or you control the account determination per valuation area and account assignment reference.
questions.question: Which account assignment references are required for the determination of G/L accounts in FI ? Is it required to create account assignment references independent of the valuation areas ?

questions.topicDefinition: [The configuration activity is preconfigured. You can adapt the settings to your needs by changing the assignment of the general valuation classes to the groups]. Within this activity you can display and change the assignment of general valuation classes to predefined groups. The groups are allocated per company code, product type, and/or transaction type. When you use the input help for assigning general valuation classes, the system displays only the general valuation classes of the group that are relevant for the specific kind of financial transaction.
questions.question: Besides the preconfigured content of GVC groups, is it required to maintain/extend/create additional groups for the different GVCs ? If so, please specify how such a grouping shall be defined and additionally refer to the relevant products which shall be assigned.

questions.topicDefinition: [This configuration activity is preconfigured. You can adapt the settings to your needs]. Within this step you can define general valuation classes (GVC) and assign them to valuation-area-dependent special valuation classes. You can display and define general valuation classes (GVCs). On an abstract level, the general valuation classes allow the trader in the front office to group the positions. In addition, you assign for each valuation area the valuation-area-dependent special valuation classes to the general valuation classes.
questions.question: In terms of GVCs there is already a predefined SAP content for grouping of positions. Is it required to maintain/extend the predefined content ? If so, please specify the differentiation criteria for GVCs. Additionally please define, if a maintenance/extension for (special) VC is required for the parallel valuation areas ? If so, please specify for which valuation areas, which GVCs and which VCs shall be maintained.

questions.topicDefinition: [Some account symbols are preconfigured. Please use them as a reference]. Within this configuration you define account symbols with posting categories that determine the type of posting and the posting currency (semantics of the account symbol).In this step, you can display or change existing account symbols or define new account symbols.
questions.question: For the definition of posting specifications account symbols with posting categories are used. Which account symbols are required and what posting category (e.g. position posting, subledger posting etc.) shall be applied for each account symbol ?

questions.topicDefinition: For each combination of company code, product type, and transaction type, assign a general valuation class for use as a default value when you create a financial transaction.A general valuation class must be assigned to every financial transaction from which the special valuation classes of different valuation areas can be derived.
questions.question: For the money market area, is it required to have a default GVC value when you create a financial transaction ? If so, please specify the GVC for the relevant product and transaction type combination and company code.

questions.topicDefinition: For each combination of company code, product type, and transaction type, assign a general valuation class for use as a default value when you create a financial transaction.A general valuation class must be assigned to every financial transaction from which the special valuation classes of different valuation areas can be derived.
questions.question: For the OTC derivatives, is it required to have a default GVC value when you create a financial transaction ? If so, please specify the GVC for the relevant product and transaction type combination and company code.

questions.topicDefinition: For each combination of company code, product type, and transaction type, assign a general valuation class for use as a default value when you create a financial transaction.A general valuation class must be assigned to every financial transaction from which the special valuation classes of different valuation areas can be derived.
questions.question: For the FX area, is it required to have a default GVC value when you create a financial transaction ? If so, please specify the GVC for the relevant product and transaction type combination and company code.

questions.topicDefinition: This configuration step allows you to determine which product types in which valuation area and accounting code are to be excluded from the Financial Accounting update. If you set this indicator, flows for this product type in the specified accounting code and valuation area are not included in the Financial Accounting update. These flows are displayed in the subledger rather than in the Display Treasury Posting Journal app.
questions.question: It it required to exclude specific product types from the FI update ? If so, please specify the products and refer to the valuation area and accounting code if required.

questions.topicDefinition: Within this configuration you can assign a general valuation class depending on the company code, product type, and transaction type. This assignment is used as a default value when you enter a financial transaction. A general valuation class must be assigned to every financial transaction from which the special valuation classes of different valuation areas can be derived.
questions.question: For the Trade Finance transactions, is it required to have a default GVC value when you create a financial transaction ? If so, please specify the GVC for the relevant product and transaction type combination and company code.

questions.topicDefinition:
This activity settings helps you to define correspondence activities for different recipients for securities transactions.
You assign each correspondence function code to a product type for an activity and also for a recipient type. This activity acts as one of the prerequisites for correspondence object creation for the securities contract type. The correspondence object is created for a financial transaction, based on the correspondence class and recipient assigned for that product type, and for the transaction type for an activity.
questions.question: With regards to the securities correspondence, which correspondence shall be created at which status activity and to whom (internal or external recipients or both) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this step you define internal recipients for correspondence.
Enter a key and a descriptive name for each recipient.
questions.question: How many internal recipients shall receive correspondence (e.g. Back-Office) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration activity is relevant for the receipt of correspondences from your counterparties via SWIFT messages. You need to assign format mappings as a function of message type, sender ID, and the SWIFT formats MT300 (for FX transactions and FX options) and MT320 (for MM transactions).
The format mapping is needed to transfer the data from the MBC file to a correspondence object.
Standard Settings:  You can use the predefined format mappings TRM_MT300 and TRM_MT320. You can define your own format mappings using the configuration activity Map Treasury Correspondence Format Data.
questions.question: Are you planning to use SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity as a basis to embed SWIFT integration ? If yes, which MT formats (e.g. MT300) are you expecting for the inbound process for format mappings from MBC ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration allows you to assign format mappings for outgoing formats (such as MT300 and MT320) as a function of business partner group and country/region.
This configuration activity is relevant for sending correspondences to your counterparties via SWIFT messages. You need to assign format mappings for the SWIFT formats MT300 (for FX transactions and FX options) and MT320 (for MM transactions) as a function of business partner group and country/region.
The format mapping is needed to transfer the data from the correspondence object to an MBC file.
questions.question: Are you planning to use SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity as a basis to embed SWIFT integration ? If yes, which MT formats (e.g. MT300) shall be created and sent out to which counterparts (here Business Partner Groups) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
With this activity you set attributes to control the outgoing and incoming correspondence process per business partner group, correspondence class, and recipient/sender type.
Here you can make the required settings for business partner groups.
You assign the following business attributes to a combination of the business partner group, correspondence class, and recipient/sender type:
Set the Automatic Correspondence indicator if it is required.
If the correspondence object is status-relevant for the financial transaction, set this indicator.
Set the Counterconfirmation indicator from the counterparty if it is required.
Set the Automatic Completion indicator if it is required.
Set the Get Values from Counterconfirmation indicator if the information about external reference and contact person in the financial transaction has to be updated with the information received in a status-relevant incoming correspondence and Auto-Matching Outgoing Correspondence.
questions.question: Shall the correspondence be send out automatically (with regards to a certain activity status, like "contract") ? Is there a release workflow or release step required ? Do you want to track the current status of the correspondence ? Do you expect a counterconfirmation from the counterpart ? Is a reconciliation of the correspondence date required ? Shall correspondence objects automatically be marked as status completed, once the process is finalized ? Shall specific information from the counterconfirmation (like external trade ID, reference, etc.) be updated within the system ? Is a confirmation of physical delivery for incoming correspondence necessary ? For outgoing correspondence objects, is an automatic search for incoming required ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this activity step you can define business partner groups used to control the correspondence process in the Assign Attributes for Business Partner Groups app.
Here you can make the required settings for the business partner group, which defines the business settings for correspondence. These settings are used to differentiate business attributes, such as counterconfirmation requirement and matching requirement, from technical attributes.
You assign the business partner group to the business partner in the Assign Profile and BP Group, External Recipients and Assign Profile and BP Group, Internal Recipients apps.
questions.question: How many different groups of Business Partners would you like to send correspondence (like confirmations, dealer slips, SWIFT files) to ?

questions.topicDefinition: With this activity you can define the rules for mapping or transforming data to enable communication with your financial institution in the required data format. You can create new format mappings or copy from existing ones, display the details of your existing format mapping, as well as import, export, edit, check, delete, and release these mappings.
questions.question: Are there any customer specific requirements with regards to the mapping of correspondence objects with the financial institution, besides the SAP Standard mapping (e.g. MT300, MT320, etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Here you can define correspondence activities for different recipients for foreign exchange transactions.
You assign each correspondence function code to a product type for an activity and also for a recipient type. This activity acts as one of the prerequisites for correspondence object creation for foreign exchange contract type. The correspondence object is created for a financial transaction, based on the correspondence class and recipient assigned for that product type, and for the transaction type for an activity.
questions.question: With regards to the FX correspondence, which correspondence shall be created at which status activity and to whom (internal or external recipients or both) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Here you can define correspondence activities for different recipients for money market transactions.
You assign each correspondence function code to a product type for an activity and also for a recipient type. This activity acts as one of the prerequisites for correspondence object creation for foreign exchange contract type. The correspondence object is created for a financial transaction, based on the correspondence class and recipient assigned for that product type, and for the transaction type for an activity.
questions.question: With regards to the Money Market correspondence, which correspondence shall be created at which status activity and to whom (internal or external recipients or both) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define the recipient/sender types for correspondence objects and select the option Internal for internal recipients, if needed.
The following are some examples of recipient or sender types:
COUNTERPARTY: Counterparty
DEPOSITORYBANK: Depository Bank
GLOBALCUSTODIAN: Global Custodian
GUARANTOR: Guarantor
INTERNAL: Internal
ISSUER: Issuer
questions.question: How many different recipients and senders of correspondence are required (internal and external) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Here you can define correspondence activities for different recipients for derivative transactions.
You assign each correspondence function code to a product type for an activity and also for a recipient type. This activity acts as one of the prerequisites for correspondence object creation for foreign exchange contract type. The correspondence object is created for a financial transaction, based on the correspondence class and recipient assigned for that product type, and for the transaction type for an activity.
questions.question: With regards to the derivative correspondence, which correspondence shall be created at which status activity and to whom (internal or external recipients or both) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this step to enter various descriptors for the date attributes in Exposure Management.
Date attribute DH01 is available in the header data of the raw exposure, whereas attribute DI01 is available in the line items of the raw exposures.
Note:
In the Define Substitution Rules for Exposure Position Fields configuration app, you can define substitution rules using these fields.
questions.question: Which types of exposures are required ? Which descriptors for the date attribues shall be applied for Exposure Management ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this step to enter various descriptors for the long attributes in Exposure Management.
The long attribute LH01 is available in the header data of the raw exposure, whereas attributes LI01 - LI04 are available in the line items of the raw exposures.
Note:
In the Define Substitution Rules for Exposure Position Fields configuration app, you can define substitution rules using these fields.
questions.question: Which types of exposures are required ? Which descriptors for the long attribues shall be applied for Exposure Management ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this step to enter various descriptors for the medium-length attributes in Exposure Management.
The medium attributes MI01 and MI02 are available in the line items of the raw exposures.
Note:
In the Define Substitution Rules for Exposure Position Fields configuration app, you can define substitution rules using these fields.
questions.question: Which types of exposures are required ? Which descriptors for the medium-length attribues shall be applied for Exposure Management ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this configuration step you can decide on the differentiation criteria that are relevant for your exposure positions. For the automatic matching process, you determine the matching exposure position type.
Differentiation Criteria of Exposure Positions:
Company Code
Risk Category
Transaction Type of the Raw Exposure
Currency of the Exposure Amount
Target Currency
Exposure Position Type
Product Type

Differentiation Criteria that can be deactivated under certain circumstances:
Raw Exposure ID
Raw Exposure Line Item ID
Planning Period
Planning Year

Additional Optional Differentiation Criteria:
Country/Region Key
Profit Center
Exposure Date
Transaction Activity
Free Attributes
questions.question: Which different kinds of exposures are you intending to report ? What differentiation criteria are relevant for your exposure positions (e.g. Company Code, Currencies, Products etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this step you can configure your exposure activity types. The exposure activity type is a required entry when you create a raw exposure.
The sub raw exposures are created for a raw exposure in accordance with what you enter here
questions.question: With regards to your defined exposures, is there a manual release step required ? If yes, please define for which of the defined exposures.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this step to enter various descriptors for the short attributes in Exposure Management.
The short attributes SH01 and SH02 are available in the header data of the raw exposure, whereas attribute SI01 is available in the line items of the raw exposures.
Note: In the predefined configuration, the predefined exposure position type YFX is assigned based on the condition that the short attribute SH01 is set to FX - FX Exposure.
In the Define Substitution Rules for Exposure Position Fields configuration app, you can define substitution rules using these fields.
questions.question: Which descriptors for the short attributes shall be applied for Exposure Management ? Is it required to change/enhance the predefined configuration ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration step you define which product types are considered for exposures. These product types must be attached to exposure position types.
The product type of the exposure positions is needed for the integration of the exposure positions (as operating exposures) in the Risk Analyzer.
questions.question: How many different exposures do you want to report ? What naming conventions (e.g. Product Type Key, Short Text, Long Text) shall theses exposures have ?

questions.topicDefinition: The following sections describe the tools for transferring market data. Market data can be transferred to the system from a file interface or via realtime datafeed. You can use the function for market data transfer from spreadsheets. In addition to the back end functions, you can also use the SAP Fiori launchpad to access the Import Market Dataapp for the data transfer, and other apps for the manual entry.
questions.question: Are you planning to import market data to the system ? How shall these market data be imported (e.g. file interface, datafeed, etc.) ? Which market data provider are you planning to use for which kind of data ? What market data are you planning to import ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration step you can define correlation types. Correlation types are used for evaluations in variance/covariance approach of value-at-risk calculations.
You enter the actual values (correlations) in the market data or scenario data and assign correlation types within the evaluation types.
questions.question: Is it intended to calculate VaR or CFaR within the TRM module ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step you can create volatility types for volatilities. Volatilities are used in the NPV calculation of options and value-at-risk calculations.
Based on market data or scenario data, you enter the actual volatility values in the application. You assign volatility types within the valuation types.
Example:
A volatility curve for the interest rate for the relevant term and that is appropriate for the cap must be assigned to a dollar cap (for example, 6-M-LIBOR).
questions.question: Are you planning to capture volatilities within the TRM module (e.g. for NPV calculation of options and VaR caluclations or FX volatilities) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This activity allows you to define statistic types that determine how the volatilities and correlations within a volatility or correlation type are calculated and interpreted during the value-at-risk calculation.
Assign the statistic type to the volatility types and correlation types.
questions.question: How do you plan to calculate and interprete the volatilities and correlations within a volatility for the VaR/CFaR calculation ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[As a prerequisite, you need to have defined credit spread IDs in the  activity Define Credit Spread IDs]. Within this configuration you define credit spread curve structures using attributes to influence market data selection and assign credit spread IDs to define the term structure of the curve.
In combination with a reference entity, a credit spread curve structure describes a concrete credit spread curve. In this way, credit spread curve structures can be assigned to reference entities.
questions.question: For the credit spread curve structure, which credit default swaps (CDS) shall be assigned ? For these CDS, what terms are required (e.g. 6 months / 1 year etc.) ? What quotation type (e.g. Middle, Bid, Ask) shall be taken ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration is for the set up of credit spread IDs by configuring their attributes.
Defining credit spread IDs is a prerequisite for the following functions:
Entering credit spread market data into the system
Constructing credit spread curve structures out of credit spreads with different times to maturity
Dependencies
The credit spread ID defines general properties of a credit spread.

To store market data, you also need to specify the reference entity (such as your business partner) to which a spread refers. To this end, you need to define reference entities. You can use credit spread curves in the price calculator.
questions.question: Which credit default swaps (CDS) are required ? For these CDS, what terms are required (e.g. 6 months / 1 year etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have already created a swap rate curve structure under Define Swap Rate Curve Structures]. Via this activity you have the possibility to assign swap rate curve structures to currency pairs.
You can assign a curve structure to multiple currency pairs by using initial entries, that is, you enter only the swap rate curve structure without specifying the other factors. The specific swap rate curve structure is then relevant to all currency pairs unless there are other suitable entries for which the remaining from-currency and/or to-currency are specified.
questions.question: Is it planned or required to have specific swap rate curve structures for specific currency pairs ?

questions.topicDefinition:
With this configuration you can define swap rate curve structures using attributes to influence market data selection. Furthermore, you define the term structure of the curve.
In combination with a currency pair and an exchange rate type, a swap rate curve structure describes a concrete swap rate spread curve. In this way, swap rate curve structures can be assigned to currency pairs.
For swap market data to be selected to build a concrete curve, the exchange rate type is also required. During the evaluation, the exchange rate type is taken either from the evaluation type settings or from the settings on the level of the valuation rule.
questions.question: For the definition of swap rate curve structures, which Extrapolationmethod shall be taken (constant or linear) ? What term structure in days (e.g. 1 / 7 / 90 / 180 etc.) is necessary ? Is there a need to have more than one swap rate curve structure available ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration step allows you to define price indexes.
Price indexes are required for the Index Valuation valuation step during the key date valuation as well as for the accrual/deferral of interest for certain money market product types related to the price index. Usually, these kind of product types are needed in countries/regions with high inflation.
You can enter the values of the price indexes using the Enter Price Index Values app on SAP Fiori launchpad.
questions.question: Is it a requirement to capture Index Valuations (e.g. for high inflation countries) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
