[Prerequisites: Ask your datafeed provider which data source the external partner program supports]. This configuration step allows you to define data sources that can be accessed from the system.
In this step you define all the data sources used by your external partner program that you want to access from the SAP system.
questions.question: Which datafeed provider are you intending to use ? Do you have different datafeed providers (e.g. for different sources, like Treasury and Cash Management) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this acitivity step you define additional indices for security class data so that you can enter additional identifiers for securities.

Example
If you want to use an internal number and, for example, the ISIN International Securities ID Number in addition to the security class ID number, you can define these indices as secondary indices.
You enter the secondary indices in the security class data on the Search Terms tab in the Secondary Indices table.
questions.question: Is it required to have more than one indice within the security class data (e.g. ISIN, WKN, Euroclear etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: Countries/regions, currencies and calendars are predefined in system. But you can Maintain Calendars under Application Platform and Infrastructure -> General Settings -> Basic Settings]. This configuration step allows you to define the exchanges, where you buy your securities, and enter the important parameters and information for each exchange.
questions.question: What exchanges are relevant for your securities ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This setting allows you to define reference interest rates with attributes such as payment frequency, currency, interest calculation method, yield curve type for forward calculation, working day shift, and maturity at month end.
In this activity, you set up reference interest rates by configuring their attributes. You enter the concrete values of the reference interest rates under Enter Interest Rates.
Reference interest rates are relevant for different functions. For example, they are needed for net present value calculation and for the definition of interest conditions of special financial transactions. In this configuration activity, you enter the master data for reference interest rates. You enter the specific values of the reference interest rates using the different apps available on the SAP Fiori launchpad.
questions.question: Which reference interest rates are intended to be used within TRM ? Is there a list of reference interest rates with property information, like currency, quotation type, term etc. available ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have defined reference interest rates in the configuration activity Define Reference Interest Rates]. In this configuration activity, you define yield curve types (YC types). Define your yield curve types using attributes influencing market data selection and interest calculations.
You define yield curve types using attributes influencing market data selection and interest calculations and using as many currencies as necessary. You then assign the reference interest rates.
questions.question: Which yield curves are relevant for your day to day operations (e.g. discounting-, forward curves etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisite: You need to have defined basis spread IDs under Define Basis Spreads]. In this activity you define basis spread curve types using attributes influencing market data selection and as many currency/tenor pairs as you require. In addition, you must assign basis spread IDs to them.
Standard Settings
SAP delivers predefined settings for this configuration activity. You can change these settings according to your needs.
questions.question: Shall cross-currency / tenor spreads be used in your valuation procedure ? If yes, for which currencies and tenors shall respective basis spread curves be maintained ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration setp you set up basis spreads by configuring their attributes. You can maintain tenor spreads as well as cross-currency spreads.
Defining basis spreads is a prerequisite for the following:
Uploading spread market data into the system
Constructing spread curves out of basis spreads with different times to maturity
Standard Settings
SAP delivers predefined settings for this configuration activity. You can change these settings according to your needs.
questions.question: For the definition of the basis spread, which currency pairs and terms are required ? Which cross-currency and tenor spreads shall be maintained ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: Default risk rules must be defined in the Define Default Risk Rules configuration activity]. Assign default risk rules to product categories, or to a combination of product category and application, for the automatic derivation of the default risk data of financial objects.
The default risk rules are the central control instances for valuing default risks arising from transactions.
questions.question: The predefined risk rules, for which product categories or application shall they be used or assigned ?

questions.topicDefinition: This configuration activity allows you to define and change value-at-risk types that are used to control the calculation of the value at risk.
questions.question: What types of VaR are required for VaR calculation (e.g. Historical Simulation, Structurized Monte Carlo, Box Muller or Bootstrapping) ?

questions.topicDefinition: Via this activity you can choose the evaluation type and the CVA/DVA type relevant for Limit Management.
questions.question: Which CVA and DVA evaluation type shall be maintained as a default setting for Limit Management ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: Limit product groups must be defined in the Define Limit Product Groups configuration activity]. Within this activity you assign limit product groups to product categories for the automatic derivation of the default risk data of financial objects.
The limit product group is a basic setting of Limit Management.
questions.question: The predefined limit product groups, to which product categories shall they be assigned (e.g. product category 510 Fixed-Term Deposit & 550 Interest Rate Instrument to LPG: Money Market) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Via this configuration you define basic settings for Limit Management.
By specifying the exchange rate type, you define which exchange rate is to be used in Limit Management. If you do not specify an exchange rate type, then the system uses the default type, which is M (middle).
questions.question: Is it necessary to specify a different exchange rate type then SAP Standard default type M (middle) ? If so, please specify.

questions.topicDefinition: This activity activates the integrated default risk limit check for applications and company codes.
questions.question: For which applications shall the integrated default risk limit check be activated (FX, MM, Derivatives etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration item allows you to define limit types and assign limit characteristics to the limit types.
The limit type is used to find the determination procedure for limit utilizations, the business partner relationship category, and to determine the extent of evaluations.
Limit characteristics form the basis for deciding whether a transaction is to be attributed to a particular limit type.

Example:
You define a four-dimensional limit type with the limit characteristics Business Partner, Limit Product Group, Trader, and Company Code, and then assign the determination procedure Procedure for Credit Risk Exposure to this limit type.
questions.question: In your day to day operations in limit management, what kind of limits do you plan to report (e.g. external counterparty - Business Partners) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
With this activity you can define limit product groups. Using limit product groups, you can group different product and transaction types to update the default risks of these transactions together.
You assign the product and transaction types to a limit product group in the configuration activities used to define transaction types.

Example:
You define the limit product group 'MM' for money market transactions, and assign product type 51A (fixed-term deposit) and transaction type 100 (investment) to the limit product group 'MM'.
questions.question: For the separation of products into specific limit product groups, how and on which granularity level shall these products be grouped (e.g. MM, FX, etc.) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration you can define the procedures for determining limit utilizations. You use these procedures to control the data, calculation rules, and risk categories that are to be used to generate limit utilizations.

Example
To value all financial transactions for all risk categories, you have to define two determination procedures:
1. Procedure for credit risk
2. Procedure for settlement risk

Standard Settings
Two determination procedures for credit risk are predefined:
10 CR - Max(0,NPV/Nom), Credit Risk - max(0,Nom) or Max(0, NPV)
20 CR - Nom/NPV, Credit Risk - Nominal or NPV

Recommendation
Choose a meaningful way of naming determination procedures (for example, the name could indicate the risk category and the general calculation rule).
questions.question: For limit utiliziations, which different procedures shall be applied (e.g. External and internal credit risk) ? Please additionally define which control parameters are relevant for these procedures (e.g. valuation factor, exposure, etc.).

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You need to have already entered the settings in the following configuration activities: Define Determination Procedures, Define Default Risk Rules]. With this configuration step you can define the attributable amount determination settings for a combination of the determination procedure and the default risk rule.

For example, the following values are assigned to the determination procedure 10 CR - Nom, Max(0,NPV) and to default risk rule MM001 Debt and Investment:

Formula ID: Max(0,CALCBAS)
Calculation basis = 1 Var1
Variable assignment ID: 101 Nominal amount


Predefined settings are available for this configuration activity.
questions.question: What determination procedure shall be applied for which default risk rule ? Please additionally define which formula determination shall be used with this assignment ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step you can define default risk rules that are the central control instances for the evaluation of default risks arising from financial transactions.
A default risk rule is assigned to each financial transaction in order to group transactions for business purposes. In the following activity, these 'groups' are valuated using standard methods. Default risk rules control the input parameters for attributable amount determination.

You make the following settings for the default risk rule:
Store date determination for calculating market value change periods for each default risk rule.
Store date determination for calculating the risk commitment period for each default risk rule.
You are also able to set an indicator to determine whether the system calculates settlement risk.
questions.question: Which different kinds of default risk rules shall be maintained for your relevant financial products and the resulting evaluation of default risks ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This step allows you to define variable assignment IDs. The variable assignment ID determines which values are taken from the data pool to fill variables in the formulas predefined in the system.

Predefined values are as followed:
Net Present Value
Nominal Amount
Advance Payment Amount
Return Payment Amount
Credit Value Adjustment
questions.question: Besides the variable assignment IDs from SAP Standard, are there any additional assignment IDs which are relevant for future scope ? Please also define, if more than one variable is required and if yes, which shall be used as variable 1 and variable 2 ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: If you require risk sensitivities other the ones delivered with the system, or if you want the valuation factor determination* to take place internally as well as externally, you need to have defined these sensitivities beforehand, and assigned a valuation factor determination using the default risk rule]. Within this configuration step you enter the relevant add-on factors for a combination of Market Value Change Period in Months and Risk Sensitivity.
An add-on factor is a percentage rate that, when multiplied by the calculation base of the transaction you want to value, results in the add-on. The add-on is a risk premium, which takes into account the potential positive market value changes of a transaction. It is a combination of the market value change period and risk sensitivity*.

Example
Transactions with a market value change period of 12 months and an 'interest-dependent' risk sensitivity should be valued with an add-on factor of 0.01%.
questions.question: For the already defined risk sensitivity type, what Add-On Factor in percent shall be applied ? Please also specify the market value change period in months if required.

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: You need to have already defined at least one default risk rule and a risk sensitivity]. Within this step you assign a risk sensitivity to the default risk rule.
questions.question: Which predefined risk sensitivity shall be assigned to which predefined default risk rules ? Please additionally explain which predefined valuation factor shall be taken ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this step you define risk sensitivities. The risk sensitivity describes the risk category in which single transactions are to be grouped.

Example:
Interest rate change risk
Exchange rate risk

Dependencies:
Risk sensitivities are used to assign add-on factors during attributable amount determination. To do this, you assign the risk sensitivities to the default risk rules and enter the add-on factors depending on the market value change period in months and the risk sensitivity.
questions.question: With regards to the assignment of add-on factors, are there specific financial products in which single transactions need to be grouped to a certain risk category ?

questions.topicDefinition: [Prerequisites: In the definition of the expected exposure type, you need to set the Use Add-Ons indicator so that the settings made here take effect]. Via this step you can enter the add-on factors for a combination of product type, product category, remaining term, and time unit.
questions.question: For which Product Categories (or Product Types) is an Add-On Factor for Expected Exposures required ? Please also refer to which remaining term this Add-On Factor is applicable for each product (e.g. 1 year = 1%; 5 years = 5%) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
[Prerequisites: You have defined expected exposure types in the configuration activity Define Expected Exposure Types]. With this activity step you can define credit and debit value adjustment types that control how the system calculates CVA and DVA.
CVA and DVA values are stored for each credit and debit value adjustment type.
questions.question: How shall the CVA and DVA be calculated ? Shall the Difference Method be used or shall it be based on Expected Exposures ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This system configuration allows you to define the expected exposure types that are used to control the calculation of expected exposures. Expected exposures are needed for the CVA/DVA calculation using the CVA/DVA Calculation Method 2: Based on Expected Exposures.

EE values are stored for each EE type.
questions.question: For the CVA/DVA calculation which Expected Exposure Calculation Method is required (Constant or Variable Exposure Approach, or Manual Entry) ? Which predefined Maturity Band shall be applied ? Shall Netting Groups be ignored ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration step you define the portfolio hierarchies that you use in Risk Management.
The portfolio hierarchy is a hierarchical structure for organizing characteristics. It influences how the results are displayed in an evaluation.
questions.question: In which aggregate level (e.g. company code and product type) shall financial transactions be stored ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you can change some settings for the yield curve types of the preconfigured evaluation types. Create evaluation types by copying a preconfigured evaluation type or change some settings for evaluation types that are required for the calculation of key figures, such as the net present value, for financial transactions/treasury positions.
When you open the apps that calculate key figures, you must choose an evaluation type.
questions.question: Is it necessary to change the preconfigured evaluation types settings for yield curve types ? Are there any specific settings required for NPV, Market Risk Key Figures, etc. ?

questions.topicDefinition:
If you want to enter target quotas for the hedge ratios in your hedging areas, you have to define target quota types. With regards to the quota types there are three different Target Quota Categories to use. The target quota category defines the kind of target quota.
The following target quota categories are available:
•Limit (A limit displayed in percentage, the target quota
•Band (A lower limit (lower quota) and an upper limit (upper quota) define a target quota band)
•Target Limit Within Band (A target limit (target quota) can be defined within a target quota band that is between a lower and an upper limit)
questions.question: Is it required to have all of the following target quota categories available (Limit, Band, Target Limit within Band) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
Within this activity you define the product types for exposure subitems created during the automatic designation process. Therefore you assign the relevant product types in the hedging area master data.
On the Main Data tab, you can enter the default product type for your exposure subitems.
On the Hedge Accounting II tab, you can replace this default product type by another product type for exposure subitems. This maybe useful if you want to differentiate the posting for the different kinds of hedging instruments.
questions.question: What key and which short and long text would you like to use for you exposure subitems ?

questions.topicDefinition:
In this activity, you define your hedging profiles, which cover all necessary settings for hedge accounting.
The hedging profile represents the hedging relationship scenario and contains additional settings to complete the settings for the hedge accounting process.
The hedging relationship scenario is a predefined system entity that contains information about the following:
Hedging relationship category
Hedged item category
Hedge accounting rule
Cardinality of the hedging relationship
Standard Settings

There are predefined hedging profiles available that you can use and adapt to your needs.
questions.question:
What types of hedging relationships are required ? Please specify and refer to the following settings:
- Scenario
- Test Plan Category (e.g. Effectiveness Testing)
- Prospective Effectiveness Method
- Calculation Type
- Skip Valuation at Contract Date
- Intrinsic Value
- Skip Designation
- etc.

questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration activity, you define your hedging classifications. The freely definable hedging classifications are used in the following way:
In the definition of your hedging areas (app Define Hedging Area), you assign the hedging classifications on the General Settings tab.
You can assign n hedging classifications to a hedging area.
A hedging classification that is active for hedge accounting can only be assigned to one hedging area that is relevant for hedge accounting.
Hedging classifications that are inactive for hedge accounting can be assigned to n hedging areas.
On the Hedge Accounting II tab, you can assign the hedging profiles as a function of the hedging classification.
You assign hedging classifications to your hedging instruments in the financial transaction data on the Administration tab.
If the hedging classification is active for hedge accounting, this information is relevant for the automated designation process. Using the data from the financial transaction including the hedging classification, the system can identify the relevant hedging area version and the relevant exposure item so that the hedged item, hedging instrument, hedging relationship, and the planned designation flows can be created according to your settings for the hedging area.
questions.question: Which hedging classifications are relevant for the management of your exposures (e.g. Forecast Exposure for a group or for a certain entity) ?

questions.topicDefinition:
This step allows you to define hedge accounting calculation types with which to control the creation of the hypothetical derivative, the decomposition of the market rate components, and the creation of the market value components.
In the Define Hedging Profiles configuration activity, you assign the hedge accounting calculation types to hedging profiles relevant for the scenarios of the Hedge Management and Accounting of Net Open Exposures process.
questions.question:
For the evaluation of the derivative for Hedge Accounting, which parameters are relevant for the calculation ? Please refer to the following parameters: 
- From currency (e.g. following, leading, traded currency)
- Spot rate used (e.g. default, financial transaction, or market data table)
- NPV calculation (with or without CVA/DVA)
- Elements (discounted/undiscounted) and the sign of elements (absolute amount or consider sign)
-  Market Value Component Calculation (complete vs. simple)
- Hypothetical Derivative Forward Rate (e.g. Yield curve, swap rate, etc.)
- Hypothetical Derivative Fixing (e.g. None, from NDFs only, from FX and NDFs)

questions.topicDefinition: Define one or more prioritization profiles, which would then be assigned to a particular notification type and plant. Each prioritization profile would then reference a consequence category group so that the system can display a list of prioritized consequences, with a likelihood for each consequence.  This is used in conjunction with the configuration to define the consequence categories, consequences, and likelihoods.
questions.question:
There are multiple steps to perform in this configuration.  The goal is to define a list of prioritization profiles.  When we define a prioritization profile, it contains a reference to the consequence category group, notification type, and plant, such that when a priority assessment is triggered for a notification at a plant, the system searches for a matching profile.

For each prioritization profile, we also associate a consequence category group, which contains a set of consequence categories (defined in SSCUI 103793) within it.

For each of the consequence categories in the group, we can assign a UI position such that the consequence categories will appear on the UI in the sequence that is defined here.

Finally we assign a priority to each of the consequences and likelihoods that are possible.

questions.topic: Define Consequences Categories, Consequences, and Likelihoods
questions.topicDefinition:
Event prioritization enables you to assess priorities based on consequence categories, consequences, and likelihoods. When you select consequences and likelihoods while creating a maintenance request, the system calculates and suggests the applicable priority for the maintenance request. This will provide contextual information to the screener.

For example, if oil is dripping from a pump in a plant, you can create a maintenance request for the technical object. Using prioritization, you can specify that it is a high priority equipment which is responsible for core drilling tasks and, if it is not repaired within two weeks, it could lead to total asset damage. Based on these details, the system suggests ‘Very High’ as the priority. This activity is maintained as a configuration step.
questions.question:
There are multiple steps to perform in this configuration.  The first step is to define the consequence categories.  There are four categories pre-configured (People, Asset, Environment, Reputation) in the system.  If additional categories are required, a new entry can be created.

The second step is to define the consequences that will be assigned to each of the consequence categories.  Again, there are pre-configured consequences assigned to each of the pre-configured consequence categories, but additional entries can be created.

The third step is to define the different ranges of likelihoods that these occurrences could happen.

questions.configRef: Assign Material Shortage Profile to Users
questions.topicDefinition: This app allows you to assign material shortage profiles to users. This controls which material shortage definitions the user can choose from in the SAP Fiori Apps for Material Requirements Planning.

questions.topicDefinition: Material shortage definitions specify the rules for the supply and demand calculations. Material shortage profiles consist of one or more material shortage definitions.
questions.question: How many days out in the future do you want to include into the supply and demand calculation?

questions.topicDefinition: The control key determines the behavior of the operation by identifying the business functions that are applicable to the operation.
questions.question:
Should the operation be scheduled?

Is capacity planning applicable to this operation?

Are inspection characteristics required at this operation?

Should an automatic goods receipt be performed at this operation?

Is the operation used for rework?

Should costing be taken into account for this operation?

How should this operation be confirmed?

Is this an operation that is performed externally?

questions.topicDefinition: This configuration screen allows you to define any formula calculations that may be required to help with capacity planning, scheduling, or costing.
questions.question: Is there a need to take multiple fields into account (for example, setup time, machine time, labor time, etc.) when coming up with a calculation for planning, scheduling, or costing?  If so, mathematical operators can be used to define a formula taking different fields into consideration into the calculation.

questions.topicDefinition: Standard value key allows you to define various (up to six) parameters that you would like to track for the operation.  These parameter values can be used as part of the calculation for scheduling, capacity planning, or costing.
questions.question:
Outside of the pre-delivered standard value keys defined in the system, are new standard value keys required for production?

What information do you need captured about your operation in order to assist with scheduling / capacity planning / costing?  For example, you may want to track labor time or machine time values.

questions.topicDefinition: Shift sequences are used to define the work schedule for your production operations.  This schedule defines the start time, end time, and break times for your production shifts.  This information is then used as part of the capacity planning and scheduling functions.
questions.question:
What are the start times, end times, and break times for each of the production shifts?

What days of the week are each of the shift definitions applicable to your production operations?

questions.topicDefinition: MRP Groups are used to group materials that use the same MRP control parameters.  By defining an MRP Group, planning can be executed for all of the materials in the group in one planning run, that you do not want to include in a generic plant-wide planning run.
questions.question: Are there materials that you would like to plan using parameters that are different than the global parameters defined for the plant?

questions.configRef: Define Period Profile for Safety Time/Actual Range of Coverage
questions.topicDefinition:

A period profile can be defined for use in a planning run.  If the period profile is not defined in the planning run, the default will be taken from the material master record.

questions.topicDefinition:

questions.topicDefinition:
The supply and demand profiles allow for grouping of the various supply and demand elements that are relevant for the evaluation of material shortages.

The supply profiles list out the supply elements (plant stock, production order, SA schedule line, etc.), and the demand profiles list out the demand elements (sales order, dependent reservations, etc.) that are taken into consideration when calculating material shortages.

questions.topicDefinition:
Rescheduling checks allow the user to identify receipt elements (such as firmed planned orders, production orders, purchase orders, etc.) are still suitable to fulfill requirements based on the existing dates on the receipt element.

You can specify which particular receipt elements should be taken into consideration for a rescheduling check.
questions.question:
For each plant, what are the receipt elements (if any) you would like to take into consideration for rescheduling if the existing dates are not longer applicable for the requirements?

What amount of tolerance (in workdays) would you want to allow for when deciding if the receipt element needs to be rescheduled?

questions.configRef: Define Single Screen Entry for Confirming Process Orders

questions.topicDefinition:

The configuration includes an "area selection" tab and a "default" tab  

The "header" section under "area selection" defines the data that identifies the operation to be confirmed. 

The "detail areas" section under "area selection" defines which fields the user will be prompted to fill in as part of the confirmation details.

The "default" tab indicates the type of confirmation to propose, if default values for quantities or services should be proposed.  If services are proposed, how many (maximum of 6) should be displayed and what are the texts associated with them?

Recommendation

To prevent the matrix from getting too large, you should combine work centers located in the same area into one location group.

questions.topicDefinition: A project coding mask is used to create a structure for the project IDs. A coding mask helps in displaying complex projectIDs. For example, it can help in indicating the level of the WBS element in the overall project hierarchy.
questions.question: While setting up a project structure, any specific pattern that needs to be used for project and WBS Elements IDs?

questions.topic: Create Project Types for WBS Elements
questions.topicDefinition: Project types are used to group projects based on a certain category, for example: Capital-investment projects, Customer projects, Development projects
questions.question: Is there a need to group similar projects together for reporting purpose?

questions.topic: Maintain Budget Availability Control Profile for Projects
questions.topicDefinition: Control budget consumption in your projects and WBS elements by creating a Budget Availability Control Profile, where you specify the time range of the budget, the relevant semantic tags, and the budget tolerance limits.
questions.question: Is there a need to control budget for a project?

questions.topic: Set Project Status Area of Project Brief
questions.topicDefinition: Project status area provides the overall status of the project along with its current trend. The detailed status can also be set for some of the critical project areas like schedule, cost, quality etc.
questions.question: Is there a need for a detailed status information like the overall project status with its current trends. By default, all detailed status areas are active such as schedule or cost, with their status values and trends.

questions.topic: Configure Flexible Workflow for Project Release
questions.topicDefinition: Set up workflow approval process before the project is set to be released. Company code, project type, profit center or responsible cost center of the project can be set as a precondition to start a workflow.
questions.question: Is there a need to for an approval before the project is released for execution?

questions.configRef: Maintain Default Purchasing Organization for Retail Site
questions.topicDefinition: Use this configuration activity to maintain the default purchasing organization for your distribution centers/stores.
questions.question: How many different purchasing departments do you have? Most companies have one central purchasing department for each company code. In general several purchasing organizations can be defined.  In this activity you should assign the default  purchasing oraganization relevant for the store/distirbituion center.

questions.configRef: Maintain Attributes for Retail Valuation Area
questions.topicDefinition: Use this configuration activity to maintain sales price valuation activation status.
questions.question: Once sales price valuation is active at valuation area level, for all valuated stocks, the system records not only the value at cost but the value at retail. Every goods movement is therefore valuated both at cost and retail. Its an important initial system setting.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to maintain information for the site such as factory calendar, POS outbound profile, POS inbound profile, POS currency and so on.

With this configuration activity, you can adjust/overwrite the settings provided by SAP and for distribution centers you have to specifiy a store specific distribution chain (sales organization and distribution channel) relevant for retail sales pricing.
questions.question:
Most of the retail site parameters are provided by default, but adjustments may be required.
Please review the available attributes assigned.
Example: 
- Is the POS currency different than company code currency?
- Is there a need to introduce a customer specific POS Inbound profil? If yes, adjust the profile for the store
- Is there a need to introduce a customer specific POS Outbound profil? If yes, adjust the profile for the store
- Is there a need to introduce a customer specific factory calender= If yes, adjust the factory calender for the store 
- Assign the relevant store distribution chain for retail pricing  (sales organiziation/channel) to the distribution center.

questions.topicDefinition: Use this configuration activity to define reasons to block a site (example renovation) and whether blocks are relevant for ordering and/or delivering and/or billing.
questions.question:
Under certain circumstances a site must be blocked for a period of time. Such a block can have an impact on ordering and/or delivering and/or billing.
- Which blocking reasons for a site could be relevant (for example: renovation)?
- Is an ordering block required for site? 
- Is a delivery block required for the site?
- Is a billing block required for the site?
Define all blocking reasons and specify all possible combinations related to ordering/delivering and billing.

questions.configRef: Edit Headers for Each Characteristic Type
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define the headers for customer specific columns  for the different characertistic types.

There is the possibility to create one entry for each characteristic type and language. Enter the corresponding headers in each required customer field.
Example with three customer fields:
Characteristic Type + Language 
- CustField1
- CustField2
- CustField3

COLOR CHAR EN Own Color Spec. Color Ext. Color 

If you then manage characteristic values for a characteristic with type "characteristic 1", three additional columns will be available  to record your customer-specific additional data, with the appropriate column headers.
The table is empty in the standard delivery.
questions.question:
During creation of a generic article (for example a t-shirt is created with different colours and sizes) the relevant characteristics are shown and by default the possible characteristic values (colours and sizes) with a descriptions. It is possible to enhance this by additional custom specific columns. 
Is there the need to have additional descriptions available? If yes, define for the available characteristic types the header description for the custom specific field(s).

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to enable generic characteristic type display in various applications.
Use General Characteristic Type Display to switch between generic labels and characteristic specific labels in the following applications:
Variant characteristic sub screen in Basic Data tab in applications Maintain Article and Display Article
Characteristic type value help in all relevant applications
questions.question: Check whether the generic description (characteristic 1, charateristic 2 etc.) is applicable for the characteristic types or descriptions like "color/ main size/ size2" fits better the requirement  of your company

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to edit/maintain brands. 

You define the brands permitted for use in the maintenance of the retail article master data. You can characterize each brand as a manufacturer or a private label.

SAP does not deliver any predefined brands. You can define the brands as required (with your language-dependent description).
questions.question:
Is there the requirement to categorize the articles based on brands? 
Specify all necessary brands and label accordingly manufacturer or private label.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to maintain controlling parameters.

You define a reference distribution center and a reference store relevant for the reference handling during retail article creation.
The sites (store and distribution center) are created via central business configuration.
Recommendation:
These sites should be non-operational sites.
SAP does not deliver any predefined assignments.
questions.question:
There is a reference handling concept available in retail to avoid/minimize the data creation for all retail article-site combinations. The reference sites (distribution center and store) assigned within this activity enables this concept.
As a one-time activity a distribution center and store are assigned to. These sites should be non-operational.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to manage general settings of the assortment module management solution.
	
- You can define the lead time for advance notifications that the system sends to users who are responsible for processing errors that occur during master data generation.	
- You can specify whether the system ignores or considers the opening	 date and closing date of a site when calculating the respective listing conditions.
- You can display the retention period that defines the number of days for which the system retains the assortment module versions after they have expired.
questions.question:
For the assortment module management solution some configuration is provided. Check the settings and adjust if necessary.
- Is the lead time for notification of errors sufficient to enable a purchasing in-time? 
- Should the opening and closing date be considered of a site during the listing process?
- how long should be the retention period of expired assortment modules versions?

questions.configRef: Assign Responsible Users for Postprocessing Errors
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign responsible users for postprocessing errors.	

Specify the users to whom the system sends advance notifications in the assortment module management solution if errors occur during the generation of retail article master data.	
The users are assigned at merchandise category level.
questions.question:
Within the assortment module management solution, retail aticles are assigned to distribution center(s) and assortment module version(s). During this process, missing master data of the retail articles are generated. In case of errors the responsible user can be notified
- Which user should get a notification for which merchandise category?
Assign the relevant data within this activity.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to maintain pricing type.

The pricing type contains several parameters for controlling sales price calculations. 
It determines:
- Which sales price calculation schema is used in sales price calculation
- Whether a pricing document is created when a calculation is saved and whether document indeces for the pricing worklist are saved at the same time
- How sales prices are affected by changes in the basic purchase price
- Which currency the system uses to calculate prices
- Which exchange rate is used for currency conversions

Standard settings are provided by SAP.

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution center based on purchase price on different organizational levels.
questions.question: The pricing type is relevant for retail sales price calculation. Analyze the standard settings and check whether pricing schemas and related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.

questions.configRef: Assign Price Point Group to Organization Level
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign price point groups to a combination of distribution chain, price list, price point currency and price point category.

Price point groups can be assigned more than once.

Standard settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question:
Are price point groups relevant for sales price definition?
Assign the relevant price point groups to the relevant organizational levels and category.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Check the settings delivered delivered by SAP standard and adjust If necessary

questions.configRef: Assign Price Point Group to Organization Level/Merchandise Category
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign price point groups to a combination of distribution chain, merchandise category (material group), price list price point currency, and price point category.

No standard settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question:
Are you using price point groups during the retail sales price calculation and do you want to enable different price point groups for different merchandise categories?
Evaluate the relevant merchandise cateogories and create if necessary merchandise category specific price point group settings.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define control settings for retail sales pricing. 

List fields with detailed information are assigned to the different pricing procedures relevant for retail pricing. These pricing procedures are defined within the configuration activity "Maintain pricing type".
For some list fields condition types are assigned to control the saving in master conditions. Example: This is done for sales price condition relevant for sales price in store (with/without tax), or promotion sales price or purchasing price. Currency relevant settings can be done in addition. For other list fields control settings for subtotals are defined.

Standard settings are provided by SAP.

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution centers based on purchase price on different organizational levels.
questions.question: The settings are relevant for retail sales price calculation. Analyze the standard settings and check whether related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.

questions.configRef: Assign Pricing Type/Reference Plant to Organizational Level
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign pricing types and reference sites for retail pricing to different organizational levels.

Organizational levels are:
•Distribution chains (combinations of sales organization and distribution channel)
•Price lists (with price list currencies) in certain distribution chains (optional)

Assign the relevant pricing type to the organizational level(s)  and enter one of the sites in the distribution chain as the reference site.

The reference site can either be a dummy site (not used in any operational process) or an operational site (store and distribution center).

Standard settings are provided by SAP for organizational levels and pricing type. The reference sites must be assigned by the customer.

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution center based on purchase price on different organizational levels
questions.question: The assignment of pricing type to organizational level and reference sites are relevant for retail sales price calculation. Analyze the standard settings and check whether related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.Assign the reference sites for pricing to the different organizational levels.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign pricing tables for the condition types for data storage.
 
The condition types defined within the configuration activity "control pricing per list field" and the relevant retail pricing procedure are relevant for this configuration activity.   
This assignment is performed separately for the three pricing levels distribution chain, distribution chain/site and distribution chain/price list.

Standard settings are provided by SAP for the retail pricing procedures and conditions types delivered by SAP.

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution center based on purchase price on different organizational levels.
questions.question: The assignment of allowed pricing levels are relevant for retail sales price calculation. Analyze the standard settings and check whether related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.

questions.configRef: Control Pricing Document Adjustment for Internal Procurement
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define how pricing documents are adjusted for internal procurement.

The documents affected by this configuration activity relate to internal suppliers (distribution centers).

Standard settings are provided by SAP for the conditions types and condition tables delivered by SAP .

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution center based on purchase price on different organizational levels. The functionality of pricing worklist enables the automatic recalculation of sales prices in case of purchase price changes. These settings are relevant for this process.
questions.question: Which price change in internal procurement should trigger a new sales price caculation?   Analyze the standard settings and check whether related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.

questions.configRef: Subsequent Index Compilation for Sales Prices
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define the control parameters for the subsequent compilation of indices for sales price conditions.

You enter the condition types and associated condition tables for which a worklist is to be generated.

Standard settings are provided by SAP for the conditions types and condition tables delivered by SAP.

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution center based on purchase price on different organizational levels. The functionality of pricing worklist enables the automatic recalculation of sales prices in case of purchase price changes. These settings are relevant for this process
questions.question: Analyze the standard settings and check whether related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.

questions.configRef: Control Pricing Document Adjustment for External Procurement
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define the control mechanisms for the adjustment of pricing documents.

The documents that are to be taken into account refer to external sources of supply, or external suppliers (vendors).

Standard settings are provided by SAP for the conditions types and condition tables delivered by SAP.

Note:
The retail sales price calculation allows you to calculate retail sales prices for stores and distribution center based on purchase price on different organizational levels. The functionality of pricing worklist enables the automatic recalculation of sales prices in case of purchase price changes. These settings are relevant for this process.
questions.question: Which price/discount change in external procurement should trigger a new sales price caculation? Analyze the standard settings and check whether related settings are sufficient. Adjust if required.

questions.configRef: Define Price Point Group and Assign Price Point Ranges
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define price point groups and assign price point ranges.

Price points are used in sales price calculations as proposals for persuasive sales prices. Price points are created with the aid of price point ranges.

Standard settings are provided by SAP

Example
Typical price points are the ninety-nine prices (such as 6.99, 7.99, 8.99, 9.99).
questions.question:
Are price point groups relevant for sales price definition?
Which ranges are available?
Are they different in different sales and different selling channels? 
Are they different for standard sales prices and promotional sales prices? 

Check price point groups provided by SAP standard or create customer specific price point groups and ranges.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define the settings controlling the behavior of the customer maintenance application in the in-store merchandise and inventory management.

You can configure this activity to create schema with basic settings:
1. Depending whether the business process requirements are the same or different in your sites, define one or more customizing schema(s). For each customizing schema, maintain the required basic settings.
2. To simplify the assignment to sites one customizing schema is defined as the standard, which is then called automatically for any sites that have not been assigned a customizing schemas. On the customizing schemas overview screen, mark a customizing schema as standard. Even if you only use one customizing schema, you must set this flag.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Do you need to create customers in a specific way depending on the site? If so, you can control this through definition of different schemas for customer maintenance.

questions.configRef: Define Grouping Schema and Assign Countries
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define the system settings that determine the countries/regions in which customers can be maintained in In-Store Merchandise and Inventory Management.

You can configure this activity to create a schema with basic settings:
1. Define one or more grouping schemas depending on whether the requirements of the business process are the same or different in your  sites. Assign the required country/region keys to each grouping schema. Using an indicator, you can define whether it is also possible to enter a region for each country/region key.
2. Flag a grouping schema as standard on the overview screen of the grouping schemas. You must set this flag even if you only use one grouping schema.
3. The countries/regions you enter here are displayed in a dropdown list in the maintenance dialog for customer master data when the input help for the country/region field is called.
The country/region keys must already have been created in the system.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Do you need to create customers in a specific way depending on the the country or the regions of a site? If so, you can control this through definition of different grouping schemas.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign the customizing schema to your stores.

In this activity you can assign the customizing schema to your sites. You do not need to make an entry for sites that are to use the standard customizing schema.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: If the way a customer needs to be maintained depends on site you can assign the appropriate schema.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign the grouping schemas to your stores.

You can assign the grouping schemas to your sites. 
You do not need to make an entry for  sites. You do not need to make an entry for sites that are to use the standard grouping schema.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: If the way a customer needs to be maintained depends on site you can assign the appropriate grouping schema.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to assign a template customer to an existing customizing schema.

You can assign a template customer to a customizing schema.

No standard settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Do you have a customer that can be used as a template for all sites belonging to the same customizing schema? If so, you can here assign these customer to the schema.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define which of the condition types used are to be sent to the POS systems using Data Replication Framework applications.

These conditions are grouped together in a condition type group.
In the first step you define the condition type group and give it a name.
In the second step you assign the relevant condition types to a group and maintain the attributes of the condition type.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question:
Find out which condition types are supported by the POS systems used in your company so that they can be used in the POS interface. Usually all you have to do is create a condition type group for every country/region and POS system in use.
If you wish to allow different condition types per assortment user or usage, you must create a number of different condition type groups.

Create at least one condition type group, which has to be assigned to POS outbound profile.

questions.configRef: Assign POS Language Profile to Organizational Units
questions.topicDefinition:
In the step, you can assign the language profile for POS at sales organization, distribution channel, or store level.

For example, if all stores in a region and belonging to the same distribution chain have identical language requirements, then you can assign a language profile at distribution chain level (sales organization and distribution channel). This setting is configured at a generic level and applies to all stores under this distribution chain.

Note: Store-specific settings are prioritized over distribution chain level settings.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: In which languages do POS receipts need to be printed? Are they same across all stores? Based on that, you can combine all languages under one profile and assign to distribution chain.

questions.configRef: Assign POS Lead Time to Organizational Units
questions.topicDefinition:
In the step, you can assign the lead time for POS at sales organization, distribution channel, or store level.

For example, if all stores in a region and belonging to the same distribution chain have identical language requirements, then you can assign a language profile at distribution chain level (sales organization and distribution channel). This setting is configured at a generic level and applies to all stores under this distribution chain.

Note: Store-specific settings are prioritized over distribution chain level settings.
questions.question: How many days in advance do stores need to receive information about sales price changes? Is the POS system designed to receive multiple prices (different validity)? Maintain "lead times" accordingly either at distribution chain level or store level.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define how master data is to be prepared for transfer to the POS systems.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question:
Which exchange rate category is to be used for transferring the exchange rate table?
Which of the possible condition types are to be transferred to the POS systems?
These parameters are grouped together in a profile which you can assign to the relevant stores. The assignment of POS outbound profiles to stores can be done using configuration activity "Maintain Retail Site Parameters".

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity if you want to use the functions of pricing worklist. 

You must create pricing documents using document index when you save sales prices.

Sales prices are generally calculated on the basis of the purchase price. If the purchase price or the above parameters for source determination change, it is advisable to check the existing sales prices with respect to the new margin. The pricing worklist function allows you to determine all calculations affected by parameter changes.
questions.question: You can maintain condition types in this customizing for which changes are tracked and an entry is created in WIND table immediately. for delta handling in POS outbound service processing worklist there are entries for Document category 80, Usage A, and Application V or M.

questions.configRef: Maintain Message Category for POS Outbound
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to include or exclude articles with missing text descriptions in XML.

You can influence the system behavior to include or exclude articles based on missing article text descriptions and/or till-receipt text descriptions in preferred language.
questions.question: For example, POS receipts must contain 'FR' descriptions (preferred language), you can customize it here so that an article with missing French description is not sent to POS. Instead an error is raised, so that you can correct the master data.

questions.configRef: Define Language Profile for POS and Include Languages
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define language profile for POS and include the necessary languages in the language profile.

Language profiles for POS are used to group together one or more languages for sending information to your POS system. For example, article descriptions  and till-receipt text descriptions. You can also enable one or more languages as preferred languages in a language profile by selecting the checkbox "Organizational Unit Preference".
questions.question: In which languages do you print POS receipts? Are they the same across all stores? Based on that, you can combine all languages under one profile and assign to distribution chain.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define additional information for controlling the summarized sales.

You can enable POS inbound for non-listed articles, that is for articles for which required article master data segments (logistics store data, storage location data, valuation data) are not yet available.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Is it possible that an article is sold in store for which it is not listed?

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define additional information to control the receipt-specific sales.

You can enable POS inbound for non-listed articles, that is for articles for which required article master data segments (logistics store data, storage location data, valuation data) are not yet available.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Is it possible that an article is sold in store for which it is not listed?

questions.configRef: Maintain Anonymous Customer for Payment List
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to maintain anonymous customer information for payment list.

This customer is used when the POS system does not transfer a customer number for a particular transaction. If no customer is maintained in this field, the customer that is assigned to the store master is used.

No standard settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Does your POS solution transfer the customer relevant for a payment list? If not, you can specify the default customer in this step.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define how data is to be processed for billing functions during SOAP service processing.

The payment list is used to receive information about the means of payment used by the customers.
The payment list is only useful if aggregated sales information is received from POS solutions, since aggregated sales usually does not contain any information on the means of payment.
The payment list also creates billing documents to pass on amounts to accounting.
Standard Settings
Following fields are required and transferred to billing functions. If no is maintained, the system creates an error during SOAP service processing.
•Sales Document Type
This order type is used for defining the source in the copy control function of billing. The copy control function enables you to specify how billing copies over data. Copy control has already been configured for the POS interface by SAP. You normally do not have to make any changes. By default, the value is set as 'EOX1'.
•Billing Type
The billing type which is to be used. This controls processing in billing functions. By default, the value is set as 'CIX1'.
•Calculation Schema
This determines how values are to be calculated for billing functions. You can use the same calculation schema as with aggregated sales. For example calculation schema 'A10034' is delivered for Germany.
•Condition type
Represents the sales price in the calculation. This condition type is used for compatibility with the calculation schema of aggregated sales. The value of this condition is always zero. By default, the value is set as 'EPV0'.
•Item Category
The item category which is to be used for billing items. The item category is also used for copy control and processing control in billing functions. You require a text item category for the payment list. By default, the value is set as 'TATX'.
•Send Confirmation
AggregatedPaymentList node can be partially processed during creation of billing and article documents for the items which are successfully processed, and the error reason is provided for failed or erroneous items. Outbound confirmation is not triggered and one of the following scenarios take place:
◦The system reprocesses the failed records. During reprocessing, if failed items are processed successfully, then outbound confirmation is triggered with information on the list of documents created.
◦If the failed items could not be corrected in SAP S/4HANA system, then AIF message is set to cancel in the AIF Monitor. The system triggers an outbound confirmation with the list of documents created and the list of failed items.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Analyze which default values are suitable for processing payment lists being transferred from your POS solution.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define additional information to control the financial transactions.

You can specify whether a successful posting of a financial transaction should trigger the sending of a confirmation message.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Do you want to send a confirmation message about the successful posting of a financial transaction?

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define transaction types for financial transactions for the POS Inbound SOAP service.

You can define the accounting related business transactions to be supported for financial transactions (service node - PosFinancialTransaction).

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Do you have different types of financial transactions you want to process from the POS system? If so, you can define here the respective financial transaction types.

questions.configRef: Transaction Type-Dependent Control Of Sales As Per Receipts
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define control parameters for sales as per cash register receipts depending on the transaction type sent by the POS system.

The sales as per cash register receipt data is passed onto the inventory management and billing functions.
Standard Settings
You can specify the following:
•Inventory Management
Use this flag to activate inventory management functions. By default, it is activated.
•Billing
The value passed controls how the billing document is updated. By default, value is set as 'X'.◦'1’ - Billing documents are created but not saved on the database, hence you cannot view billing documents if you set this value. Follow on documents are still created.
Note: Use '1' to improve system performance◦‘X’ - Billing documents are created and saved on the database
◦‘ ’ -  Billing documents are not created.
The system creates an error during processing if no value is maintained for the following fields.
•Storage location
Number of the storage location in which the inventory of the article is kept. A site may contain one or more storage locations. 
•Movement Type for Sales
This movement type for sales transaction is passed on to inventory management. By default, value is set as '251'.
•Movement Type for Returns
This movement type for returns transaction is passed on to inventory management. By default, value is set as '252'.
•Special Stock
Use this optional field to maintain stock of articles that needs to be managed separately for reasons of ownership or location.
•Item Category Standard
The item category is used for billing items. The item category is also used for copy control and processing control in billing. If you do not maintain item category, the system reads the value for item category from control sales as per receipt. By default, value is as 'EDX1'.

Configuration settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Analyze which default values are suitable for processing the different transaction type dependent sales transaction at receipt level from your POS solution.

questions.configRef: Transaction Types for Sales As Per Receipts
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define the supported transaction types.

If you wish sales as per cash register receipts to be processed differently as per the transaction type sent by the POS system, you can define them in this configuration.

No standard settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Do you have different types of sales as per receipt you want to process from the POS system? If so, you can define here the respective transaction types for sales as per receipts.

questions.configRef: Maintain Anonymous Customer for Sales As Per Receipts
questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to maintain anonymous customer information for sale per receipt data.

This customer is used when the POS system does not transfer a customer number for a particular transaction. If no customer is maintained in this field, the customer that is assigned to the store master is used.

No standard settings are provided by SAP.
questions.question: Does your POS solution transfer the customer relevant for a sales transaction as per receipt? If not, you can specify the default customer in this step.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define general parameters for controlling sales as per cash register receipts (service nodes - SalesPerReceipt and CustomerOrderPaymentList). 

Alternatively, you can process sales as per cash register receipts depending on the transaction type sent by the POS system.
The sales as per cash register receipt data is used in the inventory management and billing functions.
You can specify the following:
•Billing
The value passed controls how the billing document is updated. By default, value is set as 'X'.
◦'1’- Billing documents are created but not saved on the database, hence you cannot view billing documents if you set this value. Follow on documents are still created.
Note: Set value as '1' to improve system performance
◦‘X’ - Billing documents are created and saved on the database
◦‘ ’ -  Billing documents are not created.
•Inventory Management
Use this flag if you want to activate inventory management. By default, it is set as activated
•Send Confirmation
Triggers outbound confirmation when Send Confirmation is enabled.
•Explode article
This optional flag is used to include the components of structured articles during creation of master data when POS inbound is allowed for non-listed articles
Following fields are mandatory and are transferred to inventory management functions. If value is not maintained, the system creates an error during SOAP service processing.
•Storage Location
Number of the storage location in which the inventory of the article is stored. A site may contain one or more storage locations.
•Movement Type for Sales
This movement type for sales transaction is passed on to inventory management. By default, value is set as '251'.
•Movement Type for Returns
This movement type for returns transaction is passed on to inventory management. By default, value is set as '252'.
•Sales Document Type
The order type defined is used for defining the source in the copy control function of billing. The copy control function enables you to specify how billing copies over data. Copy control has already been configured for the POS interface by SAP. You normally do not have to make any changes. By default, value is set as 'EOX1'.
•Item Category Standard
The item category is used for billing items. The item category is also used for copy control and processing control in Billing. By default, value is as 'EDX1'.
•Billing Type
This billing type controls processing in billing. By default, the value is set as 'CIX1'.
•Calculation Schema: The calculation schema is used in billing. In this procedure you determine how the system should calculate values for inventory management, billing, and accounting processes. Transfer to subsequent functions is usually via condition values and in some cases via the subtotals in the calculation schemas. For example the default calculation schema for Germany is set as 'A10034'.
•Condition Type
This condition type represents the sales price in the calculation schema. By default, the value is set as 'EPV0'.
•Condition Type SAP Valuation Price
This condition type is used in the calculation schema to pass on the value for sales price valuation of the goods movements to Billing. By default, the value is set as 'EVS0'.
•Condition Type FI Valuation Price
This condition type is used in the calculation schema to pass on the value for valuation of the goods movements in FI to billing. By default, the value is set as 'ECV0'.

questions.topicDefinition:
Use this configuration activity to define how the aggregated sales data (service node - AggregatedSalesByProduct) is used for SOAP service processing.

You can specify the following:
•Inventory Management
The value passed controls how the inventory management is updated. By default, value is set as 'X'.
◦’X’- article documents are created without aggregation
◦’’- article documents are not created
•Billing
The value passed controls how the billing document is updated. By default, value is set as 'X'.
◦'1’- Billing documents are created but not saved on the database, hence you cannot view billing documents if you set this value. Follow on documents are still created.
Note: Set value as '1' to improve system performance
◦‘X’ - Billing documents are created and saved on the database
◦‘ ’ -  Billing documents are not created.
•Send Confirmation
AggregatedSalesByProduct node can be partially processed during creation of billing and article documents for the items which are successfully processed, and the error reason is provided for failed or erroneous items. Outbound confirmation is not triggered and one of the following scenarios take place:
◦The system reprocesses the failed records. During reprocessing, if failed items are processed successfully, then outbound confirmation is triggered with information on the list of documents created.
◦If the failed items could not be corrected in SAP S/4HANA system, then AIF message is set to cancel in the AIF Monitor. The system triggers an outbound confirmation with the list of documents created and the list of failed items.
•Send Partial Confirmation
The outbound message for partial confirmation contains the document numbers (billing and article documents) which are created successfully for the partially processed AggregatedSalesByProduct node. The confirmation service payload also contains log with sequence numbers of the failed items. The failed items can be reprocessed subsequently. The partial confirmation is triggered after every reprocessing in the SAP S/4HANA system.
Following fields are mandatory and are transferred to inventory management functions. If value is not maintained, the system creates an error during SOAP service processing.
•Storage Location
Number of the storage location in which the inventory of the article is stored. A site may contain one or more storage locations.
•Movement Type for Sales
This movement type for sales transaction is passed on to inventory management. By default, value is set as '251'.
•Movement Type for Returns
This movement type for returns transaction is passed on to inventory management. By default, value is set as '252'.
•Explode articleExplode article is used to include the components of structured articles during creation of master data when POS inbound is allowed for non-listed articles
•Sales Document Type
The order type defined is used for defining the source in the copy control function of billing. The copy control function enables you to specify how billing copies over data. Copy control has already been configured for the POS interface by SAP. You normally do not have to make any changes. By default, value is set as 'EOX1'.
•Item Category Standard
The item category is used for billing items. The item category is also used for copy control and processing control in Billing. By default, value is as 'EDX1'.
•Billing Type
This billing type controls processing in billing. By default, the value is set as 'CIX1'.
•Calculation Schema: The calculation schema is used in billing. In this procedure you determine how the system should calculate values for inventory management, billing, and accounting processes. Transfer to subsequent functions is usually via condition values and in some cases via the subtotals in the calculation schemas. For example the default calculation schema for Germany is set as 'A10034'.
•Number of Items: This field determines the number of aggregated sales items packaged into a single application interface framework (AIF) data message. A single billing document and article document is created for each AIF data message.
•Condition Type
This condition type represents the sales price in the calculation schema. By default, the value is set as 'EPV0'.
•Condition Type SAP Valuation Price
This condition type is used in the calculation schema to pass on the value for sales price valuation of the goods movements to Billing. By default, the value is set as 'EVS0'.
•Condition Type FI Valuation Price
This condition type is used in the calculation schema to pass on the value for valuation of the goods movements in FI to billing. By default, the value is set as 'ECV0'.

Use this configuration activity to make the system settings that control the store pickup order in Process Picking Requests and Hand Over Orders apps.

Standard Settings:
Generate store pickup order and store picking request when S/4HANA sales order is saved in the SAP S/4HANA system.

The following settings are applicable to all the stores:
•Shipping point: Specifies the physical location or collection point in the store for click-and-collect scenario. Use shipping point to identify a sales order which is relevant for a store pickup order. That means only sales orders containing items with shipping point mentioned here are eligible for generation of store pickup order and store picking requests.
•Rejection reason for short picking: Specifies the reason for rejecting a sales order item.
In some cases, products selected online, may not be available or only partially available in the store. In such cases, the Process Picking Request app triggers a partial or full cancellation of sales order item. The rejection reason mentioned here is used by default.
•Rejection reason for handover of reserved orders: In "Click-and-Reserve" scenario, customer collects the reserved products but can decide to return some of them. In that case, entire sales order is cancelled, and this default rejection reason is used.
Note: Currently, in the Hand Over Orders app when store associate selects Reservation handover, the sales order gets cancelled automatically by using this default rejection reason.
•Rejection reason for item cancellation: Specify a reason for rejecting a sales order item.
•Allow product cancellation during handover: Enables cancellation of item (product) in a sales order using the Hand Over Orders application.
•Reservation handover without cancellation: In the Hand Over Orders application when a store associate selects Reservation Handover, instead of sales order getting cancelled, a billing document is created.
