questions.configRef: Assign Planning Levels to Cash Trade Requests
questions.topicDefinition:
Planning level provides information on the causes of bank or account transactions for bank accounts and planning groups. For example, you can identify how a piece of information came into the system (posting or payment advices/plan item) and how probable it is that a cash inflow or outflow will take place on the day planned.
you can assign planning levels to cash requests with different statues. Planning levels are derived for a cash request. By assign planning levels to cash requests, you can then see cash requests in different statues by planning level.

questions.configRef: Assign Rules for Determining the Billing Date
questions.topicDefinition: The billing cycle is part of scheduling for billing and invoicing. It controls the derivation of the billing period for periodic bills. This step define rules for determining the billing date. Determination of the billing date is based by default on the creation date of a billable item in the system. In this step, you specify the rules that scheduling uses to calculate the target date of billing for a billable item.

questions.topicDefinition:
The new billing engine that is made available with scope item 4E9 and shipped in CE 2008 is accompanied with a new architecture that enables customers to use a new SSCUI for flexible material determination. As a result, the restriction on the number of activity types and corresponding sales materials that can be used in the traditional billing solution for professional services are overcome with the new billing solution. 

Currently, 4E9 supports the billing on a fixed-price, time and expenses, and periodic services basis. Additionally, write off or postponement of  amounts or quantities is possible. Please note that existing customers can choose when to:

•	Activate the scope item 4E9 in your quality system.
•	Switch on the new billing solution on for new projects on a case by case basis.

Once the scope item 4E9 is activated in the quality system the scope item is shipped with no configuration maintained. 
The setup and configuration specific to the customer requirements are maintained in the project billing profile and respective material determination.

For new customers, scope item 4E9 is activated by default and it is not possible to use the traditional billing solution.

questions.topicDefinition:
In professional services, the possible procurement subprocesses are:

Service procurement - an external service is ordered. The external service company confirms the purchase order and performs the service. The supplier posts the expenses back. A supplier invoice is created and processed.

Material procurement for consumption - a consumption material is requested from a customer or internal project and a purchase order is created and sent to the supplier. The supplier sends the material to the company, and the goods receipt is checked. Finally, the supplier invoice is created and the invoice is paid.

Procurement for third-party order processing - a material is ordered by the purchaser of the ordering company for an end-customer from a supplier. The supplier ships the material directly to this end-customer.

questions.topicDefinition:
In this step, you can configure how taxes are to be posted for invoice reduction.

The system creates two accounting documents for invoice reduction. The first document (original document) contains the invoice data sent by the supplier. The second document (complaint document) contains information about the invoice reduction.
questions.question:
Would you like to configure how taxes are to be posted for invoice reduction.?Example

The supplier sends the following invoice:

Gross invoice value:		1100 EUR
Tax amount at 10% tax rate: 100 EUR
Net invoice value:		1000 EUR
The system determines a proposed net invoice value of 950 EUR. The net difference of 50 EUR is claimed as a manual invoice reduction (supplier error). This net difference's 10% tax portion is calculated as 5 EUR.

Tax reduction in the original document: 100 EUR
Tax posting in the original document: 100 EUR
Tax posting in complaint document: -5 EUR
Tax reduction in the original document
Tax posting in the original document: 95 EUR
Tax posting in complaint document: 0 EUR

questions.topicDefinition:
A Sales Organization in SAP is a representation of the sales legal entity within the business, responsible for the sale of goods and/or services. This is the primary organizational unit in sales and is part of what forms the 'Sales Area'. 

Materials and Business partners can have different master data  in each sales area. 

This Configuration Activity allows the modification of the name, address, language and e-mail address of the sales organizations you have defined.

questions.topicDefinition:
The Distribution Channel in SAP represents the channels through which saleable goods or services reach the customer. Typical examples of Distribution Channels include wholesale, retail, direct and online sales. Divisions are attached to Sales Organizations, and are part of what forms the Sales Area.

This Configuration Activity allows the user to change the description of the distribution channels that have been defined.
questions.question: Please provide a description for each distribution channel you have defined (e.g. Wholesale, Retail, Digital).

questions.topicDefinition:
In SAP, a division represents a product line, or a grouping of materials or services. For example, one might categorize Fresh foods, Frozen foods and drinks into different product divisions.

A sales group is used to identify sales representatives, or groups of sales representatives. E.g. If you have nine total sales representatives split over three regions, then you might define three sales groups to represent each region's sales reps - or nine sales groups for each sales rep, depending on your business context. 

The responsible sales group can be assigned to a customer in their master data, and used for analysis or pricing determination.

questions.topicDefinition:
If you have multiple distribution channels, e.g. Retail and Digital, then this generally requires that you have separate condition, product and customer master data for each channel. 

With this Configuration Activity, you can indicate that the master data for one distribution channel is re-used in other channels. For example, you can stipulate that the digital distribution channel will refer to the retail channel master data for conditions. For each distribution channel, you can indicate a reference distribution channel to be used for 1. Conditions, and 2. Customer and product master data. Please review the starter system for examples.

questions.topicDefinition:
If you have multiple product divisions, e.g. Fresh and Frozen, then this generally requires that you have separate condition, and customer master data for each division. 

With this Configuration Activity, you can indicate that the master data for one product division is re-used in other divisions. For example, you can stipulate that the frozen product division will refer to the 'Fresh' division's master data for conditions. questions.topicDefinition: In the event that you have additional groupings of customers that you use for reporting, pricing, or other functions, this Configuration Activity allows you to define the values that may be chosen for the Customer Group 1 Reserved customer field. These values may then be assigned to business partner in their customer master data.
questions.question: Please provide the 3 digit key, and short description of the values that should be available for assignment in the Customer Group 1 master data field.

questions.topic: Maintain Reserve Fields in Customer Master
questions.topicDefinition: In the event that you have additional groupings of customers that you use for reporting, pricing, or other functions, this Configuration Activity allows you to define the values that may be chosen for the Customer Group 2 Reserved customer field. These values may then be assigned to business partner in their customer master data.
questions.question: Please provide the 3 digit key, and short description of the values that should be available for assignment in the Customer Group 2 master data field.

questions.topic: Maintain Reserve Fields in Customer Master
questions.topicDefinition: In the event that you have additional groupings of customers that you use for reporting, pricing, or other functions, this Configuration Activity allows you to define the values that may be chosen for the Customer Group 3 Reserved customer field. These values may then be assigned to business partner in their customer master data.
questions.question: Please provide the 3 digit key, and short description of the values that should be available for assignment in the Customer Group 3 master data field.

questions.topic: Maintain Reserve Fields in Customer Master
questions.topicDefinition: In the event that you have additional groupings of customers that you use for reporting, pricing, or other functions, this Configuration Activity allows you to define the values that may be chosen for the Customer Group 4 Reserved customer field. These values may then be assigned to business partner in their customer master data.
questions.question: Please provide the 3 digit key, and short description of the values that should be available for assignment in the Customer Group 4 master data field.

questions.topic: Maintain Reserve Fields in Customer Master
questions.topicDefinition: In the event that you have additional groupings of customers that you use for reporting, pricing, or other functions, this Configuration Activity allows you to define the values that may be chosen for the Customer Group 5 Reserved customer field. These values may then be assigned to business partner in their customer master data.
questions.question: Please provide the 3 digit key, and short description of the values that should be available for assignment in the Customer Group 5 master data field.

questions.topic: Shipping Point and Goods Receiving Point Determination
questions.topicDefinition:
A Shipping Point within SAP is an organizational entity which is responsible for planning and processing deliveries to the customer. Each plant needs to have at least one shipping point from where the deliveries pertaining to that plant can be processed.

This Configuration Activity allows you to update the Shipping Point Description, Address, stipulate what factory calendar it runs on, loading time, and picking/packing time to be defaulted when this shipping point is being used.
questions.question: For each shipping point you have defined in the organizational structure, please indicate which factory calendar it is aligned to and how many days should be assumed for delivery loading, and picking/packing. Please also provide an address for each shipping point.

questions.topic: Shipping Point and Goods Receiving Point Determination
questions.topicDefinition:
A shipping condition is a way of classifying the way a shipment will be handled. For example, you may have separate Standard, Pick-Up, Priority, or Return shipments which you handle in different ways. These conditions can be assigned to specific customers, or defaulted depending on the delivery type - for example, the return shipping condition on return deliveries.

This Configuration Activity allows you to modify existing, or define new shipping conditions that can be used in shipping point determination.
questions.question: The SAP Starter System has some pre-configured shipping conditions. Please advise if you need to edit the definition of these configuration settings, or create new ones.

questions.topic: Shipping Point and Goods Receiving Point Determination
questions.topicDefinition:
Loading groups are used to cluster materials with similar requirements when being loaded for shipment. For example, some materials may be loaded by crane, some by hand, some by pipe etc. This can be taken into account in determining what shipping point is determined for use to ship a particular material. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the description of existing loading groups, or define new loading groups that can be assigned to materials in their master data.
questions.question: SAP Starter System has some pre-configured Loading Groups. Please advise if you need to edit the definition of these configuration settings or create new ones.

questions.topic: Shipping Point and Goods Receiving Point Determination
questions.topicDefinition: Using this Configuration Activity, you allocate the shipping points to the desired combinations of shipping condition and loading group for each plant. You can assign one shipping point to multiple plants, or one plant can have multiple shipping points.
questions.question: Please provide details to allocate the shipping points to the desired combinations of shipping condition and loading group for each plant.

questions.topicDefinition:
The sales document type used will determine the type of standard sales process that will follow, e.g. whether you are conducting a Sell from Stock, Sale of Non-Stock, Return etc. process. 

With this Configuration Activity, you can adjust the description of the various sales document types.
questions.question: Please evaluate the descriptions of the Sales Document Types in Starter System and advise if you would like to change any.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to configure whether for each pre-delivered item category, rounding is enabled or not. Rounding may be useful if you want to allow the system to round the quantity in the sales document up or down to match the permitted delivery quantity for example.
questions.question: Should all sales order line items be processed for the quantity ordered, or should rounding of the ordered quantity be permitted? If rounding should be allowed, please describe in which scenarios or item categories this should be enabled.

questions.topicDefinition: When you add a material to a sales document, the system automatically determines its item category based on the order type, item category group of the material, and the high level item category group. This Configuration Activity allows you to change the default item category, and manually selectable item categories that can be chosen for some Sales Order Type + Item Category group combinations.
questions.question: Do you require different default, or manually selectable item categories for some sales document types? If so, please provide the allowed material item categories for each combination.

questions.configRef: Define Number Ranges for Sales Documents
questions.topicDefinition: When a sales document is saved, it may be assigned an automatic number or it may allow the user to assign a manual number to it. These numbers must be within the an allowed range of numbers that is defined in this Configuration Activity. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the number ranges assigned to each number range group, and to modify the number considered as the current number within each of these groups.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered number ranges in your starter system, and the sales documents assigned to each number range. If you require changes to these combinations, please list the new combinations required.

questions.topicDefinition:
This Configuration Activity allows you to define various purchase order types by which your customers submit their order requests to you. Purchase order type refers to the channel a customer uses to place an order, such as email. With the purchase order types, you can specify whether an order was received online, by phone, or by fax.

When creating or changing a sales document, a salesperson can select an order type in purchase order data at the header level, and it will be copied to the item level. Once defined, you may assign the purchase order type on your sales document for use in reporting and logic.
questions.question: Do you need to track different means of purchase requests used by your customers? If so, please describe the types that you would like to track in your sales documents. You can specify whether an order was received online, by phone, or by fax etc.

questions.configRef: Assign Custom Routines to Sales Document Types
questions.topicDefinition:
Requested delivery date during sales order creation is defaulted based on lead time maintained in configuration step 'configure sales document types (102495). 

Alternatively, you can choose to apply a custom logic to determine the requested delivery date in Sales documents.

In this configuration step, you choose relevant sales document types and assign custom routines for determination of requested delivery date.
questions.question: Please mention if you require flexible proposal of requested delivery date to be applied and further choose the sales document types (Quotation / Sales Order) that are relevant.

questions.configRef: Define Rules to Determine Factory Calendar
questions.topic: Custom Adaptations for Requested Delivery Date
questions.topicDefinition:
Flexible Proposal of Requested Delivery Dates feature allows to dynamically propose an appropriate requested delivery date when you a process a new sales document (quotation / sales order).

This Configuration Activity allows to use the calendar rules to define how the system determines the factory calendar that is later used to dynamically propose the requested delivery date during Sales document processing .
questions.question: Choose the relevant calendar rule that best suits your business needs, which is later used for flexibly proposing the requested delivery date in newly created sales documents.

questions.configRef: Define Parameter Catalog for Requested Delivery Date
questions.topic: Custom Adaptations for Requested Delivery Date
questions.topicDefinition:
With this configuration step you can list the parameters that the Configurable Parameters Formulas (CPF) Framework can include in the formulas that allows flexible proposition of requested delivery date in a sales document. 

This Configuration Activity also provides the flexibility to add custom fields as additional input parameters if necessary.

The parameter catalog lists the parameters that the CPF framework can include in the formulas to determine requested delivery date in sales document. The following six parameters are the standard parameters predelivered by SAP.

1) DISTRIBUTIONCHANNEL 
2) DIVISION
3) SALESDOCUMENTTYPE
4) SALESGROUP
5) SALESOFFICE
6) SALESORGANIZATION
questions.question: Decide and mention which standard fields you would like to apply and whether you want to include any custom sales document header fields in your decision tables.

questions.configRef: Define Formulas for Requested Delivery Date in Sales Documents
questions.topic: Custom Adaptations for Requested Delivery Date
questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration step allows to create one or more formulas that facilitates flexible proposal of requested delivery dates by evaluating parameters according to the rules you specify in a decision table.

Each row in the decision table represents a rule that the system uses to propose requested delivery dates and is a conditional expression that specifies values for some or all of the input parameters, as well as for the result parameter.
questions.question: Decide and mention the specific parameter fields to define the formula and their corresponding values that can be applied in the decision table.

questions.configRef: Define Custom Routines for Requested Delivery Date in Sales Documents
questions.topic: Custom Adaptations for Requested Delivery Date
questions.topicDefinition:
In this configuration step, you can register routine numbers and assign them to enhancement id. Routine numbers must be in the number range from 3000000 to 3009999.

The routine evaluates the sales document header fields to select an appropriate lead time, factory calendar, and processing indicator as defined in the earlier dependent configuration steps 103827, 103828 & 103829.
questions.question: Choose the routine number that can be assigned to the enhancement id.

questions.configRef: Maintain Algorithm Parameters for Intelligent Product Proposal
questions.topicDefinition:
With this feature, you get a product and quantity proposals as an input help to enable faster selection of products during sales order entry with Create Sales Orders – VA01 app. It allows to predict whether the quantity of products ordered will increase or decrease.

In this configuration step, you have to maintain an algorithm parameter that helps to calculate and predict whether the quantity of the products ordered will increase or decrease. The default smoothing factor is 0.2, but you can change this to any value between 0 and 1.
questions.question:
Decide and mention if you wish to enable the intelligent product proposal.

Additionally, identify the customers (Business Partners) for whom you want to enable the intelligent product proposal.

questions.configRef: Maintain Backgr. Procedure Determination for Intelligent Product Proposal
questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration step enables you to choose which product proposal procedure you want to use to receive product and quantity proposals.

In the product proposal procedure, you determine:

How the product proposal should be displayed in the sales documents. For instance, if the system accesses the order history, how many columns should be displayed, and the interval at which the historic order quantities should be shown (for example, day, week, or month).

Which data sources the system should access (for example, order history, listing, item proposal) and sequence of accesses to data sources.
questions.question:
For Background procedure determination

Choose which product proposal procedure you want to use to receive product and quantity proposals.

The product proposal procedure is determined based on:
1) Sales area
2) Customer determination procedure for the product proposal
3) Document determination procedure for the product proposal

questions.configRef: Maintain Online Procedure Determination for Product Proposal
questions.topicDefinition:
This configuration step enables you to choose which product proposal procedure you want to use to receive product and quantity proposals.

The product proposal procedure is determined based on:
Sales area
Sales office
Sales group
Customer determination procedure for the product proposal
Document determination procedure for the product proposal
questions.question:
For Online procedure determination

Choose which product proposal procedure you want to use to receive product and quantity proposals.

The product proposal procedure is determined based on:
1) Sales area
2) Sales Office
3) Sales Group
4) Customer determination procedure for the product proposal
5) Document determination procedure for the product proposal

questions.topicDefinition:
There may be various reasons that lead to a sale which you are interested in tracking for reporting and analytics. For example, a sale may be triggered due to a sales call, a newspaper advertisement etc.
This Configuration Activity allows you to define reasons why an order is being placed - including return orders.
questions.question:
The Starter System provides pre-configured Order Reasons to track why an order might be placed. 
Please advise if you want to revise the description of these order reasons, or if you would like to add new ones.

questions.topicDefinition:
Individual line items on a sales order may be assigned a reason for rejection. This indicates that the remainder of that line item will not continue through the sales process. The rejection reason also controls whether the rejected quantity is to be billed, if it is shown or hidden on printouts, and whether the rejected quantity is considered pending further processing. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the billing, printing and open-line status of pre-delivered rejection reasons, or define new rejection reasons.
questions.question: The Starter System provides pre-configured rejection reasons why a line item might be rejected. Please advise if you would like to modify the billing, printout and open status controls in the pre-delivered rejection reasons, or if you need to define new reasons.

questions.configRef: Assign Rejection Reasons to Sales Document Types and Sales Organizations
questions.topicDefinition:
You may enable only specific reasons for rejections to be used on specific Sales Organization-Order combinations. For example, you may want 'Rejected by Customer' to be a rejection option on a standard customer order, but not to be an option for rejecting a credit memo line.

This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which rejection reasons are available to use in each Sales Organization + Document Type combination.
questions.question: For each sales organization and order type combination that you will use, please list the rejection reasons that should be available for use with that combination.

questions.topicDefinition: You may use workflows to prevent further processing of sales documents until they are released by a specific user or function. This Configuration Activity allows you to define the reason that will be displayed in a sales quotation to let the user know why an approval is required.
questions.question: Will you utilize workflows on sales quotations? If so, please list the reasons to be displayed to business users as to why the document requires release.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to assign the reasons for approval defined earlier to a sales document type.
questions.question: If you have defined reasons for approval on sales documents, please indicate which of these should be available for each sales document type. As of 1902, this is only possible for sales quotations.

questions.configRef: Define Return Reasons for Customer Returns
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to configure various reasons that  can be assigned to return order types. These reasons may be used in analytics and reports.
questions.question: Please review the standard return order reasons in the starter system. If you require modifications to the existing descriptions, or if you need additional reasons, please describe the additional reasons.

questions.configRef: Define Blocking Reasons for Sales Documents
questions.topicDefinition:
If you would like to prevent sales orders from being processed for a customer, you can configure a Sales Blocking Reason which will show the message you indicate when a user attempts to create an order for that customer. 

In this activity, you can define or modify blocking reasons that can be assigned to customers in various languages. These blocking reasons can then be assigned to customers in their master data.
questions.question: Please evaluate the Sales Blocking reasons that are available as standard in the Starter System. Provide details of new blocking reasons or revised descriptions that you require.

questions.configRef: Assign Blocking Reasons to Sales Document Types
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to assign the sales blocking reasons defined to specific sales order types. Suppose you have two sales block reasons defined: 01 - Missing Credit Limit, and 02 - Political Reasons. If you assign 01 blocking reason to Order Type OR (Standard Order) here but don't do the same for 02 - Political Reasons, then sales orders with a 01 blocking reason assigned will prevent a user from saving while OR type sales orders with an 02 blocking reason can be saved.
questions.question: Please review the standard combinations of sales blocking reasons and sales order types in the starter system. If you require additions or modifications to these combinations, then please describe which blocking reasons should block or warn the user when attempting to save an order with that reason applied.

questions.configRef: Define Reasons for Blocking in Shipping
questions.topicDefinition:
You can define different 'Blocking Reasons' with each one controlling whether the sales order creation, delivery creation, picking confirmation or goods issue activities are blocked for documents with that reason on them. The blocking reasons may be assigned to a customer and copied into the sales document from that customer, or assigned manually on a particular order.

This Configuration Activity to define new and modify existing blocking reasons along with which activities each one should block.
questions.question: The Starter System provides pre-configured Delivery blocking reasons. Please advise if you want require changes or additions to the existing blocking reasons, and note which activities each blocking reason should prohibit.

questions.configRef: Assign Blocking Reasons to Delivery Types
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to assign the delivery blocking reasons defined to specific delivery types. Suppose you have two delivery block reasons defined: 01 - Missing Credit Limit, and 02 - Political Reasons. If you assign 01 blocking reason to Delivery Type LF (Standard Delivery) here but don't do the same for 02 - Political Reasons, then sales orders with a 01 blocking reason assigned will prevent a user from creating a delivery while orders with a 02 blocking reason will allow the user to create a delivery.
questions.question: Please review the standard combinations of delivery blocking reasons and delivery types in the starter system. If you require additions or modifications to these combinations, then please describe which blocking reasons should prevent delivery creation on which delivery types.

questions.topicDefinition: With this app, you define and maintain possible reasons for blocking the creation of billing documents. For example, you may want to ensure a second review before a billing document is issued to customer with an at-risk relationship because of previous errors. In that case, if you may define a Billing Block Reason Z1 - Special Review that can then be assigned to that customer in their master data.
questions.question: The Starter System provides pre-configured Blocking Reasons for Billing. Please advise if you want to modify these descriptions, or define custom billing blocking reasons.

questions.configRef: Assign Blocking Reasons to Billing Types
questions.topicDefinition:
All billing types that should be blocked from creation if the preceding document has a billing block on it should be defined here. For example, if you want blocking reason 01 to block invoices of type Invoice (CI01) and Debit Memo (l2) but not block Credit Memo (G2) creation, then you would assign blocking reason 01 to Billing Types CI01 and L2 only in this Configuration Activity.

Note that blocking reasons defined here, once saved, cannot be deleted.
questions.question: As part of SAP Best Practice, standard assignments of Blocking Reasons to Billing Types are delivered in Starter System. Based on business needs, if you have created custom Blocking Reasons for Billing, then please advise the Billing Document Types for which they are relevant so that the necessary assignment(s) can be made here.

questions.topicDefinition:
An incompleteness procedure can be used to stop the sales process from proceeding if critical data is missing. E.g. This can be used to set a sales order as incomplete and ineligible for delivery if incoterms have not been entered .

This Configuration Activity allows you to modify existing incompleteness procedures, or define new ones - that control when various aspects of a sales document are considered incomplete, and how the system reacts to that status.

With CE2011, you can now use custom fields in incompleteness procedures for sales documents. You can add custom fields to an incompleteness procedure and navigate to the custom fields tab from the incompletion log.
questions.question: Please review the preconfigured incompleteness procedures in the starter system. Do you have any additional requirements for data that must exist on sales orders or delivery documents in order for them to proceed to the next stage of the sales process?

questions.configRef: Assign Incompleteness Procedures to Sales Document Types
questions.topicDefinition: Different incompletion checks can be applied to different types of sales orders. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which incompletion procedures are considered on each sales order type.
questions.question: Please review the preconfigured incompleteness procedures in the starter system. Do you have any additional requirements for data that must exist on sales orders or delivery documents in order for them to proceed to the next stage of the sales process?

questions.configRef: Assign Incompleteness Procedures to Item Categories
questions.topicDefinition: Different incompletion checks can be applied to each type of item on a sales order. E.g. a stock item and a free of charge item can have different critical data requirements. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which incompletion procedures are considered on each item category.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered settings in the starter system. Do you require any modification or addition to the standard incompletion checks for each item category?

questions.configRef: Assign Incompleteness Procedures to Schedule Line Categories
questions.topicDefinition: A single line item on a sales order can be split into multiple schedule lines - which controls when each amount is delivered, and whether the quantities are relevant for MRP consideration, availability check and other settings. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which incompletion procedures are considered on each schedule line item category.
questions.question: Please review the standard setup in the starter system. Do you expect any custom or non-standard completion checks to be applied to particular schedule line categories?

questions.configRef: Assign Incompleteness Procedures to Partner Functions
questions.topicDefinition: You can stipulate business partner related data that must be populated for the document to be considered complete. E.g. You can stipulate that a country key must exist for a sold-to customer, otherwise the document is considered incomplete.
questions.question: Please review the standard setup in the starter system. Do you expect any custom or non-standard completion checks to be applied to your business partner?

questions.configRef: Assign Incompleteness Procedures to Delivery Types
questions.topicDefinition: An incompleteness procedure can be used to stop the delivery process from proceeding if critical data is missing. This Configuration Activity allows you to specify which incompleteness procedure is used on each delivery type.
questions.question: Please review the standard setup in the starter system. Do you expect any custom or non-standard completion checks to be applied to particular delivery types?

questions.configRef: Assign Incompleteness Procedures to Delivery Item Categories
questions.topicDefinition: Different incompletion checks can be applied to each type of item on a delivery. E.g. an item can be considered incomplete and ineligible for delivery if batches have not been completely assigned. This Configuration Activity allows you to specify which incompleteness procedure is used on each delivery item category.
questions.question: Do you expect  any custom or non-standard completion checks to be applied to particular item types on deliveries?

questions.topicDefinition: An incompleteness status group can be flagged as blocking sales, delivery, billing, picking and other transactions. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify which action types should be blocked if the item on the sales, delivery or billing document has a particular incompleteness status group.
questions.question: Please review the standard incompleteness status groups and the fields assigned to these status groups in the starter system. If you require modifications to the standard settings, please advise.

questions.topicDefinition:
Material listing and exclusion allows you to restrict what materials can or cannot be bought by a customer.

The system will check against a set of tables when determining if the combination of customer, material, plant, or organizational unit is relevant for material listing or exclusion.

This Configuration Activity lists the pre-delivered tables available for checking listing or exclusion applicability.
questions.question: Do you need to restrict the materials that can be sold to a customer based on specific criteria? If so, please review the available tables in your starter system to see if the criteria is achieved with pre-delivered tables. If not, please indicate the criteria that needs to be considered for discussion.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to modify which of the predefined tables the system considers in determining material listing or exclusion functionality, and in what order.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered access sequences for material listing/exclusion. If you require modifications to this, please indicate that here.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define new condition types that can be determined for material listing and exclusion. For each condition type that you define for listing or for exclusion, you may assign a specific access sequence to be considered.
questions.question: If you require additional condition types for exclusions beyond the pre-delivered options, please indicate those condition types and the access sequence to be assigned to each.

questions.topicDefinition: The Configuration Activity allows you to view predelivered procedures for material listing/exclusion condition type determination, or to create new procedures. With this you can define the sequence of multiple condition types to be considered.
questions.question: If you require additional listing/exclusion procedures for determining the condition types to be assigned within a sales document, please detail the new procedures including order and related condition types here.

questions.configRef: Activate Listing/Exclusion by Sales Document Type
questions.topicDefinition:
Material listing and exclusion allows you to restrict what materials can or cannot be bought by a customer.

The system will check against a set of tables when determining if the combination of customer, material, plant, or organizational unit is relevant for material listing or exclusion.

This Configuration Activity allows you to assign a listing/exclusion procedure to each different sales document type. For example, you may enable an exclusion procedure only on return type sales documents if you only needed to prevent return of particular materials but do not enforce such exclusion on outbound sales.
questions.question: Do you restrict which materials can be sold, credited, debited, returned etc. on the basis of material, customer, plant or unit of measure? If so, please describe the listings or exclusions that need to be considered in your various sales scenarios.

questions.topicDefinition: Incoterms can be assigned to specific customers in their master data, or on sales orders. It can also be considered in freight and shipment pricing. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the description of standard incoterms, create new incoterms, and for each incoterm, specify whether or not a named location must be provided for that incoterm.
questions.question: Please review the standard provided incoterms in the starter system. Do you require additional incoterms? If so, please describe each new incoterm and whether for each one a named location is mandatory.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define multiple versions of incoterms. For example, you could define version '2010' with a description '2010 Incoterms Definition', and another version '2018' with description '2018 Incoterms Definition'.
questions.question: Do you need to maintain multiple versions of the same incoterm? If so, please describe the different versions of each incoterm you need to maintain.

questions.topicDefinition: On sales documents and master data, you may provide one or two pieces of location information per incoterm. With this Configuration Activity, you can set the label for these fields. For example, you could set the label for Incoterm Location Information 1 to be 'Port of Destination', and the label for the second piece of information to be 'Port of Delivery'.
questions.question: Please provide label descriptions for location fields 1 and 2 for each incoterm-version combination you have defined.

questions.topicDefinition: If you have defined multiple incoterms versions, this Configuration Activity allows you to map them to specifically defined incoterms. For each version-incoterm combination, you stipulate whether a location is mandatory, and whether additional location information is allowed or mandatory.
questions.question: Please review the standard incoterm and version mappings. If you require additional mappings and have defined new incoterm versions, please provide information for these combinations.

questions.topicDefinition:
A material sales status can be used to identify where in the material's lifecycle it is. For example, you may define statuses as 'Pre-Release', 'Active' and 'Obsolete'. You may assign materials to these statuses in their distribution chain master data, and prevent the sale of materials with a particular status on particular orders. For example, you could set 'Obsolete' type materials as eligible for return order types, but blocked for standard order types.

This Configuration Activity allows you to define new material statuses, and indicate whether materials with that status are permitted or blocked in various order types.
questions.question: Do you manage material lifecycle related statuses, and use this to limit when a sale can or cannot be made? If so, please describe the statuses assigned, and for each of those statuses - on which order types they should prevent the sales process from going forward.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define commission groups that you can apply to materials in their master data, and subsequently use for pricing or reporting.
questions.question: If you would like to use commission groups for  classifying materials, please provide a list of the groups that should be created.

questions.configRef: Define Relevant Date for Product Hierarchy Determination
questions.topicDefinition: The product hierarchy can be used in sales document for reporting and pricing calculation. You may have different product hierarchies that are applicable on different dates. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate for each sales organization whether the document creation date, or document pricing date is relevant for product hierarchy determination.
questions.question: Will you be using product hierarchy for sales pricing? If so, please indicate for each sales organization whether the document creation date or document pricing date is relevant for the hierarchy determination.

questions.topicDefinition: For availability checking, SAP uses a concept of available-to-promise (ATP). In addition to the physical stock currently on hand, the ATP can be configured to include or exclude planned future stock receipts and issues, safety stock, quality inspection stock, stock in transfer and other parameters. How the system calculates possible delivery dates to customers are can also be adjusted here, to include or exclude purchase orders etc. with or without a lead time applied.
questions.question: Do you consider different factors such as stock committed to other orders, stock in restricted status, safety stock, and stock due to be received at a later date when determining stock available to offer to customers? If so, please describe these scenarios

questions.topicDefinition: Advanced available to promise enables additional functionality to the standard ATP check, including backorder processing, product allocation checking, and release for delivery logic. This Configuration Activity can be used to enable this additional functionality to be used.
questions.question: For materials which have may have limited availability at a point in time, do you choose to prioritize certain customers or sales locations over others when determining stock availability? Do you accept backorders?

questions.topicDefinition: Delivery priorities are used to prioritize the delivery of sales order items. This Configuration Activity allows you to define more delivery priority categories which can then be assigned to customers on their master data. A customer with a delivery priority of 1 will get priority delivery over a customer with delivery priority of 2.
questions.question: Do you give priority for orders/deliveries to certain customers or groups of customers on a regular basis? The SAP Starter System comes with three delivery priorities, 1 - High, 2 - Medium and 3 - Low that can be assigned in customer master. Please advise if you want to edit these descriptions or create more Delivery Priority categories.

questions.topicDefinition: Pricing is used to automatically arrive at a specific price for customers under different circumstances. Condition types are the elements of that final price. So for example, if the final price was calculated based on: Base Item Price - Customer % Discount - Fixed Material Discount + Freight Charge + Government Tax, then each of these 5 elements would be a different condition type.
questions.question: Please describe the elements that make up your pricing process. For each element, please stipulate whether it is a price, discount, surcharge or tax. Please also indicate whether each element is calculated on a percentage, quantity or other basis.

questions.topicDefinition:
A pricing procedure is the logic used to determine the final price of an item or service. It stipulates the condition types that are evaluated, the order in which they are evaluated, and the relationship between the pricing elements such as the subtotals that are to be calculated.

If for example, tax is calculated in one country on subtotal of pricing elements A + B, and in another country it is calculated on the basis of pricing elements B + C, then you may achieve this with different pricing procedures.
questions.question: Do you require a different pricing logic to be used in different circumstances? If so, please describe the different pricing flows you anticipate and their pricing elements.

questions.topicDefinition: A customer pricing procedure can be assigned to a customer in their master data. This can then be used to determine which pricing procedure will be used to determine the final price in a sales document. E.g. If you create three customer pricing procedures 01, 02 and 03, then each of these can be assigned to different customers and used to determine different pricing procedures in the sales document.
questions.question: Do you determine the pricing logic to be applied to a document partially on the basis of customer? If so, please describe the various customer groupings used.

questions.topicDefinition: If you have different pricing procedures, you can define which combination of sales area, document pricing procedure and customer pricing procedure should tell the system to use which overall pricing procedure.
questions.question: If you have multiple pricing procedures, please describe in which circumstances each one should be used.

questions.topicDefinition: It is possible that a customer and material combination fills the requirements for multiple discounts or surcharges. In this case, the multiple results might be added together to give the customer a bigger total discount or surcharge than desired. If you want to prevent this, you can define condition exclusion groups into which you classify various pricing elements, and finally stipulate which of these groupings of price elements are not allowed to occur at the same time. This Configuration Activity allows you to define the different groups of pricing elements whose interaction you will define later.
questions.question: Do you have pricing elements that should not be permitted to occur together? If so, please describe these pricing elements and their relationships.

questions.configRef: Assign Condition Types to Exclusion Groups
questions.topicDefinition:
It is possible that a customer and material combination fills the requirements for multiple discounts or surcharges. In this case, the multiple results might be added together to give the customer a bigger total discount or surcharge than desired. If you want to prevent this, you can define condition exclusion groups into which you classify various pricing elements, and finally stipulate which of these groupings of price elements are not allowed to occur at the same time.

This Configuration Activity allows you to assign specific condition types to the exclusion groups you have defined.
questions.question: Do you have pricing elements that should not be permitted to occur together? If so, please describe these pricing elements and their relationships.

questions.configRef: Maintain Condition Exclusion for Pricing Procedures
questions.topicDefinition: Your condition exclusion groups can be set to apply only to certain pricing procedures. This Configuration Activity allows you to define in which pricing procedures the condition exclusion groups should be active.
questions.question: Please describe to which pricing procedures the condition exclusion groups you defined should be applied.

questions.topicDefinition:
This Configuration Activity allows you to define custom requirements to be applied to your pricing logic. For example, you may define a requirement which says that a particular pricing condition for a country-specific tax is only considered if the Ship-To party has a particular destination-country.
These requirements may be applied at a header or item level.
questions.question: Please review the standard requirements delivered in the starter system in the pricing procedure definition area. If you require additional pricing requirements, please provide details on the logic to be defined.

questions.configRef: Set Alternative Calculation of Condition Amount
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity is a component that allows you to use custom logic to define different ways in which the system might calculate a condition amount. In this Configuration Activity, you define an identifier for the calculation logic, and assign a BaDI logic previously defined to that identifier.
questions.question: Do you require custom formula calculation logic beyond what is available with the pre-delivered system? If so, please describe the requirement.

questions.configRef: Set Alternative Calculation of Condition Base Value
questions.topicDefinition: You may use a custom routine to enable the system to calculate the base value of a condition in a way not provided by the standard system. For example, you could use this to have the system determine the base value used by a condition as net volume of the order. This Configuration Activity allows you to define and assign a routine that may be used in calculating a condition's base value.
questions.question: Do you need to calculate condition base values in ways not provided by the standard system? If so, please describe the condition and the values that are used as its base.

questions.configRef: Edit List of Fields Used in Pricing Routines
questions.topicDefinition: When using a custom routine, various document fields may be a part of that calculation. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which document fields should be considered in your custom routine.
questions.question: Are you using custom requirements for pricing logic? If so, please list the document fields  that will be used in your pricing routine.

questions.configRef: Set Price List Types for Customers
questions.topicDefinition: You can define different pricing lists that can be assigned to customers in their master data. These price lists can be used to define different prices or rates in various pricing elements. E.g. One might maintain separate price lists for Corporate and Private customers to stipulate that a material has a base price of 10£ for corporate customers and 8$ for private customers. The price list can be used in conjunction with customer price group.
questions.question: Do you maintain different price lists that should be applied to specific customers? If so, please list and describe each.

questions.topicDefinition: You can define different pricing groups into which customers can be classified. These groupings can then be used to maintain different rates in each condition type. E.g. If you defined customer price groups Gold, Silver and Bronze, then these groups could be used in a discount condition type to stipulate that Gold customers get a 5% discount, Silver customers a 4% discount and Bronze customers get a 3% discount.
questions.question: Do you have different groupings of customers that determines what pricing rate they are eligible for in any specific pricing element? If so, please list and describe these groups.

questions.topicDefinition: You can define different pricing groups into which materials can be classified. These groupings can then be used to maintain different rates in each condition type. E.g. If material price groups 'Luxury' and 'Standard' were defined, these two groups could be used to determine surcharge rates of 5% and 3% respectively.
questions.question: Do you group materials into clusters that determine what pricing rate is applied in any specific pricing element? If so, please list and describe these groups.

questions.topicDefinition:
The field catalog is the list of fields that are available to be used in pricing determination. For example, the standard fields Sales Organization and Material are a part of the field catalog, and so these can be used in pricing condition tables.
This Configuration Activity allows you to add custom fields to the sales field catalogs.
questions.question: Are you using custom fields in your sales process that will also be a part of pricing conditions? If so, please describe the custom fields that should be included in the field catalog.

questions.topicDefinition:
Each pricing element that is a part of the pricing procedure is determined based on a condition table. The condition table is composed of multiple levels of field-combinations. For example, you could have a discount pricing element be determined based on up to three levels: 1) Sales Group-Customer-Material 2) Sales Group-Material and 3) Material where each of these levels corresponds to a condition table that has been defined in the system.
This Configuration Activity allows you to create new condition tables.
questions.question: Please review the available tables for condition types that you will utilize. If new combinations are required, please detail which field combinations are required.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to update description of existing custom condition tables. Standard table descriptions cannot be modified.
questions.question: If you require an update to the description of any existing custom condition table, please provide the revised description for each.

questions.topicDefinition: An access sequence is a search strategy that the system uses to search for valid condition records of a certain condition type. For example, you can define for a price that the system first searches for a customer-specific price and then for a price-list price. This Configuration Activity allows you to define a new access sequence that could then be assigned as the search strategy to be used in a condition type.
questions.question: Please review the starter system pre-delivered access sequence for examples. Do you require a custom access sequence to be assigned to a condition type for pricing determination? If so, please describe the tables that should be checked as a part of the access sequence.

questions.topicDefinition:
The system is pre-delivered with country specific tax codes. For each of these tax codes, there are defined possible customer tax classifications. For example, for the TTX1 tax category (DE relevant), the standard system has customer classifications: 1 - Liable for taxes and 2 - EU-Consumer in the pre-delivered system.
This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the descriptions for the various customer tax classifications.
questions.question: If you require a change to the standard description for the various customer tax classification values, please provide the new descriptions. Character Limit = 20.

questions.topicDefinition:
The system is pre-delivered with country specific tax codes. For each of these tax codes, there are defined possible material tax classifications. For example, for the TTX1 tax category (DE relevant), the standard system has customer classifications: 1 - Full tax and 2 - Reduced Tax in the pre-delivered system.
This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the descriptions for the various material tax classifications.
questions.question: If you require a change to the standard description for the various material tax classification values, please provide the new descriptions. Character Limit = 20.

questions.configRef: Maintain Determination of Value-Added Tax Registration Number
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to choose amongst various options for how the system determines what business partner VAT number to determine in a sales document. With this Configuration Activity you may choose the standard system determination, or choose the setting so that VAT is always determined based on the sold to party, payer, or ship-to party.
questions.question: Please review the configuration help for this SSCUI in the starter system, which describes the standard system logic for determining VAT ID on sales documents. If you require a different option to be selected, please indicate whether VAT should be determined based on sold-to, party, payer or ship-to.

questions.topicDefinition: Customers can be assigned to an account assignment group in their master data, and this can be used as a part of the logic in determining which GL account a pricing element is posted to. E.g. Customers could be classified as domestic, export or intercompany if different GL postings should be made on this customer classification basis.
questions.question: Do you determine the GL account that pricing elements such as discounts, surcharges or revenues are posted to on the basis of different material classifications? If so, please describe those different material classifications.

questions.topicDefinition: Customers can be assigned to an account assignment group in their master data, and this can be used as a part of the logic in determining which GL account a pricing element is posted to. E.g. Customers could be classified as domestic, export or intercompany if different GL postings should be made on this customer classification basis.
questions.question: Do you determine the GL account that pricing elements such as discounts, surcharges or revenues are posted to on the basis of different customer classifications? If so, please describe those different customer classifications.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define the access sequences that are used in automatic revenue account determination.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered access sequences in your starter system in preparation to discuss your revenue account determination requirements.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define the account determination types that are used in automatic revenue account determination.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered settings in your starter system in preparation to discuss your revenue account determination requirements.

questions.topicDefinition:
An account key can be used alone, or in combination with other master data elements to determine the G/L account that is posted to. E.g. SAP default account keys are Revenue, Output Tax and Sales Deductions
This Configuration Activity allows you to define additional account keys that can be used in GL account determination
questions.question: Do you wish to define any new account keys to be used as part of the G/L account number determination? If so, please describe these account groupings.

questions.configRef: Define Sales and Distribution Access Sequences
questions.topic: Batch Determination for Sales and Distribution
questions.topicDefinition:
If the products that you sell are managed in batches, then you can define via configuration how the system can automatically determine the batches to be proposed in a sales order. 
The Access sequence defined in this Configuration Activity controls which table-combinations you can use to differentiate between the batch determination strategy used in different cases. For example, if for a specific customer-material combination, you select batches on a FIFO basis, whereas for every other case the batch strategy varies between FIFO and Expiration date  basis depending on the material being sold, then the standard SD01 access sequence with 1) Customer-Material and 2) Material, allows you to stipulate for which customer-material combinations the FIFO strategy is used, and then for all other cases, you stipulate per material whether FIFO or Expiration date search criteria is used.
questions.question: Please review the standard access sequences provided in the starter system. If you determine which batch search strategy is used in your sales orders on different basis than the standard, please describe the logic you follow in each different case here.

questions.configRef: Define Sales and Distribution Strategy Types
questions.topic: Batch Determination for Sales and Distribution
questions.topicDefinition: Different 'Strategy Types' for batch determination can be defined with this Configuration Activity. A strategy type can be configured to select batches on a first in first out basis, or based on expiration date. The strategy type can also be assigned an access sequence to control in which sales scenarios this strategy is applied.
questions.question: Please review the standard batch search strategy types in the starter system. If you require additional search strategies, please describe each one including whether batches are selected on a first-in-first-out basis, or expiration date basis.

questions.configRef: Define Sales and Distribution Search Procedure
questions.topic: Batch Determination for Sales and Distribution
questions.topicDefinition:
A batch search procedure is composed of multiple search strategies. So, for example, the standard search procedure defined in the starter system YB0001 stipulates that first the YB11 - FIFO based search strategy is used, and then if no result is found with that strategy then next the YB12 - Expiration date based strategy is used.
This Configuration Activity allows you to create or modify existing search procedures and indicate which batch search strategy should be used in which order.
questions.question: Please describe the order in which you  want the different batch search strategies you have defined to be applied for each sales area and sales document item type.

questions.topic: Batch Determination for Sales and Distribution
questions.topicDefinition: With this Configuration Activity, you can specify for each Sales Area + Sales order type, which batch search procedure is used. For example, you could define that for 'Free Goods' sales order type, an expiration-date batch search procedure is used, while for a 'Standard Order' in the same sales area, a first-in-first-out strategy is used.
questions.question: Please list the batch search procedure to be used for each sales area + sales document type combination.

questions.configRef: Activate Automatic Batch Determination for Sales Order Item Categories
questions.topic: Batch Determination for Sales and Distribution
questions.topicDefinition: Depending on the sales order type and material type you are using, an Item Category is determined for each order line item. For example, on a standard order for a stock material the TAN item category is determined, while for a free of charge order and a stock material the item category CBXN is determined. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate for each item category, whether or not automatic batch determination should be carried out in the sales order.
questions.question: Do you only want automatic batch determination to be carried out on the sales order? If so, please describe the types of materials and transactions in which sales order automatic batch determination should occur.

questions.configRef: Activate Automatic Batch Determination for Delivery Item Categories
questions.topic: Batch Determination for Sales and Distribution
questions.topicDefinition: Depending on the delivery type and item you are using, an Item Category is determined for each order line item. For example, on a standard order for a stock material the TAN item category is determined, while for a free of charge order and a stock material the item category CBXN is determined. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate for each item category, whether or not automatic batch determination should be carried out in the delivery.
questions.question: Do you only want automatic batch determination to be carried out on the delivery? If so, please describe the types of deliveries in which automatic batch determination should occur.

questions.topicDefinition: Billing document type controls processing of billing documents such as invoices, credit and debit memos as well as cancellation documents. You can use billing document types to deal with the different business transactions carried out during billing processing. Using this Configuration Activity, you can change the description of the Billing Document Types.
questions.question: Please evaluate the descriptions of the Billing Document Types in Starter System and advise if you would like to change any.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to edit the description that is assigned to specific Language, Tax Procedure and Tax Code combinations. When this combination is being outputted on a billing document because of the tax procedure, customer and material being sold,  the description you provide here will be shown.
questions.question: If you require changes to the printed descriptions of legal tax codes and rates being applied in your sales process, please specify the revised description needed in each case.

questions.configRef: Maintain the Milestone Billing Plan Type
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate whether the billing plan is controlled by the creation date of the order, the contract start date, or other parameters. You may also change the default description of the Milestone Billing type.
questions.question: Will you use milestone billing? If so, indicate the basis on which the start and end of the milestone billing plan will be based.

questions.topicDefinition: When creating billing documents for a milestone billing plan, the date descriptions selected in your billing plan will show on the output. This is useful for describing the activity that was completed and is being billed. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the description of the pre-delivered milestone billing date descriptions, as well as define new ones.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered milestone billing date descriptions in the starter system. If you require modifications to these descriptions, or require new date description options, please provide that list.

questions.configRef: Maintain Date Categories for Milestone Billing Plans
questions.topicDefinition: The date category selected for your milestone billing plan will trigger a date description, as well as the type of delivery and billing blocks to be put on the document if the milestones are not met. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the date description, as well as indicate which delivery and billing block indicator assigned to each available date category.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered date category combinations in the starter system. If you require adjustments to the default combinations, please advise which assignments should be changed for each date category.

questions.configRef: Copying Control: Sales Document to Billing Document
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to control how pricing elements, the exchange rate, and the reference number is handled when you create a new sales document with reference to a pre-existing billing document for pre-defined Billing Document, Sales Document and Item Category combinations. You may also indicate whether a custom data transfer routine is used for this combination.
questions.question: Please review the standard settings for copying between billing document and sales document types you use. If you require changes to any available options, please list the required changes.

questions.configRef: Copying Control: Delivery Document to Billing Document
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to control how pricing elements, the exchange rate, and the reference number is handled when you create a new billing document with reference to a pre-existing delivery document. For the pre-defined Delivery Document, Billing Document and Item Category combinations, you may also indicate whether a custom data transfer routine is used.
questions.question: Please review the standard settings for copying between delivery document and billing  document types you use. If you require changes to any available options, please list the required changes.

questions.configRef: Copying Control: Billing Document to Billing Document
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to control how pricing elements, the exchange rate, and the reference number is handled when you create a new billing document with reference to a pre-existing delivery document. For the pre-defined Delivery Document, Billing Document and Item Category combinations, you may also indicate whether a custom data transfer routine is used.
questions.question: Please review the standard settings for copying between billing document types. If you require changes to any available options, please list the required changes.

questions.configRef: Define Custom Routines for Data Transfer to Billing Documents
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define a custom routine that can be called to determine the logic the system should use when transferring data to the billing document from reference documents.
questions.question: Do you require custom logic to be applied to determine the data that is transferred to your billing document from predecessor documents? If so, please describe the different routines to be defined.

questions.configRef: Define Number Ranges for Billing Documents
questions.topicDefinition:
When a billing document is saved, it may be assigned an automatic number. These numbers must be within an allowed range of numbers that are defined in this Configuration Activity. This Configuration Activity allows you to define  the number ranges for billing documents. Also, you can use this Configuration Activity to define number ranges with a prefix in the step 'Define Number Range Prefixes for Billing Document' (103283).
Please note that there is a system restriction to define prefix characters up to 5 digits only. The number range including the prefix has a total limit of 10 digits.
questions.question: If you require a modification to the pre-delivered number ranges assigned to preliminary billing documents and billing documents, please indicate the number ranges to be assigned to each.

questions.configRef: Define Number Range Prefixes for Billing Document
questions.topicDefinition:
This Configuration Activity allows you to define various number range prefixes to be assigned to your billing document before the automatically generated number. For example, you could define a prefix 'US' that is applied to all billing documents in the US company code if you include this logic as a part of your custom routine.
Please note that there is a system restriction to define prefix characters up to 5 digits only. The number range including the prefix has a total limit of 10 digits.
questions.question: Do you require custom logic to be applied to determine the billing document numbering the system should apply to your billing documents? If so, please describe the prefixes that should be assigned to the different scenarios.

questions.configRef: Define Parameter Catalog Entries for Flexible Billing Document Numbering
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate what header custom fields can be considered in flexible billing document numbering logic.
questions.question: Do you need to use custom fields as a part of the logic in determining the billing document number to be assigned? If so, please indicate which header-level custom fields will be a part of the flexible billing document determination.

questions.configRef: Define Formulas for Flexible Billing Document Numbering
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define the formula to be used in determining the billing document number. For example, you can indicate that Company Code and Billing Document Type should both be considered. You can also indicate the priority in which parameters are considered, and define the logic as to when each number range is determined.
questions.question: If you are using flexible billing document determination logic, please indicate which number range and prefix should be determined in each separate situation.

questions.configRef: Define Custom Routines for Flexible Billing Document Numbering
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define a custom routine that can be called to determine the logic the system should use when determining the billing document number and prefix to assign to the billing document. This is a prerequisite for other configurations that must be completed to utilize the flexible billing document numbering functionality. You may stipulate which routine should be called for each different billing document type.
questions.question: Do you require custom logic to be applied to determine the billing document numbering the system should apply to your billing documents? If so, please define the custom routines that will be required for this purpose.

questions.configRef: Define Process Enhancements According to Billing Type
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to assign the custom routine number for flexible billing to be used for each different billing document type.
questions.question: If you will utilize flexible billing document logic and have defined custom routines, please indicate which billing document types should consider which custom routine.

questions.topicDefinition:
You may define groups into which you can classify customers on their master data. For example, you may create different groups for Wholesale, Retail and Government customers. These groupings can be used to control pricing, analytics, and authorizations.

This Configuration Activity allows you to update the description of customer groups created in the organizational structure.
questions.question: Do you define multiple customer groups for pricing or reporting purposes? If so, please describe the various groups.

questions.topicDefinition:
You can define a set of customer classifications that can be assigned to customers in their master data. This classification can be used for some reports and product allocation logic. For example, you can classify customers as A,B or C ranking. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the description of existing classification groups A, B and C, or to define new classification groups.
questions.question: Do you classify customers into separate groups that are used to determine priority when determining product allocation? If so, please provide a list of your customer categories and describe how you handle the customers differently according to this classification.

questions.topicDefinition: A Sales District is defined as a geographical district or sales region. With this Configuration Activity, you can define sales districts that you can assign to customers and use in analytics or reporting. For example, US sales districts might be defined as Southeast, Northeast, Northwest etc.
questions.question: Please define the different sales districts that you would want to identify separately in your sales reports.

questions.configRef: Assign Department Numbers for Contact Person
questions.topicDefinition: You may assign contact persons to your customers in their master data. The contact person that is assigned can be allocated to a department, such as the Financial Department (0009), Legal Department (0010) etc. This Configuration Activity allows you to map the department code you assign to contact persons in your business partner master data to department codes that may have existed in customer vendor integration.
questions.question: Please review the default mapping in the starter system. If you require a new mapping of department number IDs, please provide information here.

questions.topicDefinition: You may assign contact persons to your customers in their master data. The contact person that is assigned can be allocated to a function, such as the Executive Board (0001), or Purchasing Manager (0002) etc. This Configuration Activity allows you to map the function code you assign to contact persons in your business partner master data to department codes that may have existed in customer vendor integration.
questions.question: Please review the default mapping in the starter system. If you require a new mapping of department number IDs, please provide information here.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to map the authority assignment for business partners to authority assignment of customer contact person.
questions.question: Please review the default mapping in the starter system, and provide a revised mapping if required.

questions.configRef: Assign VIP Indicator for Contact Person
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to map the VIP Indicator for the business partner to the VIP Indicator for the contact person in the customer master record.
questions.question: Please review the default mapping in the starter system, and provide a revised mapping if required.

questions.topicDefinition:
Business Partners such as customers can be assigned to an authorization group in their master data. This Configuration Activity allows you to define additional Authorization Groups that can be assigned to customers.
