These authorization groups can then be used to restrict access to business partner information for specific business roles. For example, you could stipulate that users with access to authorization group 0001 can edit business partners,  while users who only have access to authorization group 0002 cannot edit business partners in group BUPA.
Please note that the BUPA object group refers to general business partner master data, while the CUST object group refers to sales area specific customer data.
questions.question: Please review the standard Business Partner Group and Authorization Group combinations in the starter system. If you need to change description of any of these combinations, or define new authorization groups for more authorization group combinations, please describe the additional combinations required.

questions.topicDefinition:
When creating a business partner, you can select which business partner grouping you are assigning the customer to. Each business partner grouping is assigned to an 'account group', that controls the screens and fields that are mandatory to be entered. This Configuration Activity allows you to assign each business partner grouping to either the standard customer, or one-time customer account group. 

You can also use this Configuration Activity for each business partner grouping to indicate whether or not the same numbering is retained for other functions.
questions.question: For each type of business partner that you manage, for example suppliers, customers and contacts - please describe how numbering should be handled for each grouping. Please indicate whether for the same entity that acts in multiple roles (e.g. as a customer and a supplier), whether the business partner number assigned in each case should be the same or different.

questions.configRef: Set BP Role Category for Direction BP to Customer
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define which business partner role categories are synchronized in the direction from the business partner to the customer.
questions.question: The starter system defines a mandatory synchronization of the Customer role from Business Partner to Customer. If you require modifications to these settings, please advise which additional business partner roles you need to synchronize.

questions.topicDefinition: Number ranges indicate the range of numbers or letters that can be used per grouping. The number range group can be assigned to a business partner group, and the business partner group is assigned to a business partner on creation. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the pre-delivered number ranges, stipulating what range of numbers or alphanumeric characters can be assigned to the various business partner groups. You can also stipulate here whether the number is automatically (internally) determined, or manually (externally) assigned by the user.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered number ranges in the starter system. Please advise the revised ranges or internal/external control if required.

questions.configRef: Define Groupings and Assign Number Ranges
questions.topicDefinition: When you create a business partner, you assign them to a business partner grouping. This Configuration Activity allows you to assign each business partner grouping to the number ranges and number range control types you have defined.
questions.question: Please review the predefined business partner grouping and number range allocation in the starter system. Please advise if you require different number range assignments for these business partner groupings.

questions.configRef: Set Up Partner Determination for Customer Master
questions.topicDefinition: There may be various business partner roles that are relevant to your business. For example, in a sales process you may deal with the sold-to party buying the goods, a freight forwarder who is delivering the goods, a related sales representative etc. With this Configuration Activity, you can stipulate the various business roles that are relevant to your customers.
questions.question: Please review the standard partner roles configured in the starter system, and describe any additional business partner roles that may be a part of your sales process.

questions.configRef: Set Up Partner Determination for Sales Document Header
questions.topicDefinition:
You can stipulate that various types of business partner roles must be on a sales order. For example, you could stipulate that in addition to the standard sold-to, ship-to, bill-to and payer parties, a sales document must have an employee responsible assigned.
This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which business partner roles are allowed, and are mandatory on a sales document header.
questions.question: Do you require the same business partner roles, such as ship-to party, supplier, on all of your sales order types? Which business partner roles are a) possible and b) mandatory, in your different sales scenarios?

questions.configRef: Set Up Partner Determination for Delivery
questions.topicDefinition:
You can stipulate that various types of business partner roles must be on a delivery document. For example, you could stipulate that in addition to the standard ship-to party, a relevant supplier must be included.
This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which business partner roles are allowed, and are mandatory on a delivery document type.
questions.question: Do you require business partner roles besides the ship-to party to be included on delivery documents?

questions.configRef: Set Up Partner Determination for Billing Header
questions.topicDefinition:
You can stipulate that various types of business partner roles must be on a billing document. For example, you could stipulate that in addition to the standard sold to party, a relevant employee responsible must be included.
This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which business partner roles are allowed, and are mandatory on a billing document type.
questions.question: Do you require business partner roles besides the sold-to party, bill-to party, or payer to be included on customer billing documents?

questions.configRef: Set Up Text Determination for Customer Master
questions.topicDefinition: In SAP, you may maintain various types of text notes that you attach these to your business partner. For example, you may maintain an Accounting Note to record special accounting instructions, and a Delivery Note for delivery related instructions for that customer e.g. 'Deliver between 09:00 and 11:00' etc. In this Configuration Activity, you can assign which text types are available to be maintained on the customer master.
questions.question: What different types of notes about customers do you need to maintain?

questions.configRef: Set Up Text Determination for Sales Document Header
questions.topicDefinition:
Parties to a sales transaction often exchange various instructions and information during the course of the sales process. This information could be in the form of shipping instructions, packing instructions, delivery terms, remarks maintained by the partner’s agent, and so on. In SAP, you maintain all this information as Text which can be stored in various places including different business partner roles. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to determine what types of texts are available on a sales document header, and where the text comes from.
questions.question: Please describe what sorts of texts you need to be maintained in a sales order header. For each of these texts, please indicate which business partner role it should come from.

questions.configRef: Set Up Text Determination for Delivery Header
questions.topicDefinition:
Parties to a sales transaction often exchange various instructions and information during the course of the sales process. This information could be in the form of shipping instructions, packing instructions, delivery terms, remarks maintained by the partner’s agent, and so on. In SAP, you maintain all this information as Text which can be stored in various places including different business partner roles. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to determine what types of texts are available on a delivery document header, and where the text comes from. Texts on a delivery document may be determined from various business partner roles, from the preceding sales document, or maintained manually.
questions.question: Are there any customer specific texts or comments which should be included on shipping documents? Are these added manually per order or if they should be determined automatically, please describe the source for this information.

questions.configRef: Set Up Text Determination for Billing Header
questions.topicDefinition:
Parties to a sales transaction often exchange various instructions and information during the course of the sales process. This information could be in the form of shipping instructions, packing instructions, delivery terms, remarks maintained by the partner’s agent, and so on. In SAP, you maintain all this information as Text which can be stored in various places including different business partner roles. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to determine what types of texts are available on a billing document header, and where the text comes from. Texts on a billing document may be determined from various business partner roles, from the preceding sales document, or maintained manually.
questions.question: Are there any customer specific texts or comments which should be included on billing documents? Are these added manually per order or if they should be determined automatically, please describe the source for this information.

questions.configRef: Set Up Text Determination for Sales Document Item
questions.topicDefinition:
Parties to a sales transaction often exchange various instructions and information during the course of the sales process. This information could be in the form of shipping instructions, packing instructions, delivery terms, remarks maintained by the partner’s agent, and so on. In SAP, you maintain all this information as Text which can be stored in various places including different business partner roles. 

This Configuration Activity allows you to determine what types of texts are available on sales document at the line item level and where the text comes from.
questions.question: Are there any customer specific texts or comments which should be included on sales order line items? Are these added manually per order or if they should be determined automatically, please describe the source for this information.

questions.topicDefinition: A payment card plan controls how the sales document will be settled for payment. This Configuration Activity allows you to assign the payment plan type to all sales document types in which you will be using payment cards. Only sales documents assigned a payment card plan type here will have the payment card functionality enabled.
questions.question: The standard system contains payment plan type 93 for processing payment cards. In the Starter System, an assignment of Payment Card Plan type has been made to sales document types. Please advise if you require changes to these assignments.

questions.topicDefinition:
For each payment card type, you can define a period in days for which the authorization will remain valid. 
This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate the number of days for which the authorization is to remain valid. At the end of this period, the authorized amount will expire, and you will have to carry out a fresh authorization check for the sales order.
questions.question: Please review the standard assignment of authorization days in the starter system and provide a revised number of days required for your business for each payment card type.

questions.topicDefinition:
Checking Groups control how SAP checks payment card data before authorization. Checking groups define custom routine checks, authorization horizons, and validity.
This Configuration Activity allows you to define additional checking groups that can then be assigned to specific sales document types where payment cards should be enabled.
questions.question: If you require additional payment checking groups, please indicate the number and description for each new group.

questions.topicDefinition:
Checking Groups control how SAP checks payment card data before authorization. Checking groups define custom routine checks, authorization horizons, and validity.
This Configuration Activity allows you to assign a checking group to sales document types in which payment cards should be enabled.
questions.question: In the Starter System, 01 is the standard Checking Group that has been assigned to relevant sales document types. Please review these settings and advise if you require changes.

questions.topicDefinition:
During an intercompany sales process, where both companies
are processed in the same system (& client), the supplying company generates an intercompany invoice made out to the ordering company. Automatic posting to vendor account is done by SAP Electronic Data Interchange (EDI).  Using this app, you can generate the EDI configuration that the system uses to post this invoice to the ordering company code. Also, the system automatically generates the corresponding payables in the ordering company's accounts.
questions.question: Do you have intercompany trading between your legal entities where one legal entity provides stock to a customer on behalf of the other? Do you require automatic reconciliation of accounts? Please describe the selling and receiving company relationships to be activated.

questions.configRef: Assign Customer/Supplier to Sales Organization Data
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to assign a customer or supplier to a specific sales organization, sales area, sales order type etc. These values can then be used when that customer or supplier are used in B2B scenarios.
questions.question: Will you be using EDI communications with an external SAP system for B2B scenarios? If so, stipulate which customers and suppliers should use specific sales area data for this purpose.

questions.configRef: Convert External to Internal Partner Numbers
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define a mapping between S/4HANA Cloud customers (using an external system), and that customer's external partners.
questions.question: Do you need to have a mapping between customers in the S/4HANA Cloud system, and their external partners for different partner functions? If so, please detail the mappings to be created. Note that this activity must be re-configured in the P-system.

questions.configRef: Define Mapping for Inbound Texts for Integration with Buyers
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to map XML tagged fields from external buyer systems to particular text fields in S4HC so that information from their purchase requests can be replicated in the S4HC sales order. For example, with this Configuration Activity you can define a mapping between the item-level Material Text in the XML document, and the Material Sales text on the relevant sales document.
questions.question: Will you be receiving electronic messages from customers with text information that needs to be replicated in your sales order? If so, please review the available text object mappings available in the starter system, and indicate which mappings will be required in your system.

questions.configRef: Define Mapping for Outbound Texts for Integration with Buyers
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to map billing document texts in your system at header or item level to one of the predefined XML types. This predefined XML type can then be mapped in the receivers system so they can import the text to the desired text field in their purchasing document.
questions.question: Will you be sending electronic messages with billing document information from this system to an external supplier system? If so, and if you need to transmit billing document texts to the external system, please detail the required assignments.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to create new activity reason codes to be assigned to settlement documents or document cancellations.
questions.question: Do you report on reasons for rebate settlement, or the reason for cancelling rebate settlements? If so, please describe the reasons for settlement or reversal that you track.

questions.topicDefinition: A number of different settlement document types are defined  to classify different settlement processes in settlement management. For example, 0S12 - Sales Rebate Credit is defined in the starter system. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify the description of these settlement document types.
questions.question: Please review the settlement document types and their descriptions in the starter system. If you would like to revise the descriptions of any of these settlement document types, please provide the settlement document ID and the revised description.

questions.topicDefinition: A number of settlement process types are defined for  settlement management in the starter system. For example, OS40 - Sales Rebate Delta Accruals. This Configuration Activity allows you to update the description of these process types.
questions.question: Please review the settlement process types and their descriptions in the starter system. If you would like to revise the descriptions of any of these process types, please provide the settlement process ID and the revised description.

questions.configRef: Sales Rebate - Configure Condition Contract Types and Settlement Settings
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to create new condition contract types for rebate settlements. For each new condition contract type, you must specify the settings related to the various permitted combinations of settlement date type, settlement type and handling of the reversal of partial settlement.
questions.question: Please review the contract condition types in the starter system, and the settlement settings related to the contract condition types. If you require additional contract types, please describe them here along with their related settlement settings.

questions.configRef: Specify Pricing Procedures for Settlement Documents / Settlement Doc Lists
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to determine different settlement pricing procedures based on a number of factors such as the country code of the relevant business partner, the customer pricing procedure, or purchasing organization in the case of suppliers.
questions.question: If you have multiple pricing procedures to be used for rebates, please describe in which circumstances each one should be used.

questions.configRef: Specify Partner Functions to Identify External Sales Agents
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define the partner functions that will be used to identify which documents are considered for commissions. Only documents with a partner function defined here will be in scope when the settlement run for business volume determination is carried out.
questions.question: A standard partner function is pre-delivered with the system for External Sales Agent. If you require additional functions, please provide a listing.

questions.configRef: Purchasing Rebate – Configure Condition Contract Types and Settle. Settings
questions.topicDefinition: SAP delivers a number of contract types with various settlement settings to be used when settling a sales commission rebate. This Configuration Activity allows you to create new custom contract types with different settings by creating a copy of a pre-delivered combination, and making changes to the settlement settings as needed.
questions.question: If you require non-standard contract processes, please provide the codes, description, approval requirements and grouping for these new process variants.

questions.topicDefinition:
This Configuration Activity allows you to define new contract process variants, and assign them to the pre-delivered contract types.
You may also stipulate whether a process variant is applicable system-wide, or whether it is sales organization specific.
questions.question: If you require non-standard contract processes, please provide the codes, description, approval requirements and grouping for these new process variants.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define different material rebate groups. These may then be assigned to materials in their master data, and used for grouping and calculations for rebate settlement.
questions.question: Do you use groupings of materials to determine rebate pricing or settlement? If so, please provide a code and description of each material rebate group you wish to define.

questions.configRef: Define Instructions for Planning Delivery Schedules
questions.topicDefinition: The instruction for planning delivery schedule contains the set of characteristics that control how planning delivery schedules are created. This Configuration Activity allows you to create, copy, change, and delete instructions for planning delivery schedule.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered delivery instructions in the starter system. If you require additional instructions to be set up, please indicate the settings required for each.

questions.configRef: Define Splitting Rules for Delivery Schedules
questions.topicDefinition: Splitting rules are used to define the proportion by which weekly or monthly schedule lines in a forecast delivery schedule are split into more manageable units (daily schedule lines). Daily schedule lines are then copied to the planning delivery schedule for requirement planning. This Configuration Activity allows you to create, copy, change, and delete splitting rules. For example, with pre-delivered splitting rule SD1, the system will split the schedule line into three parts such that one third is split to Monday, another third for Wednesday, and the final third for Friday.
questions.question: Please review the pre-delivered splitting rules. If you require modifications to existing splitting rules, or new splitting rules to be defined, please describe the  required values.

questions.topicDefinition: Since you can assign several splitting rules to an instruction, you define a date type and splitting rule range for each splitting rule. Based on the splitting rule ranges, the system determines different time periods. For example, based on the pre-delivered combination of Date Type 2, Range 8 and Splitting rule SD2: The system will take a weekly schedule line (date type 2) from the baseline date through 8 weeks, and split this based on the splitting rule defined with ID SD2.
questions.question: If you require additional splitting rule assignments beyond the pre-delivered combinations, please specify for both weekly and monthly date types the applicable ranges and splitting rules to be assigned in each case.

questions.configRef: Define Rules for Determination of Master Form Template
questions.topicDefinition: Master forms are used in Output documents such as Print, Emails, Fax, EDI. They include information like Company Logo, Company Address and Contact details. Some organizations might require different master forms for different entities. Using this activity, you can define rules that determine the master form template. This Configuration Activity allows you to define the rules that determine the master form template.
questions.question: In order to determine Master Forms, some parameters are available in SAP: Company Code, Organizational Units(Sales Organization, Purchasing Organization, Plant), Sender Country and Form Template. Keeping these parameters in mind please advise rules for determination of Master Form.

questions.topicDefinition: Standard SAP provides pre-delivered Content Form templates. These are application-specific output forms (e.g. form template for Sales Order Confirmation, form template for Purchase Order). These form templates can be customized to business's specific requirements. This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which Form Templates are available on specific output IDs.
questions.question: In the Starter System, please check the standard form templates that are assigned to specific combination of application objects and output types. Once you have created custom form templates, please assign to the relevant combination(s) of application objects and output types. It is possible to assign multiple Form Templates. When end users want to output a document, they can choose from the selection of form templates that you have assigned.

questions.topicDefinition:
With this activity you can ensure that business applications use the correct pre-delivered and custom email templates. You can check which standard email templates are assigned to specific application objects and output types. 
When end users want to output a document, they can choose from the selection of email templates that you have assigned to the respective application object and output type.

This Configuration Activity allows you to stipulate which email templates are available on which output type and application type combinations.
questions.question: Please review the standard e-mail template assignments to output types and application types. Please advise if you require modifications to this. If you have defined custom e-mail templates, they should be assigned to their allowed output types here.

questions.topicDefinition: Output channels are the different ways that an output can be generated: Example by E-mail, Print etc. This Configuration Activity allows you to view and modify the output channels allowed for various application and output type combinations.
questions.question: Please review the standard assignments of output channels to application and output types in the starter system. Advise if you require additional combinations or modifications to the existing assignments.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define one or more email domains from which emails can be sent. E.g.: sap.com would allow any email address in this domain, including email addresses from sub-domains such as sales.sap.com
questions.question: Please advise the default email sender domain for email communications from the system. One default sender domain is required. Organizational specific addresses can also be maintained.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to define a default sender address for emails in case the application did not determine a more specific sender address.
questions.question: Please provide a default sender address in case the application is not able to determine the sender address. E.g. Do_not_reply@sap.com.

questions.configRef: Define Email Receiver Addresses for Test Systems
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to specify a the email addresses or domains that can receive documents dispatched by test systems. This is useful if for example you want to test a dunning run in a test system but not send communications to your actual business partners.
questions.question:
Please provide receiver email addresses for test systems. The settings from this activity are only checked in test systems; no check is executed in the production system. E.g.: *@sap.com: would allow to send emails to all receivers in the domain sap.com.
123@sap.com: would allow to send emails to precisely this email address.

questions.topicDefinition: SAP provides functionality to define output message texts to be shown when changes occur to specified document attributes. This is done using message identifiers. For example, a pre-delivered combination in the starter system is that when you first save a complete sales order, the 'Order Confirmation' output type is generated. When the order is later modified, the 'Order_Confirmation_Change' is used to identify the changed output. This Configuration Activity allows you to modify which change output type is used for changes to original document types and enable/disable the storing of changed document types.
questions.question: Review the current message identifiers that are used for detecting changes to document attributes in the starter system. Please advise if you require modifications to the existing settings.

questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity is used define print message texts to be shown when changes occur to specified document attributes. You can also choose the language that the message will be translated into; this should match the language of the receivers expected to receive the output being issued for the sales documents.
questions.question: Please check the default messages available in the system and review if you need to add any custom message(s). Are they translated in additional languages? What is the default language to be selected if the translated message cannot be found for the language of the document receiver?

questions.configRef: Assign Message Texts to Table Fields
questions.topicDefinition:
Before an output for change document is generated, you must first define your message identifiers in order to detect changes in that business document. This Configuration Activity allows you to assign and change document output message identifiers to a specified table field combination. 

Depending on the group indicator defined for the message identifier, the message identifier will be assigned to either a single document attribute or a group of document attributes.
questions.question: Please review the standard settings for changed document customization. You can use any or all of the sample table field combinations and assigned message identifiers to show an appropriate message when a document attribute is changed. Or, you can create your own set of table field combinations and assign your own message identifiers.

questions.configRef: Assign Message Texts to Partner Table Fields
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to indicate which partner table field sales document outputs should refer to for message texts.
questions.question: Please review the starter system settings, and advise if you require modifications to the predefined message texts for partner fields.

questions.configRef: Assign Message Texts to Document Text Types
questions.topicDefinition: This Configuration Activity allows you to indicate from which table and field the message texts in sales documents should derive from.
questions.question: Please review the starter system settings, and advise if you require modifications to the predefined text derivation logic.

questions.topicDefinition: The rejection reasons are attached to the rejected time entries by the person approving the data. You can attach a comment line to time sheet data for which an approval is withheld. The comment line states the reason why the approval was withheld. In this step, you define the rejection reasons that the person approving the data can attach to a rejected record.
questions.question: Can you list all reject reasons for time entry  for various employee groups (such salary vs. hourly employee), work sites (front office, field services, warehouse, etc.),  projects, etc.?

questions.topicDefinition: A personnel area is a specific unit for personnel administration, and constitutes a subunit of the company code. The individual personnel areas of a company code are identified by a four-character alphanumeric code.
questions.question: Can you identify the legal employing entity  and the physical state of employment of  employees within each company code? List all those entities and locations.

questions.topicDefinition: A personnel subarea represents a subunit of the personnel area. It is at this level that the organizational control of pay scale structures, wage type structures, and work schedules occurs. A personnel subarea is identified by a four-character alphanumeric code.
questions.question: Can you identify the sub entity and the additional sub locations within each personnel area, list all those sub entities and locations?

questions.topicDefinition: A data entry profile enables you to configure and save data entry settings in the Cross-Application Time Sheet, define field selection inputs and perform checks required to process a timesheet. You can set up more than one data entry profile for different user groups. You can also use authorizations to protect each data entry profile from unauthorized access.
questions.question: Do you want to maintain different user groups for every data entry profile?

questions.topicDefinition:
Define the rejection reasons that the person approving the data can attach to a rejected record.

Your company regulations stipulate overtime hours are not recognized unless approved. You enter Unapproved overtime as a reason for rejection.
questions.question: What rejection reasons do you want to maintain??

questions.configRef: Specify Task Types, Components, and Levels
questions.topicDefinition: The task type, task component, and task level fields enable you to specify in the time sheet the elements of the task that are relevant for evaluation. Elements that are relevant for evaluation are entered for the following business processes, for example: Payroll (wage types, attendance types); Controlling and Billing (activity types, statistical key figures); Invoice verification for external employees (activity numbers)
questions.question: Do you want to track task type and task level details as component & fields?

questions.topicDefinition:
Maintain the work locations that is different from your regular work tax area. Define the work location.
Define the End date and Start date for which the work location is applicable.
Define the Country and Region for the new work location.
Define a description for the new work location.
questions.question: Do you want to define work location and description?

questions.topicDefinition: Overtime - A method of classifying the working time outside of contractual working hours.
questions.question: Do you want to enable the field overtime? Used for over time reporting?

questions.topicDefinition: A data entry profile enables you to configure and save data entry settings in the Cross-Application Time Sheet, define field selection inputs and perform checks required to process a timesheet. You can set up more than one data entry profile for different user groups. You can also use authorizations to protect each data entry profile from unauthorized access.
questions.question: Do you want to maintain different user groups for every data entry profile?

Define the rejection reasons that the person approving the data can attach to a rejected record.

Your company regulations stipulate overtime hours are not recognized unless approved. You enter Unapproved overtime as a reason for rejection.
questions.question: What rejection reasons do you want to maintain??

questions.configRef: Specify Task Types, Components, and Levels
questions.topicDefinition: The task type, task component, and task level fields enable you to specify in the time sheet the elements of the task that are relevant for evaluation. Elements that are relevant for evaluation are entered for the following business processes, for example: Payroll (wage types, attendance types); Controlling and Billing (activity types, statistical key figures); Invoice verification for external employees (activity numbers)
questions.question: Do you want to track task type and task level details as component & fields?

questions.topicDefinition:
Maintain the work locations that is different from your regular work tax area. Define the work location.
Define the End date and Start date for which the work location is applicable.
Define the Country and Region for the new work location.
Define a description for the new work location.
questions.question: Do you want to define work location and description?

questions.topicDefinition: Overtime - A method of classifying the working time outside of contractual working hours.
questions.question: Do you want to enable the field overtime? Used for over time reporting?

questions.topicDefinition: You can maintain descriptions for existing storage locations that are relevant for your company. Storage locations are the places where stock is physically kept within a plant. They are also used to define an organizational unit that allows the differentiation of material stocks within a plant.
questions.question: What are the descriptions and location information describing the existing storage locations?

questions.topicDefinition: For existing plants, you can maintain descriptions and assign them to a factory calendar, a county code, and a city code. Plants are used to separate a company by organizational units according to production, procurement, maintenance, and materials planning.
questions.question: What are the descriptions and location information describing each plant defined in the system?

questions.topicDefinition: When performing a goods movement, you can define various reasons that can be logged to indicate the reason behind the goods movement.
questions.question: What reasons, if any, are required for logging with the goods movement?

questions.topicDefinition:
A warehouse complex is represented in the Warehouse Management system as a warehouse number that is used to identify a complex warehouse setup. The physical location is usually decisive for assigning the definition of the warehouse number. A warehouse number groups together storage types and storage bins that are organized and maintained as a complete unit. All warehouse procedures, such as stock placements and stock removals of materials, are always executed within a warehouse number.

A warehouse number has the following characteristics:
• A warehouse number does not have an address, but a short descriptive text
• It is possible to store material data that is specific to a warehouse number
• Within each warehouse number, the stock figures are managed as quantities, not as values
• Within a plant it is possible to assign several storage locations to the same warehouse number
questions.question: Describe the structure of your warehouse.

questions.configRef: Define New Route Determination By Delivery Type
questions.topicDefinition:
Define, by delivery type, whether or not route determination should be repeated when creating a delivery.

If route determination should be repeated, you can have the system check whether the actual route found for the delivery is allowed instead of the original proposed route .
questions.question: Define Routes to be used.

questions.configRef: Define Rules for Picking Location Determination
questions.topicDefinition: This activity defines rules for automatic picking location determination. One picking rule will be defined for each delivery type. The picking rule defines how the system determines the picking location.
questions.question: Will you maintain picking strategies?

questions.topicDefinition: The transportation groups are maintained in material master data to enable route determination in shipping.
questions.question: Describe your transportation handling in detail.

questions.configRef: Assign Warehouse Number to Plant/Storage Location
questions.topic: Assign Warehouse Number to Plant/Storage Location
questions.topicDefinition: To ensure that SAP S/4HANA can recognize which storage locations in Materials Management are controlled by the Warehouse Management system (LE-WM), you must assign the plants and the storage location to the warehouse number. Within a plant, it is possible to assign several storage locations to the same warehouse number.
questions.question: How many storage locations are used in each plant and which are relevant for the Warehouse Management. Name these storage locations and the relevant plants.

questions.topicDefinition: Carry out a consistency check for settings related to integration with a decentralized warehouse management system.
questions.question: Do you have decentralized Warehouse System

questions.topicDefinition: Define the default values that should be used for deliveries for each warehouse number.
questions.question: Are there any default values that need to be maintained for Warehouse?

questions.configRef: Define New Route Determination By Delivery Type
questions.topicDefinition: This activity determines, for each delivery type, whether or not route determination should be repeated by the SAP System when creating a delivery.
questions.question: Do you group together your pick list for multiple processing for a particular shipping point, route, pick date, stock placement, or stock removal?

questions.topicDefinition: Using this activity, you can define routes that you regularly use to ship goods to customers. Then, you can either manually enter a defined route into the business documents. For example, sales orders, or set up a route determination where the system automatically adds a defined route to the documents.
questions.question: The SAP Starter-System provides standard routes with settings such as shipping type (rail/road/sea etc.), transit time, and transportation lead time. You can either use these standard settings or create new ones to capture all routes relevant for your business.

questions.topicDefinition: A picking location refers to a place from where goods ordered by a customer are picked, to be transported to another place. For example, if the goods are picked up from a warehouse to be delivered to the customer, then the warehouse is considered to be the picking location. Using this SSCUI, you can define which delivery item categories are relevant for picking or putting away.
questions.question: Please identify which delivery item categories are relevant for picking or putting away.

questions.topicDefinition: In this activity, you define if at the time of creating delivery documents there is a need for confirmation of picking step by shipping point.
questions.question: Please identify if there is a need for confirmation of picking by shipping point.

questions.configRef: Set POD-Relevance Depending on Delivery Item Category
questions.topicDefinition: Proof of delivery is a method to track the goods receipt by the customer. In this activity, you can set the proof of delivery (POD) relevance depending on the delivery item category. When the system creates billing documents for the item categories that are marked as POD-relevant, it copies the verified quantity rather than the delivery quantity.
questions.question:
Please examine the processes where you require Proof of Delivery before generating the invoice for the customer. Evaluate the delivery types and item categories that are available in the Starter-System.  
Check to what extent you can use the defaults that are contained in the standard system and if you have to make changes to represent your business processes.

questions.topicDefinition: Delivery document types represent the different business transactions in shipping.
questions.question: List all documents required to complete the delivery process (i.e. picking list, packing list, or bill of loading) and what information they contain.

questions.topicDefinition: Delivery priorities are used to give priorities to different customers.
questions.question: How do you allocate merchandise which is in short supply (delivery priorities)?

questions.topicDefinition: A shipping point within SAP is an independent organizational entity which is responsible for planning and processing deliveries to the customer.
questions.question: How do you determine multiple shipping points?

questions.topicDefinition: The shipping point is the top priority in the organization for shipping. Shipping points can be allocated to the desired combinations of shipping condition and loading group for each plant. Before allocation of shipping points, the following needs to be defined: plants, shipping points, shipping conditions, and loading groups.
questions.question: How do you determine shipping points?

questions.topicDefinition: A loading group is defined in the material master record in the sales data for the plant. It represents how materials are loaded for transportation. For example, by crane or on pallets. A loading group is a subdivision of a shipping point. A loading group can be assigned to multiple shipping points and a shipping point can have multiple loading groups.
questions.question: How do you determine multiple shipping points?

questions.topicDefinition: Storage conditions are used to define the conditions under which the materials are stored. The storage condition is copied to the sales delivery item.
questions.question: How do you determine the location at which an item must be picked?

questions.topicDefinition: Stock is allocated to storage locations in SAP. These represent physical or logical locations. When a delivery is created, a picking location (or storage location) is automatically determined for each line item in the delivery based on the shipping point, plant, and shipping condition.
questions.question: Describe the structure of warehouse picking location?

questions.topicDefinition: Modes of transport specify certain aspects of shipping and shipping costs.
questions.question: Describe your transportation handling in detail.

questions.topicDefinition: Shipping conditions are used in the determination of the shipping point and route in a sales document and control how goods are delivered. A shipping condition is maintained in the customer master and vendor master.
questions.question: Does your organization always dispatch products to customers or can they collect them?

questions.topicDefinition: Shipping types are used within route determination to specify whether a route from dispatch to a destination is by air, sea, road, etc.
questions.question: When you dispatch goods to customers, which different modes of transport do you use? For example, road, sea, air, and/or courier - please provide a list.

questions.topicDefinition: The warehouse number identifies a physical warehouse structure within the Warehouse Management system (for example, SAP EWM).
questions.question: Technical integration: Do you have an EWM system for integration setting?

questions.configRef: Define Reasons for Blocking in Shipping
questions.topicDefinition: Delivery blocking reasons are used to separate certain transactions from process flow for special reasons and to avoid further automatic processing. As a result, the transaction is blocked until the person responsible reviews the situation, makes a decision, and possibly removes the delivery block manually.
questions.question: How many delivery block reasons would you like to maintain?

questions.configRef: Assign Blocking Reasons to Delivery Types
questions.topicDefinition: Assign delivery blocking reasons to the delivery types where they should apply.
questions.question: What delivery blocking reasons do you want to assign for delivery types?

questions.configRef: Assign Goods Receiving Points for Inbound Deliveries
questions.topic: Shipping Point and Goods Receiving Point Determination
questions.topicDefinition: Assign and prioritize goods receiving points to the plant/storage location.
questions.question: What Goods receiving points need to be assigned to plant/storage location.

questions.configRef: Define Batch Creation Controls in Inbound Deliveries
questions.topicDefinition: Define the combination of controls allowed for batch creation.
questions.question: Define for each desired delivery item category how batch creation, batch classification or expiration date checks are performed in inbound deliveries.

questions.topicDefinition: Define keys and descriptions for reasons for quantity variance.
questions.question:
Do you want reasons for quantity variance during POD.

Note: Reasons for variance must always be indicated in the POD. Since you may not yet be aware of the reasons at the time the POD is verified, we suggest that you set up a 'Difference under investigation' reason that can be manually changed when you receive the POD.

questions.topicDefinition: Delivery scheduling takes pick/pack times and loading times into account. These times are dependent on the shipping point which is responsible for delivering the order item.
questions.question:
Define for each shipping point whether and how the pick/pack times and/or the loading times should be determined.
Define the scheduling indicators for each shipping point.

questions.configRef: Maintain Country And Transportation Zone For Shipping Point
questions.topicDefinition: Assign country and transportation zones to previously defined shipping points.
questions.question: Enter a country key and transportation zone for each shipping point.

questions.topicDefinition:
Define transportation zones according to country.
Transportation zones represent delivery recipient (ship-to party) regions or delivery shipper (supplier) regions.
questions.question: Define the transportation zones you need for each country and enter the corresponding description.

questions.configRef: Define Shipping Conditions by Sales Document Type
questions.topic: Shipping Point and Goods Receiving Point Determination
questions.topicDefinition: Specify shipping conditions for sales document types.
questions.question:
1. For which sales document types a shipping condition should be specified.
2. Specify a shipping condition for the sales document types

questions.topicDefinition:
Set the most suitable route for inbound deliveries.
You can set the route determination for inbound deliveries for each supplier and receiving plant.

questions.question: Depending on the material number, different stock determination groups are found - this means that with the same movement type, different stock determination strategies (combination of stock determination group + stock determination rule) are used. On the other hand, however, a new stock determination rule is found for the same material number  with another movement type. This means that for the material , various strategies are found depending on the application and its stock determination rule. In the example above, three different stock determination strategies exist each containing different parameters for the automatic stock determination. We recommend that you work on the conceptual details of the required strategies first. Consider how many different material groups are required for stock determination depending on the material master record. Materials that behave in a similar way in stock determination are grouped together. The result corresponds to the number of Stock determination groups* that have to be maintained in the first step. The combination of stock determination group and stock determination rule provides a separate strategy which is saved in the stock determination header table.

questions.configRef: Assign Default Plant for Company Code
questions.topicDefinition: You assign a default plant for a company code to be used when Transportation Management (TM) posts the transportation cost to procurement.
questions.question:
When transportation costs are posted, procurement creates service purchase orders and service entry sheets to pass on the costs to financials. In the configuration step, Assign Default Plant to Company Code, you define a default plant for a company code to be applied to the service purchase order Item.                                                         Example

You have defined the default plant as 1710 for the company code 1710

Example 1: outbound deliveries from the same plant.

Freight order 8472817 consolidates the following delivery items:

Purchasing company code: 1710

Delivery 1029283 10 Finished product 1 1711- Plant 1 20 qty 1000 Kgs

Delivery 1049392 10 Finished product 3 1711 - Plant 1 40 qty 500 Kgs

Delivery 1045412 10 Finished product 9 1711 - Plant 1 15 qty 800 Kgs

In this case during the freight cost posting for this freight order, as all deliveries originate from plant 1711, the system determines this plant for the service purchase order item.

Example 2: Outbound deliveries from different plants

As a prerequisite for this example, you have specified the default plant for company code 1710 as “1710 - Plant 1”.

Freight order 8562545 consolidates the following delivery items:

Purchasing company code:  1710

Delivery 1029283 10 Finished product 1 1712- Plant 1 9 qty 700 Kgs

Delivery 1049392 10 Finished product 3 1711 - Plant 1 15 qty 800 Kgs

Delivery 1045412 10 Finished product 9 1712 - Plant 1 1 qty 100 Kgs

In this case during the freight cost posting for this freight order, as the plants are different at the delivery item level, the system checks the default plant that has been defined for the purchasing company code 1710, which is this case you have previously defined as “1710 - Plant 1”.

The plant 1710 is determined on the service purchase order item based on the default plant defined for the purchasing company code 1710.

questions.configRef: Maintain SSCC Generation for each Plant/Storage Location

questions.topicDefinition:
You can define an SSCC using a basis number of an International Location Number (ILN) and a number from the number range assigned. The basis number of ILN must be 8 characters long.

Note that if your SSCC does not begin with the basis number of ILN, the system assigns the first number of the internal number interval as first number of the SSCC. Therefore, make sure that the first number of the internal number range is not zero.
questions.question:
If your entire organization does not create more than 1,000 billion handling units per year, you only need one ILN from which to copy the 8-digit basis number of an ILN into an entry (by leaving all key fields blank: plant and storage location, for example).

If you would also like to send smaller packages and manage them with SSCCs as well, you would need more than 1,000 billion SSCCs per year. In this case, you can add another base number to the same organizational unit and number the base numbers in ascending order. Or you can enter separate base units for specific plants and storage locations. Kindly specify which option you wish to proceed with

questions.question:
There are two types of number assignment:

Internal number assignment
The SAP System automatically assigns a sequential number from the specified number range.
External number assignment
When creating a handling unit, you use a number from the external number range.
It is possible to maintain multiple internal and external number range intervals in order to assign numbers from different internals to various combinations of packaging material types, plants, and storage locations. Please validate which option suites you well.

questions.topic: Provides an overview of packaging material types.
questions.topicDefinition: The packaging material type combines packaging materials into groups and contains essential control features which apply to the corresponding shipping materials.
questions.question:
The packaging material type controls the following points:

Plant determination
Within delivery processing, delivery items can be generated from the handling units. This allows you to manage stocks for packaging materials (for example, your own or possibly special stocks) and to bill packaging materials.
Generate delivery items
Separate delivery items are generated for packaging materials of this packaging material type.
Number assignment
By entering a packaging material, you define, when generating a handling unit according to the method set for number assignment, how the identification of the handling unit is created. The system supports the numbering based on internal number ranges or SSCC settings.
Tare variable
The tare weight for packaging materials for this packaging material type has a changeable tare volume. Please check with your logistics team regarding valid packaging materials to use.

For the service order items SVS1, SVS2, SVS4, SEW1, SEW2, and SEW4 condition type PMP0 is used to define a valuation price for service parts that don’t have the source of supply maintained in the system. When you add a service part item to a service order, you must enter a price so that the system can automatically create a purchase requisition.

For the service confirmation items SCS1, SCS3, SCW1, and SCW3 condition type PMP0 defines that the price of a service part you order is initially obtained from the purchase order. Once a supplier invoice is available, the system uses the price contained in the invoice if the service confirmation hasn't been released for billing.

If you want to change this standard configuration, you must assign a custom condition type using this configuration step.
